title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄序
正德丙子天下鄉舉之期也
山東右布政使鄭〔陽〕以故事
白于巡按御史張〔羽〕請監臨
焉于時鎮巡則有太監黎〔鑑〕
右副都御史黃〔瓚〕先後以事
至者則有工部右侍郎趙〔璜〕
===
監察御史周〔朝佐〕徐〔冠〕馬〔録〕
萬〔鏓〕郎中倪〔璋〕員外郎詹〔昇〕
主事東〔魯〕葉〔寬〕羽曰是皆
明于故實可質之以贊不逮
者也詢謀僉同乃具書幣聘
〔承〕〔恩〕等九人為考試官提調
于內者則左參政許〔淳〕右參
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄序

正德丙子，天下鄉舉之期也。山東右布政使鄭〔陽〕以故事，白于巡按御史張〔羽〕，請監臨焉。于時鎮巡則有太監黎〔鑑〕、右副都御史黃〔瓚〕；先後以事至者，則有工部右侍郎趙〔璜〕、監察御史周〔朝佐〕、徐〔冠〕、馬〔録〕、萬〔鏓〕、郎中倪〔璋〕、員外郎詹〔昇〕、主事東〔魯〕、葉〔寬〕。羽曰：「是皆明于故實，可質之以贊不逮者也。」詢謀僉同，乃具書幣，聘〔承〕〔恩〕等九人為考試官。提調于內者，則左參政許〔淳〕、右參
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

The bingzi year of the Zhengde reign (1516) was the appointed year for provincial examinations throughout the empire. Following established precedent, Zheng Yang, Shandong’s Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, reported to Regional Inspector Zhang Yu and requested that he serve as Supervising Official. At that time, the regional command and grand coordinatorship were held respectively by the eunuch Director Li Jian and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Huang Zan. Those who arrived successively on official business included Zhao Huang, Right Vice Minister of Works; Investigating Censors Zhou Chaozuo, Xu Guan, Ma Lu, and Wan Cong; Bureau Director Ni Zhang; Vice Director Zhan Sheng; and Secretaries Dong Lu and Ye Kuan. Zhang Yu said: “These men are all well versed in precedents and established practices. They can be consulted to help make good my shortcomings.” Their deliberations were unanimous, and letters of invitation and gifts were accordingly prepared to engage Cheng’en [?] and eight others as Examiners. Those serving as Proctors within the examination compound were Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Xu Chun and the Right Vice…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
政徐〔蕃〕監試則按察使王〔良〕
〔臣〕副使盛〔儀〕又恐外或不理
以撓乎內也則分撥右布政
使盛〔應期〕副使原〔軒〕林〔琦〕王
〔鉉〕吳〔漳〕陳〔和〕胡〔文璧〕潘〔珍〕左
叅議閔〔楷〕右叅議李〔恢〕僉事
呂〔和〕蔡〔芝〕許〔逵〕張〔嘉謨〕胥〔隋〕
===
範焉以八月七日事內者咸
集入院惟規惟法既備以嚴
御史焚香籲天陳矢言几上
進曰惟
國家求材資用事莫大於茲凡
我有事尚同心殫力克襄厥
載如或售私奸政取舍罔中
punctuated:
政徐〔蕃〕，監試則按察使王〔良〕〔臣〕、副使盛〔儀〕。又恐外或不理，以撓乎內也，則分撥右布政使盛〔應期〕、副使原〔軒〕、林〔琦〕、王〔鉉〕、吳〔漳〕、陳〔和〕、胡〔文璧〕、潘〔珍〕、左叅議閔〔楷〕、右叅議李〔恢〕、僉事呂〔和〕、蔡〔芝〕、許〔逵〕、張〔嘉謨〕、胥〔隋〕，範焉。
以八月七日，事內者咸集入院，惟規惟法，既備以嚴。御史焚香籲天，陳矢言几上，進曰：「惟國家求材資用，事莫大於茲。凡我有事，尚同心殫力，克襄厥載。如或售私奸政，取舍罔中
translation_en:
…Administration Vice Commissioner Xu Fan. Overseeing the examination were Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Wang Liangchen and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Sheng Yi. Fearing also that disorder outside might disrupt proceedings within, they assigned Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Sheng Yingqi; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Yuan Xuan, Lin Qi, Wang Xuan, Wu Zhang, Chen He, Hu Wenbi, and Pan Zhen; Left Administration Assistant Commissioner Min Kai; Right Administration Assistant Commissioner Li Hui; and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Lü He, Cai Zhi, Xu Kui, Zhang Jiamo, and Xu Sui to maintain order [?].
On the seventh day of the eighth month, all those serving within assembled and entered the examination compound. Rules and procedures were fully established and rigorously enforced. The censor burned incense and invoked Heaven, laid a written oath upon a table, and stepped forward, saying: “For the state, no undertaking is greater than seeking talented men for its service. May all of us engaged in this work unite our resolve and expend our utmost strength to accomplish our charge. Should anyone advance private interests and corrupt the administration, or fail to act impartially in accepting and rejecting candidates…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
用僨於茲事有如矢言〔承恩〕
率諸考試者進曰因文取才
其眞其允如弗旣厥心自作
慝者亦如之提調監試者乃
率諸執事進曰如有怠若職
亂若事者亦如之旣各宅厥
居宣力靡懈其惟愼矣御史
===
又曰遼東士選于御史張〔文〕
明其六府則副使趙〔鶴〕選也
葢千七百有奇盍愼擇之悶
俾遺美焉衆乃精白審度悉
閱於文旣得儁七十五人文
之粹者篇二十爲録〔承恩〕曰
昔人謂文章關世道隆汙科
punctuated:
用僨於茲事，有如矢言。」〔承恩〕率諸考試者進曰：「因文取才，其眞其允。如弗旣厥心，自作慝者，亦如之。」提調監試者乃率諸執事進曰：「如有怠若職、亂若事者，亦如之。」旣各宅厥居，宣力靡懈，其惟愼矣。
御史又曰：「遼東士選于御史張〔文〕明，其六府則副使趙〔鶴〕選也。葢千七百有奇，盍愼擇之，悶俾遺美焉？」衆乃精白審度，悉閱於文。旣得儁七十五人，文之粹者篇二十爲録。〔承恩〕曰：「昔人謂文章關世道隆汙，科
translation_en:
…thereby bringing this undertaking to ruin, let the consequences be as declared in this oath.” Cheng’en then led the Examiners forward and said: “In selecting talent through written compositions, we shall be genuine and impartial. If any fail to devote themselves fully to the task and perpetrate wrongdoing, let the same apply to them.” The Proctors and Examination Monitors then led the various functionaries forward and said: “If any neglect their duties or disrupt their work, let the same apply to them.” Each then took up his assigned quarters and exerted himself without flagging. They were indeed conscientious.
The Censor further said: “The candidates from Liaodong were selected by Censor Zhang Wenming; those from the six prefectures were selected by Vice Commissioner Zhao He. There are more than seventeen hundred in all. Should we not select carefully from among them, lest worthy talent be overlooked [?]?” All accordingly purified their intentions and weighed their judgments carefully, reading every composition. Having selected seventy-five outstanding men, they compiled twenty of the finest compositions into this record. Cheng’en said: “People of old held that literary composition bears upon the flourishing or decline of the moral order. The civil-service examinations …

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
舉者尤重也何則上以文取
也士以文進也士賢不肖治
忽從焉豈不重與然自賔興
之法廢而辭科興雖或得人
氣習靡矣我
皇祖始損益之立學申教獨重經
術下選舉之
===
詔期得明經之士以收實用燕
翼之謀不可尚已
列聖相承恪守成憲故至今日士
崇經學賢才彙進作人之效
非前代所及矧山之東實邇
文教鄒魯之化猶存士之興起
固宜滋盛茲惟文爲觀之然
punctuated: 舉者尤重也。何則？上以文取也，士以文進也。士賢不肖，治忽從焉，豈不重與？然自賔興之法廢而辭科興，雖或得人，氣習靡矣。我皇祖始損益之，立學申教，獨重經術，下選舉之詔，期得明經之士，以收實用。燕翼之謀，不可尚已。列聖相承，恪守成憲，故至今日，士崇經學，賢才彙進。作人之效，非前代所及。矧山之東，實邇文教，鄒魯之化猶存，士之興起，固宜滋盛。茲惟文爲觀之，然
translation_en: …civil-service examinations are especially consequential. Why? Those above select men through their writing, and scholars advance through their writing. Whether these scholars are worthy or unworthy determines whether government is orderly or negligent: how could this not be consequential? Yet since the ancient practice of honoring and recommending worthy men fell into disuse and examinations in literary composition arose, although capable men were sometimes found, prevailing dispositions and habits grew decadent. Our imperial ancestor first reformed this system, establishing schools and strengthening instruction, with particular emphasis on learning in the Classics. He issued an edict on selection and recommendation, seeking scholars who understood the Classics so that they might render practical service. His plans to secure the welfare of his descendants could not be surpassed. Successive sage emperors have scrupulously upheld these established rules. Thus, to this day, scholars esteem classical learning, and worthy and talented men advance together. The results in nurturing men surpass anything achieved by earlier dynasties. Moreover, Shandong lies close to the wellspring of cultural instruction; the transforming influence of Zou and Lu still endures there. It is surely fitting that scholars should rise in ever greater numbers. Now, examining them solely through their writings, only then …

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
後知其士之信多賢也何則
文德之宣也文之盛矣匪實
而何智斯有言苟理之弗達
言之其能文乎行雖艱也匪
知何行智以及之行達幾何
行且有用必皆可觀已然後
知山之東士之信多賢也
===
聖代作人之效不其滋盛矣乎嗚
呼用者行其學也行非其學
者恥也書曰靜言庸違蓋悖
學也故選以觀學用以觀行
達不變塞用令厥終用無忝
厥薦斯善士也苟利達之移
恥孰甚焉詩曰靡不有初鮮
punctuated:
後知其士之信多賢也。何則？文，德之宣也。文之盛矣，匪實而何？智斯有言：苟理之弗達，言之其能文乎？行雖艱也，匪知何行？智以及之，行達幾何？行且有用，必皆可觀已。然後知山之東士之信多賢也。
聖代作人之效，不其滋盛矣乎？嗚呼！用者行其學也，行非其學者恥也。《書》曰：「靜言庸違。」蓋悖學也。故選以觀學，用以觀行。達不變塞，用令厥終，用無忝厥薦，斯善士也。苟利達之移，恥孰甚焉？《詩》曰：「靡不有初，鮮
translation_en:
…only then does one know that their scholars truly include many worthy men. Why is this? Writing gives expression to virtue. When writing flourishes, what can this be but evidence of genuine substance? Concerning knowledge, there is this saying [?]: if one has not comprehended principle, can one express it in accomplished writing? Though putting it into practice is difficult, without knowledge what can one practice? Knowledge may reach it, but how far does conduct attain? When that conduct is put to use, it must all be worthy of regard. Only then does one know that the scholars of Shandong truly include many worthy men.
Have not the results of nurturing men under our sagely dynasty become abundantly evident? Alas! To be employed in office is to put one’s learning into practice; to act contrary to one’s learning is shameful. The Book of Documents says: “His words are fair, but his actions go against them.” This is surely a betrayal of learning. Thus, in selecting men we examine their learning; in employing them we examine their conduct. A man who, upon attaining success, remains as he was in adversity, thereby bringing his course to a worthy conclusion and bringing no disgrace upon his recommendation—such a man is a worthy scholar. If profit and advancement cause him to change, what shame could be greater? The Book of Odes says: “All have a beginning; few…”

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
克有終此之謂與〔承恩〕始而
於士喜其學也終而於士慮
其行也多士尚亦勗哉斯舉
也〔承恩〕與教諭何〔潔〕爲主考
教授陳〔鑾〕汪〔文明〕學正越〔臻〕
教諭楊〔澤〕高〔通〕訓導張〔珊〕余
〔蘊〕同焉
===
浙江嚴州府儒學教授蔣〔承〕
〔恩〕謹序
punctuated:
克有終」，此之謂與？〔承恩〕始而於士喜其學也，終而於士慮其行也。多士尚亦勗哉！斯舉也，〔承恩〕與教諭何〔潔〕爲主考，教授陳〔鑾〕、汪〔文明〕，學正越〔臻〕，教諭楊〔澤〕、高〔通〕，訓導張〔珊〕、余〔蘊〕同焉。

浙江嚴州府儒學教授蔣〔承〕〔恩〕謹序。
translation_en:
…can carry it through to the end.” Is this not what those words mean? I, Cheng’en, began by rejoicing in the candidates’ learning; in the end, I am concerned about their conduct. May all you scholars strive diligently! For this examination, I, Cheng’en, and Instructor He Jie served as chief Examiners. Professors Chen Luan and Wang Wenming, School Director Yue Zhen, Instructors Yang Ze and Gao Tong, and Assistant Instructors Zhang Shan and Yu Yun served with us.

Preface respectfully composed by Jiang Cheng’en, Professor of the Confucian School of Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.

Shandong Provincial Examination, eleventh year of the Zhengde reign (1516).

Proctors:

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
四書
見善如不及見不善如探湯
正己而不求於人則無怨
君子之於物也愛之而弗仁於民也仁之
而弗親親親而仁民仁民而愛物
易
乾元用九天下治也
六五鼎黄耳金鉉利貞
===
極數知來之謂占通變之謂事
夫乾天下之至健也德行恒易以知險夫
坤天下之至順也德行恒簡以知阻
書
帝曰疇若予工僉曰垂哉帝曰俞咨垂汝
共工垂拜稽首讓于殳斨暨伯與帝
曰俞往哉汝諧帝曰疇若予上下草
木鳥獸僉曰益哉帝曰俞咨益汝作
朕虞益拜稽首讓于朱虎熊羆帝
punctuated:
四書
見善如不及，見不善如探湯。
正己而不求於人，則無怨。
君子之於物也，愛之而弗仁；於民也，仁之而弗親。親親而仁民，仁民而愛物。

易
乾元用九，天下治也。
六五：鼎黄耳金鉉，利貞。
極數知來之謂占，通變之謂事。
夫乾，天下之至健也，德行恒易以知險；夫坤，天下之至順也，德行恒簡以知阻。

書
帝曰：「疇若予工？」僉曰：「垂哉！」帝曰：「俞！咨，垂，汝共工。」垂拜稽首，讓于殳、斨暨伯與。帝曰：「俞！往哉，汝諧。」帝曰：「疇若予上下草木鳥獸？」僉曰：「益哉！」帝曰：「俞！咨，益，汝作朕虞。」益拜稽首，讓于朱、虎、熊、羆。帝
translation_en:
Four Books

On seeing goodness, pursue it as though unable to catch up; on seeing what is not good, recoil as though plunging a hand into scalding water.

If one sets oneself right and makes no demands on others, there will be no resentment.

In relation to things, the gentleman cherishes them but does not treat them with benevolence; in relation to the people, he treats them with benevolence but not with the affection due to kin. He is affectionate toward his kin and extends benevolence to the people; he is benevolent toward the people and extends care to things.

Book of Changes (Yijing)

When the primal power of Qian employs the nines, all under Heaven is well governed.

Six in the fifth place: the cauldron has yellow ears and a metal carrying bar. It is favorable to remain steadfast.

To fathom the numbers and know what is to come is called divination; to comprehend changes and put them into effect is called undertaking affairs.

Qian is the utmost strength under Heaven. Its virtuous conduct is always easy, and thereby it knows danger. Kun is the utmost compliance under Heaven. Its virtuous conduct is always simple, and thereby it knows obstruction.

Book of Documents (Shujing)

The emperor said, “Who can manage my works?” All replied, “Chui!” The emperor said, “Yes! Ah, Chui, you shall be Minister of Works.” Chui bowed and touched his forehead to the ground, yielding the appointment to Shu, Qiang, and Boyu. The emperor said, “Yes! Go and undertake it; you will bring harmony to the work.” The emperor said, “Who can manage for me the grasses, trees, birds, and beasts of the highlands and lowlands?” All replied, “Yi!” The emperor said, “Yes! Ah, Yi, you shall be my Forester.” Yi bowed and touched his forehead to the ground, yielding the appointment to Zhu, Hu, Xiong, and Pi. The emperor…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
俞往哉汝諧
德懋懋官功懋懋賞用人惟己改過不吝
時人斯其惟皇之極
迪知忱恂于九德之行乃敢告教厥后曰
拜手稽首后矣曰宅乃事宅乃牧宅
乃準茲惟后矣
詩
淑人君子其帶伊絲其帶伊絲其弁伊騏
如跂斯翼如矢斯棘如鳥斯革如翬斯飛
===
奕奕梁山維禹甸之有倬其道韓侯受命
王親命之纘戎祖考無廢朕命夙夜
匪解虔共爾位朕命不易榦不庭方
以佐戎辟四牡奕奕孔脩且張韓侯
入覲以其介圭入覲于王王錫韓侯
淑旂綏章簟茀錯衡玄衮赤舃鉤膺
鏤鍚鞹鞃淺幭鞗革金厄
明昭有周式序在位
punctuated:
俞，往哉！汝諧。

德懋，懋官；功懋，懋賞。用人惟己，改過不吝。

時人斯其惟皇之極。

迪知忱恂于九德之行，乃敢告教厥后，曰：「拜手稽首，后矣！」曰：「宅乃事，宅乃牧，宅乃準，茲惟后矣。」

詩

淑人君子，其帶伊絲。其帶伊絲，其弁伊騏。

如跂斯翼，如矢斯棘，如鳥斯革，如翬斯飛。

奕奕梁山，維禹甸之。有倬其道，韓侯受命。王親命之：「纘戎祖考，無廢朕命。夙夜匪解，虔共爾位。朕命不易，榦不庭方，以佐戎辟。」四牡奕奕，孔脩且張。韓侯入覲，以其介圭，入覲于王。王錫韓侯，淑旂綏章，簟茀錯衡，玄衮赤舃，鉤膺鏤鍚，鞹鞃淺幭，鞗革金厄。

明昭有周，式序在位。
translation_en:
…“Yes, go! You will bring harmony.”

For outstanding virtue, confer high office; for outstanding achievement, confer generous rewards. Employ others as though their abilities were your own, and correct your faults without hesitation.

These people will thus conform to the sovereign’s supreme standard.

Only those who understand and sincerely and faithfully practice the nine virtues dare to admonish and instruct their ruler, saying: “We bow with hands joined and foreheads to the ground, O ruler!” They say: “Settle those responsible for your affairs in their offices; settle your governors in theirs; settle those who uphold your standards in theirs. This is what it means to be a ruler.”

Book of Odes

The good man, the noble gentleman—his sash is of silk. His sash is of silk; his cap is adorned with dark green gems.

Like a man rising on tiptoe, poised with dignity; like an arrow, straight and true; like a bird spreading its wings; like a pheasant taking flight.

Lofty is Mount Liang, which Yu brought under cultivation. Splendid is its road. The Lord of Han received his charge. The king personally charged him: “Continue the work of your forefathers; do not neglect my commands. Morning and night, be unflagging, and reverently discharge the duties of your position. Do not alter my commands. Bring into order the regions that do not attend court, thereby assisting your sovereign.” His four stallions were magnificent, very tall and strong. The Lord of Han entered for an audience, bearing his great jade tablet, and appeared before the king. The king bestowed upon the Lord of Han a fine banner with its hanging ornaments, a bamboo carriage screen and an ornamented crossbar, a dark dragon robe and red ceremonial shoes, breast straps with metal fittings and engraved forehead ornaments for his horses, a leather-covered carriage handgrip and a tiger-skin covering, and leather reins with gold fittings.

Bright and illustrious is Zhou; in due order its officers occupy their places.

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
及宋人盟于宿〔隱公元年公及宋公遇于〕
清　宋公陳侯蔡人衛人伐鄭　翬
帥師會宋公陳侯蔡人衛人伐鄭〔俱隱公四年〕
郲人鄭人伐宋　宋人
伐鄭圍長葛〔俱隱公五年〕鄭人來輸
平〔隱公六年〕鄭伯使宛來歸祊　庚
寅我入祊〔俱隱公八年〕翬帥師會齊
人鄭人伐宋　辛未取郜辛巳取防
〔俱隱公十年〕
===
冬公次于滑〔莊公三年〕
滕子來朝〔桓公二年〕杞子來朝〔僖公二十有〕
〔七年〕
公會晉侯齊侯宋公衛侯鄭伯曹伯莒子
邾子于商任〔襄公二十有一年〕公會晉
侯齊侯宋公衛侯鄭伯曹伯莒子邾
子薛伯杞伯小邾子于沙隨〔襄公二〕
〔十有二年〕衛侯之弟鱄出奔晉〔襄公〕
〔二十有七年〕楚公子比自晉歸于楚
punctuated:
及宋人盟于宿〔隱公元年。公及宋公遇于〕清。宋公、陳侯、蔡人、衛人伐鄭。翬帥師會宋公、陳侯、蔡人、衛人伐鄭〔俱隱公四年〕。郲人、鄭人伐宋。宋人伐鄭，圍長葛〔俱隱公五年〕。鄭人來輸平〔隱公六年〕。鄭伯使宛來歸祊。庚寅，我入祊〔俱隱公八年〕。翬帥師會齊人、鄭人伐宋。辛未，取郜；辛巳，取防〔俱隱公十年〕。

冬，公次于滑〔莊公三年〕。

滕子來朝〔桓公二年〕。杞子來朝〔僖公二十有〕〔七年〕。

公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子于商任〔襄公二十有一年〕。公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子于沙隨〔襄公二〕〔十有二年〕。衛侯之弟鱄出奔晉〔襄公〕〔二十有七年〕。楚公子比自晉歸于楚。
translation_en:
… joined the men of Song in making a covenant at Su. 〔First year of Duke Yin.〕 The duke met the Duke of Song at Qing. The Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, and men of Cai and Wei attacked Zheng. Hui led an army to join the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, and men of Cai and Wei in attacking Zheng. 〔Both entries: fourth year of Duke Yin.〕 Men of Lai [?] and Zheng attacked Song. Men of Song attacked Zheng and besieged Changge. 〔Both entries: fifth year of Duke Yin.〕 Men of Zheng came to offer peace. 〔Sixth year of Duke Yin.〕 The Earl of Zheng sent Wan to transfer Beng to us. On the gengyin day, we entered Beng. 〔Both entries: eighth year of Duke Yin.〕 Hui led an army to join men of Qi and Zheng in attacking Song. On the xinwei day, we took Gao; on the xinsi day, we took Fang. 〔Both entries: tenth year of Duke Yin.〕

In winter, the duke encamped at Hua. 〔Third year of Duke Zhuang.〕

The Viscount of Teng came to pay court. 〔Second year of Duke Huan.〕 The Viscount of Qi came to pay court. 〔Twenty-seventh year of Duke Xi.〕

The duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, and the Viscount of Zhu at Shangren. 〔Twenty-first year of Duke Xiang.〕 The duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Xiao Zhu at Shasui. 〔Twenty-second year of Duke Xiang.〕 Zhuan, younger brother of the Marquis of Wei, fled to Jin. 〔Twenty-seventh year of Duke Xiang.〕 Prince Bi of Chu returned from Jin to Chu.

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
昭公十有三年
禮記
貧者不以貨財為禮老者不以筋力為禮
樂正崇四術立四教順先王詩書禮樂以
造士春秋教以禮樂冬夏教以詩書
民有德而五穀昌
是故聖人之制行也不制以己使民有所
勸勉愧恥以行其言
第貳場
===
論
千聖相傳心法之要
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令禮官勸學興禮詔〔元朔六年〕
擬唐以宋璟為黃門侍郎誥〔神龍元年〕
擬宋以唐介知諫院謝表〔嘉祐元年〕
判語〔五條〕
選用軍職
磨勘卷宗
punctuated:
昭公十有三年。

禮記
貧者不以貨財為禮，老者不以筋力為禮。
樂正崇四術，立四教，順先王詩書禮樂以造士。春秋教以禮樂，冬夏教以詩書。
民有德而五穀昌。
是故聖人之制行也，不制以己，使民有所勸勉愧恥，以行其言。

第貳場

論
千聖相傳心法之要。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令禮官勸學興禮詔〔元朔六年〕。
擬唐以宋璟為黃門侍郎誥〔神龍元年〕。
擬宋以唐介知諫院謝表〔嘉祐元年〕。

判語〔五條〕
選用軍職。
磨勘卷宗。
translation_en:
…the thirteenth year of Duke Zhao.

Record of Rites (Liji)
“The poor are not required to offer wealth and goods in performing rites; the old are not required to exert physical strength in performing rites.”
“The Director of Music honors the four disciplines and establishes the four branches of instruction, following the former kings’ Poetry, Documents, Rites, and Music to educate scholars. In spring and autumn, he teaches Rites and Music; in winter and summer, Poetry and Documents.”
“The people possess virtue, and the five grains flourish.”
“Thus, when the sage establishes standards of conduct, he does not take himself as the measure. He gives the people grounds for encouragement, effort, shame, and remorse, so that they may put his words into practice.”

Second Session

Discourse
The essentials of the teaching of the mind transmitted from sage to sage through the ages.

Edicts, Pronouncements, and Memorials 〔One question from among these [?]〕
Compose an edict in the voice of a Han emperor commanding the ritual officials to encourage learning and promote ritual observance. 〔Sixth year of Yuanshuo〕
Compose a Tang imperial pronouncement appointing Song Jing as Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Gate. 〔First year of Shenlong〕
Compose a Song memorial of thanks from Tang Jie upon his appointment to administer the Bureau of Policy Criticism. 〔First year of Jiayou〕

Legal Judgments 〔Five items〕
Selection and appointment of military officers.
Detailed examination of case files.

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
辯解官物
辯明冤枉
帶造貶疋
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問我
宣宗章皇帝御製五倫書所以惇叙彝倫見
國家以綱常為治萬世人道之大經所由正
也其書總其論于前列其倫于後為卷
===
六十有二然獨詳於君道臣道者盖以
君臣所以主持乎父子夫婦朋友之道
於五倫為尤重也君之善行為目四十
有八臣之善行為目四十有三然君臣
一體其道未始不合今即書中事目觀
之無非相資相成之道若聖德必資輔
德聖學必求正學法祖與守法同心制
治與經國同謀求賢豈不待夫薦舉去
姦寧不用夫彈劾褒嘉者必忠義聽納
punctuated:
辯解官物
辯明冤枉
帶造貶疋

第叁場
策〔五道〕

問：我宣宗章皇帝御製《五倫書》，所以惇叙彝倫，見國家以綱常為治，萬世人道之大經所由正也。其書總其論于前，列其倫于後，為卷六十有二。然獨詳於君道、臣道者，盖以君臣所以主持乎父子、夫婦、朋友之道，於五倫為尤重也。君之善行為目四十有八，臣之善行為目四十有三。然君臣一體，其道未始不合。今即書中事目觀之，無非相資相成之道。若聖德必資輔德，聖學必求正學，法祖與守法同心，制治與經國同謀。求賢豈不待夫薦舉？去姦寧不用夫彈劾？褒嘉者必忠義，聽納
translation_en:
Accounting for government property [?].
Clearing up wrongful accusations.
Arranging the manufacture of inferior bolts of cloth [?].

Third Session
Policy Questions〔Five questions〕

Question: The imperially composed Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun shu) of our Emperor Xuanzong Zhang serves to foster and order the enduring human relationships. It shows that the state governs through the cardinal bonds and constant virtues, thereby setting right the great guiding principles of human conduct for all ages. The book presents its general discussion first and sets out the relationships afterward, comprising sixty-two juan. Yet it treats the way of the ruler and the way of the minister in particular detail because ruler and minister uphold the ways governing fathers and sons, husbands and wives, and friends; their relationship thus carries particular weight among the five relationships.

The ruler’s good conduct is arranged under forty-eight headings, and the minister’s good conduct under forty-three. Yet ruler and minister form one body, and their ways have never been separate. Looking now at the subjects treated in the book, all concern ways of mutually supporting and completing one another. Thus, sagely virtue necessarily relies upon assistance in cultivating virtue, and sagely learning necessarily seeks correct learning. Taking the ancestors as models and observing established laws share one purpose; establishing good government and administering the state share one plan. Does seeking worthy men not depend upon recommendations? Can removing the wicked dispense with impeachment? Those commended must be loyal and righteous; those whose words are heard and accepted …

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
者必諫諍仁民之有待於恤民撫字御
夷之有取於將略備邊若此之類可條
舉一二事以言之乎自餘諸目亦罔不
然不俟盡舉也至於父子夫婦兄弟朋
友之道書或分而言之亦或合而言之
又或各有所附著其亦有說乎諸士子
服膺
聖訓于茲有年矣其敬陳之毋忽
問人君之學與不學天下之治忽關焉然
===
經以載道史以載事二者誠為學之資
不可偏廢也先儒之論有曰人主讀經
則師其意讀史則師其迹豈帝王之學
與韋布不同止得其意與迹而已邪又
曰讀經以尚書為先讀史以唐書為首
今二編之書固在也其要歸何在而以
為先邪抑君人者六經諸史固在所不
必學邪昔漢從之臣日侍經筵者摭取
說命三篇為訓詞苑之臣有事纂脩者
punctuated:
者必諫諍，仁民之有待於恤民撫字，御夷之有取於將略備邊，若此之類，可條舉一二事以言之乎？自餘諸目，亦罔不然，不俟盡舉也。至於父子、夫婦、兄弟、朋友之道，書或分而言之，亦或合而言之，又或各有所附著，其亦有說乎？諸士子服膺聖訓，于茲有年矣，其敬陳之，毋忽。
問：人君之學與不學，天下之治忽關焉。然經以載道，史以載事，二者誠為學之資，不可偏廢也。先儒之論有曰：「人主讀經則師其意，讀史則師其迹。」豈帝王之學與韋布不同，止得其意與迹而已邪？又曰：「讀經以尚書為先，讀史以唐書為首。」今二編之書固在也，其要歸何在，而以為先邪？抑君人者，六經諸史固在所不必學邪？昔漢從之臣日侍經筵者，摭取說命三篇為訓；詞苑之臣有事纂脩者，
translation_en:
…those whose words are heard and accepted must offer forthright remonstrance. Benevolence toward the people depends upon relieving their distress and nurturing them; managing relations with the non-Chinese peoples draws upon military strategy and frontier defense. Could you enumerate one or two instances of such matters and discuss them? All the remaining headings follow the same pattern, and need not be exhaustively listed. As for the proper relations between fathers and sons, husbands and wives, elder and younger brothers, and friends, the book sometimes treats them separately, sometimes together, and sometimes attaches them to other topics. Is there an explanation for this as well? You examination candidates have respectfully taken the imperial instructions to heart for years now. Set forth your views reverently, without negligence.
Question: Whether a ruler studies or fails to study bears upon order or disorder throughout the realm. The classics convey the Way, while histories record events. Both are indeed resources for learning, and neither may be neglected. An earlier Confucian scholar said: “When a ruler reads the classics, he takes their meaning as his teacher; when he reads histories, he takes the recorded deeds as his teacher.” Can the learning of emperors and kings differ from that of common scholars, consisting merely in grasping these meanings and deeds? It has also been said: “In reading the classics, give priority to the Book of Documents; in reading histories, begin with the History of the Tang.” These two works are certainly still available. What is their essential purport, such that they should be given priority? Or are the Six Classics and the various histories really things that a ruler need not study? Formerly, an attendant official [?] who attended the Classics Colloquium daily selected the three chapters of “The Charge to Yue” (Yue ming) to provide instruction; an official of the Hanlin Academy engaged in compilation…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
採取唐鑑一部以進二臣之見豈亦有
類於此歟有參酌周禮彙成通典進勸
其君於豐大之日者又有家學春秋作
為傳義啓迪其君於恢復之時者夫周
禮春秋其於尚書唐鑑果有同歟而臣
工所以進講者其意亦有在歟願究言
之以觀稽古事君之學
問天下不可一日無儒者之論古人或平
居先慮獨出己見可為萬世之法程或
===
臨事發謀審察時變可正一時之權度
然事同而論異不能無是非利害之殊
也試舉其關乎治者言之論封建者曰
非聖人意不可行也或又曰天道至公
百世以俟而不惑論井田者曰亂世之
後乃可行也或又曰處之有術不刑一
人而可復易肉刑以笞法論者美其君
好生之仁矣而又或以為啓斯民之易
犯者馬代府兵以宿衛論者謂其憫百
punctuated:
採取《唐鑑》一部以進，二臣之見豈亦有類於此歟？有參酌《周禮》，彙成《通典》，進勸其君於豐大之日者；又有家學《春秋》，作為傳義，啓迪其君於恢復之時者。夫《周禮》《春秋》，其於《尚書》《唐鑑》果有同歟？而臣工所以進講者，其意亦有在歟？願究言之，以觀稽古事君之學。
問：天下不可一日無儒者之論。古人或平居先慮，獨出己見，可為萬世之法程；或臨事發謀，審察時變，可正一時之權度。然事同而論異，不能無是非利害之殊也。試舉其關乎治者言之。論封建者曰：「非聖人意，不可行也。」或又曰：「天道至公，百世以俟而不惑。」論井田者曰：「亂世之後乃可行也。」或又曰：「處之有術，不刑一人而可復。」易肉刑以笞法，論者美其君好生之仁矣，而又或以為啓斯民之易犯者馬？代府兵以宿衛，論者謂其憫百
translation_en:
…selected a volume of the Mirror of the Tang (Tang jian) and presented it to the throne. Were the views of these two ministers perhaps similar to this? There was one who consulted the Rites of Zhou (Zhou li), compiled the Comprehensive Institutions (Tong dian), and presented it to counsel his ruler in a time of abundance and greatness. There was another who studied the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) in his family tradition and composed a commentary elucidating its meaning, guiding his ruler during a time of restoration. Do the Rites of Zhou and the Spring and Autumn Annals indeed have something in common with the Book of Documents (Shangshu) and the Mirror of the Tang? Did the ministers also have particular intentions in presenting their expositions? Discuss these matters fully, so that we may assess your learning in examining antiquity and serving the ruler.
Question: The realm cannot go a single day without the discussions of Confucian scholars. Some men of antiquity, in ordinary times, considered matters in advance and independently advanced views that could serve as models for all ages. Others devised plans when affairs arose, carefully examining changing circumstances and thereby establishing appropriate standards for their time. Yet when the matters discussed are the same but the arguments differ, there must be distinctions between right and wrong, benefit and harm. Let us take examples concerning governance and discuss them. Of enfeoffment, one said, “It was not the intention of the sages and cannot be put into practice.” Another, however, said, “The Way of Heaven is utterly impartial; one may await it for a hundred generations without doubt.” Of the well-field system, one said, “It can be implemented only after an age of disorder.” Another, however, said, “With the proper method of handling it, it can be restored without punishing a single person.” When mutilating punishments were replaced with flogging, commentators praised the ruler’s benevolence in cherishing life. Yet did others consider this an encouragement to the people to offend readily [?]? When the militia system was replaced with palace guards, commentators said that the ruler was showing compassion for the people…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
姓從軍之苦矣而或又以爲致兵農之
始分者馬論行禮不可泥古須當視時
之風氣者胡不同於必復古禮之言創
立貢舉私議分經書論策之年者胡不
酌夫四科取士之制之數者皆平居先
慮獨出己見者而其論既異則是非必
有可言者矣匈奴遠塞或欲誘致以擊
或欲結好以和而馬邑之詐誰其料之
弃𦊆入寇或請奮武立功或請留屯圖
===
策而先零之弊誰其秉之侍單于之禮
丞相御史與太傅之言孰宜議禧宣之
祧宰相宗枝與侍講之疏孰正靈州綏
州之城守群議當何所折衷而中當時
之會夏人遼人之攻伐衆言當何所取
正而免噬臍之患之數者皆臨事發謀
審察時變者而其言既殊則利害必有
可議者矣又其中人品不同意見隨之
得聖賢義理之中正而爲知言者顧以
punctuated: 姓從軍之苦矣，而或又以爲致兵農之始分者馬？論行禮不可泥古，須當視時之風氣者，胡不同於必復古禮之言？創立貢舉私議，分經書論策之年者，胡不酌夫四科取士之制？之數者，皆平居先慮、獨出己見者，而其論既異，則是非必有可言者矣。匈奴遠塞，或欲誘致以擊，或欲結好以和，而馬邑之詐，誰其料之？弃𦊆入寇，或請奮武立功，或請留屯圖策，而先零之弊，誰其秉之？侍單于之禮，丞相御史與太傅之言孰宜？議禧宣之祧，宰相宗枝與侍講之疏孰正？靈州綏州之城守，群議當何所折衷，而中當時之會？夏人遼人之攻伐，衆言當何所取正，而免噬臍之患？之數者，皆臨事發謀、審察時變者，而其言既殊，則利害必有可議者矣。又其中人品不同，意見隨之。得聖賢義理之中正而爲知言者，顧以
translation_en:
…the common people’s hardship in military service; yet others held that this brought about the initial separation of soldiers from farmers. Those who argued that ritual practice must not cling rigidly to antiquity but must take account of the prevailing customs of the age—why did they differ from those who insisted on restoring ancient rites? Those who formulated private proposals for tribute recruitment, assigning the classics, writings, discourses, and policy essays to separate years—why did they not weigh the system of selecting men under four categories? These several cases all concern men who deliberated beforehand in ordinary circumstances and independently advanced their own views. Since their arguments differed, there must be questions of right and wrong that can be discussed.

When the Xiongnu remained far beyond the frontier, some wished to lure them in and attack them, while others wished to establish friendly relations and make peace. Yet who anticipated the deception at Mayi? When 弃𦊆 [?] invaded, some requested vigorous military action to win distinction, while others requested that troops remain encamped while a strategy was devised. Yet who took charge of dealing with the troubles involving the Xianling [?]? Concerning the ceremonial treatment of the chanyu, whose statements were appropriate: those of the Counselor-in-Chief and the Censor-in-Chief, or those of the Grand Mentor? In the deliberations over removing Xi and Xuan from their ancestral shrines [?], whose submissions were correct: those of the chief councilors and imperial clansmen, or those of the Expositor-in-waiting? Regarding the fortification and defense of Lingzhou and Suizhou, how should the various proposals have been reconciled to meet the circumstances of the time? Regarding military campaigns against the people of Xia and Liao, which of the many opinions should have been accepted as correct, so as to avoid the anguish of futile regret? These several cases all concern men who devised plans when faced with events and carefully examined changing circumstances. Since their statements differed, there must be advantages and disadvantages that can be debated.

Moreover, these men differed in personal character, and their opinions varied accordingly. Yet those who grasp the balanced correctness of the sages’ and worthies’ moral principles and can discern the worth of words must rely on …

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
何者爲法邪諸士子群居思義其有槩
於中久矣今旣有叩之者其容以不言
乎
問任人而不任法則法簡而人重任法而
不任人則法密而人輕法簡而人重其
弊也請謁公行而私邪之黨盛法密而
人輕其弊也賢愚混滯而僥倖之俗成
昔人有是言矣是故有奏語務日薦人
至二千石者亦又有小心謹畏出入禁
===
闥不孤大事之託者焉有爲相二百日
除官八百員者亦又有失心論議共濟
時艱不負天子之知者焉執政紛更獨
爲國家當事與兩宮虛已以聽新政者
均之任人之專也而其弊果如昔人之
所論歟有謹守晝一民戴清靜者矣而
其後法具文深號爲厲政者乃成虛耗
之風有守文成務佐致太平者矣而其
後奏循資格人謂聖書者乃啓忠賢寃
punctuated:
何者爲法邪？諸士子群居思義，其有槩於中久矣。今旣有叩之者，其容以不言乎？

問：任人而不任法，則法簡而人重；任法而不任人，則法密而人輕。法簡而人重，其弊也請謁公行而私邪之黨盛；法密而人輕，其弊也賢愚混滯而僥倖之俗成。昔人有是言矣。是故有奏語務日薦人至二千石者，亦又有小心謹畏、出入禁闥、不孤大事之託者焉；有爲相二百日、除官八百員者，亦又有失心論議、共濟時艱、不負天子之知者焉。執政紛更，獨爲國家當事，與兩宮虛已以聽新政者，均之任人之專也，而其弊果如昔人之所論歟？有謹守晝一、民戴清靜者矣，而其後法具文深、號爲厲政者，乃成虛耗之風；有守文成務、佐致太平者矣，而其後奏循資格、人謂聖書者，乃啓忠賢寃
translation_en:
…what should be taken as the model? You candidates, living together and reflecting upon what is right, have long had thoughts on these matters. Now that someone has put the question to you, could you possibly remain silent?

Question: When reliance is placed upon men rather than laws, laws are simple and men carry weight; when reliance is placed upon laws rather than men, laws are elaborate and men carry little weight. When laws are simple and men carry weight, the resulting abuses are that requests for favors circulate openly and factions pursuing private and improper interests flourish. When laws are elaborate and men carry little weight, the resulting abuses are that worthy and foolish alike are held back indiscriminately, and a habit of seeking advancement through mere good fortune develops. People of former times have said this.

Thus, there was one who, in his submissions [?], made it his daily task to recommend men, including men for posts ranked at two thousand bushels; there was also one who was cautious and circumspect, entered and left the palace precincts, and did not betray the trust placed in him in great affairs. There was one who, during two hundred days as chief minister, appointed eight hundred officials; there were also those who deliberated with ‘lost hearts’ [?], joined in overcoming the difficulties of the times, and did not disappoint the Son of Heaven’s recognition of their abilities. One took sole responsibility for the state’s affairs amid repeated changes in government; in another instance, the occupants of the two palaces set aside their own views to give a hearing to new policies. These were equally instances of exclusive reliance upon men. Yet were their abuses really as earlier writers described?

There was one who scrupulously maintained uniformity [?], and whose quiet and undisturbing government won the people’s gratitude. Yet afterward, those whose laws were comprehensive and whose legal provisions were exacting, and whose government was called harsh, brought about a tendency toward depletion and exhaustion. There was one who observed established forms, accomplished affairs, and helped bring about peace. Yet afterward, submissions followed prescribed qualifications [?], and what people called ‘sacred writings’ opened the way to wrongs suffered by the loyal and worthy…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
諍護持新法更相汲引以進與各陳利
害以定法令者均之任法之專也而其
弊亦如昔人之所論歟茲欲任人必得
無或敢於專恣任法必行無或流於拘
畏必有至當之論也諸士子其悉言之
毋徒曰思不出其位
問知人安民帝王爲治之要道臣子所宜
敬承而將順之者也古人成說歷代所
行有可言乎今山東吏治固多得失所
===
患在於人心難保民情易移伊欲揆其
迹而詢之人則寸朽或至棄材容舟容
有漏網將如之何哉蓋嘗伏讀
祖宗之
訓有曰人有卓然自立不同於俗而得
毀者亦有諂媚狎昵同乎汙俗而得譽
者又曰有勤於職業不免施刑小人誣
爲酷暴者庸濫之官人所狎玩乃致吏
有保留者又曰有優於用刑巧於取索
而能集事者有廉潔無私謹身自守而
punctuated:
諍。護持新法，更相汲引以進，與各陳利害以定法令者，均之任法之專也，而其弊亦如昔人之所論歟？茲欲任人必得，無或敢於專恣；任法必行，無或流於拘畏，必有至當之論也。諸士子其悉言之，毋徒曰思不出其位。
問：知人安民，帝王爲治之要道，臣子所宜敬承而將順之者也。古人成說、歷代所行，有可言乎？今山東吏治固多得失，所患在於人心難保，民情易移。伊欲揆其迹而詢之人，則寸朽或至棄材，容舟容有漏網，將如之何哉？蓋嘗伏讀祖宗之訓，有曰：「人有卓然自立，不同於俗而得毀者；亦有諂媚狎昵，同乎汙俗而得譽者。」又曰：「有勤於職業，不免施刑，小人誣爲酷暴者；庸濫之官，人所狎玩，乃致吏有保留者。」又曰：「有優於用刑，巧於取索，而能集事者；有廉潔無私，謹身自守而
translation_en:
…remonstrance [?]. Those who upheld the New Policies and drew one another forward into office, and those who each set forth advantages and disadvantages to determine laws and ordinances, were alike in their exclusive reliance on laws. Were the resulting abuses also as earlier men described? Now we wish appointments invariably to secure suitable men, without anyone daring to act arbitrarily, and laws invariably to be implemented, without anyone lapsing into timid rigidity. There must be a wholly fitting account of how to achieve this. You candidates should explain it fully; do not merely say, “One’s thoughts do not go beyond one’s position.”
Question: Discerning men’s character and bringing peace to the people are essential principles of imperial government, which subjects ought respectfully to uphold and help carry out. What can be said about the established teachings of the ancients and the practices of successive dynasties? Today, the administration of officials in Shandong certainly has many successes and failures. The difficulty is that men’s hearts cannot reliably be counted upon, and popular sentiment changes readily. If we seek to assess their conduct and inquire about them among others, a little rot may cause an entire timber to be discarded, while a net with openings large enough for a boat may still let offenders escape [?]. What should be done?
I have reverently read the instructions of the imperial ancestors, which say: “There are men who stand firmly on their own, differ from prevailing customs, and are disparaged; there are also men who flatter and cultivate undue familiarity, conform to corrupt customs, and are praised.” They also say: “There are men who diligently discharge their duties and cannot avoid imposing punishments, whom petty men falsely accuse of cruelty and violence; mediocre and unworthy officials, whom people treat with contemptuous familiarity, may even come to be retained in office [?].” They further say: “There are men adept at administering punishments and skilful at exacting payments who can nevertheless get things done; there are men who are incorruptible and impartial, scrupulously guarding their own conduct, yet…”

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
政務不舉者
祖宗知人之明豈非萬世所當法者乎若山東
民生尤多疾苦所憂在於室家轉徙田
廬捐棄伊欲蠲其賦而還其人則額稅
不可或虧宿逋不容擅免又將如之何
哉亦嘗莊誦
祖宗之諭嘗因遣使賑恤省臣以國用不足爲
對乃曰得天下者得民心也宜速行之
又因南陽縣民逃徙有司乞令捕之乃
曰歸且何休捕之益困之耳又因議寬
登萊逋賦戶部亦以國用不足爲言乃
曰君臣一體民貧不可不恤也
===
祖宗安民之心豈非萬世所當體者乎
今上自即位以來屢下蠲逋賦復流移之詔近
又屢
俞吏部之請命撫按之臣訪察官吏賢否以
備黜陟不知撫按之臣所以究心而稽
事者道將安在抑不知吏治得失其
punctuated:
政務不舉者。」祖宗知人之明，豈非萬世所當法者乎？若山東民生尤多疾苦，所憂在於室家轉徙，田廬捐棄。伊欲蠲其賦而還其人，則額稅不可或虧，宿逋不容擅免，又將如之何哉？亦嘗莊誦祖宗之諭：嘗因遣使賑恤，省臣以國用不足爲對，乃曰：「得天下者，得民心也。宜速行之。」又因南陽縣民逃徙，有司乞令捕之，乃曰：「歸且何休？捕之益困之耳。」又因議寬登萊逋賦，戶部亦以國用不足爲言，乃曰：「君臣一體，民貧不可不恤也。」祖宗安民之心，豈非萬世所當體者乎？
今上自即位以來，屢下蠲逋賦、復流移之詔。近又屢俞吏部之請，命撫按之臣訪察官吏賢否，以備黜陟。不知撫按之臣所以究心而稽事者，道將安在？抑不知吏治得失其
translation_en:
…yet leave administrative affairs unattended.” Is not the ancestral emperors’ discernment in judging men something that should be emulated for ten thousand generations? In Shandong, the people suffer especially numerous hardships. The concern is that households migrate and abandon their fields and homes. If one wishes to remit their taxes and bring the people back, the prescribed tax quota must nevertheless suffer no shortfall, and arrears cannot be remitted without authorization. What, then, is to be done?
I have also reverently recited the ancestral emperors’ instructions. Once, when an emperor dispatched envoys to provide relief, officials of the Secretariat responded that state revenues were insufficient. He then said: “To gain All-under-Heaven is to gain the people’s hearts. Carry this out promptly.” Again, when people fled Nanyang County and the responsible officials requested orders to arrest them, he said: “Even if they return, what respite will they have [?]? Arresting them will only compound their distress.” Again, when relief from tax arrears in Dengzhou and Laizhou was being discussed, the Ministry of Revenue likewise pleaded insufficient state revenues. He then said: “Ruler and ministers form one body. When the people are impoverished, we cannot fail to relieve them.” Is not the ancestral emperors’ concern for bringing peace to the people something that should be embodied for ten thousand generations?
Since ascending the throne, the present emperor has repeatedly issued edicts remitting tax arrears and restoring displaced people to their homes. Recently, he has also repeatedly approved requests from the Ministry of Personnel, ordering grand coordinators and regional inspectors to investigate the worthiness of officials and clerks, as a basis for dismissal and promotion. By what means, one wonders, should these grand coordinators and regional inspectors apply themselves conscientiously and investigate affairs? Or, one wonders, do the successes and failures of official administration …

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
生疾苦果有相關進退之間亦可收安
輯之效乎諸生幸明言之以觀所以留
心世務者
punctuated: 生疾苦果有相關，進退之間亦可收安輯之效乎？諸生幸明言之，以觀所以留心世務者。
translation_en: …are indeed related to the people’s livelihood and hardships [?], and can the promotion and dismissal of officials also help bring peace and stability to the people? You students are requested to explain this clearly, so that we may see how you attend to the affairs of the world.

text:
第壹塲
四書
見善如不及見不善如探湯
林�William

考試官教諭何　批〔善惡非真知不能好惡子旨盡見是宜錄之〕
〔之此作其亦真知者乎〕
===
考試官教授蔣　批〔明暢痛切〕
真知其善而好之誠真知其惡而惡之誠夫人
莫不好惡而能誠者鮮矣自非知善惡之真者
豈能極其誠哉聖人引古語如此其意謂夫人
性惟有善而無惡故人情皆好善而惡惡彼其
原於天命人心之正而全之可進於聖賢者善
也善固人之所同好矣然而好之有不誠者以
其知之未真焉耳今其見是善也知爲懿德可
好而中心好之初非矯飾於容貌知爲理義可
punctuated:
第壹塲。
四書。
「見善如不及，見不善如探湯。」
林�William
同考試官教諭楊，批〔論語題雖若平易，作者多爲所窘，且知二如字意者亦少。此篇從容數語而本〕
考試官教諭何，批〔善惡非真知不能好惡，子旨盡見，是宜錄之。〕
〔之此作，其亦真知者乎？〕
考試官教授蔣，批〔明暢痛切。〕

真知其善，而好之誠；真知其惡，而惡之誠。夫人莫不好惡，而能誠者鮮矣。自非知善惡之真者，豈能極其誠哉？聖人引古語如此，其意謂：夫人性惟有善而無惡，故人情皆好善而惡惡。彼其原於天命人心之正，而全之可進於聖賢者，善也。善固人之所同好矣，然而好之有不誠者，以其知之未真焉耳。今其見是善也，知爲懿德可好，而中心好之，初非矯飾於容貌；知爲理義可

Truly knowing something to be good, one is sincere in loving it; truly knowing something to be evil, one is sincere in hating it. Everyone has likes and dislikes, but few can be sincere in them. Unless one truly knows good and evil, how can one attain the utmost sincerity? In quoting this ancient saying, the Sage means this: human nature contains only goodness and no evil, and thus human feelings all incline toward loving goodness and hating evil. What originates in the correctness of Heaven's mandate and the human heart, and what, when preserved whole, enables one to advance toward sagehood and worthiness, is goodness. Goodness is indeed what everyone loves. Yet some are insincere in loving it simply because their knowledge of it is not yet true. title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
悅而我心悅之初非勉强於辭色篤好於深喻
之餘必欲得之於心而勇猛精進之志浩乎其
莫遏也欣慕於黙契之際必欲體之於身而邁
往直前之氣勃乎其莫禦也皇皇焉無異有所
追而弗逮者焉其進也豈能已乎真知其善而
好之誠有如此乃若生於人情物欲之私而溺
之近於禽獸者不善也不善固人所同惡然
而惡之有不誠者以其知之未真焉耳今見夫
不善也知爲脩德之累而奮然惡之蓋出於疾
===
惡之真情知爲制行之玷而毅然惡之蓋發於
羞惡之實念痛絶於滌濯之後惟恐其或萌於
心而防衛之嚴一息不敢懈也深懲於猛省之
中惟恐其或加於身而畏避之念一刻不敢寧
也惴惴焉無異折沸湯而恐傷者焉其止也豈
容緩乎真知其惡而惡之誠有如此吁誠於好
善則於善也不患其不爲誠於惡惡則於惡也
不患其或爲然非知至意誠孰能與於斯哉抑
斯義也其在聖門顔曾閔冉之徒蓋嘗之故曰
punctuated: 悅，而我心悅之，初非勉强於辭色。篤好於深喻之餘，必欲得之於心，而勇猛精進之志浩乎其莫遏也；欣慕於黙契之際，必欲體之於身，而邁往直前之氣勃乎其莫禦也。皇皇焉，無異有所追而弗逮者焉，其進也豈能已乎？真知其善而好之誠有如此。乃若生於人情物欲之私，而溺之近於禽獸者，不善也。不善固人所同惡，然而惡之有不誠者，以其知之未真焉耳。今見夫不善也，知爲脩德之累而奮然惡之，蓋出於疾惡之真情；知爲制行之玷而毅然惡之，蓋發於羞惡之實念。痛絶於滌濯之後，惟恐其或萌於心，而防衛之嚴，一息不敢懈也；深懲於猛省之中，惟恐其或加於身，而畏避之念，一刻不敢寧也。惴惴焉，無異折沸湯而恐傷者焉，其止也豈容緩乎？真知其惡而惡之誠有如此。吁！誠於好善，則於善也不患其不爲；誠於惡惡，則於惡也不患其或爲。然非知至意誠，孰能與於斯哉？抑斯義也，其在聖門顔曾閔冉之徒蓋嘗之，故曰：
translation_en:
…delightful, and my heart delights in it, without any forced expression in words or countenance. After understanding it deeply, one loves it ardently and is determined to attain it within the heart; the resolve to advance with courage and diligence surges beyond restraint. In moments of silent comprehension, one admires it joyfully and is determined to embody it in oneself; the vigor of pressing straight ahead rises irresistibly. Eager and anxious, one is like someone pursuing something yet unable to catch it. How could such progress cease? Such is the sincerity of loving goodness when one truly knows it to be good.
As for what arises from the selfishness of human feelings and material desires, indulgence in which brings one close to birds and beasts: this is what is not good. Everyone indeed hates what is not good. Yet some are insincere in their hatred because their knowledge of it is not yet true. Now, on seeing what is not good, one knows it to be a hindrance to cultivating virtue and vehemently hates it: this comes from a genuine feeling of abhorrence for evil. One knows it to be a blemish upon the regulation of one’s conduct and resolutely hates it: this arises from a sincere sense of shame and aversion. Having cleansed oneself, one utterly severs oneself from it, fearing only that it might sprout again within the heart; so strict is one’s vigilance that one dares not relax for a single breath. Amid searching self-examination, one sternly checks oneself, fearing only that it might attach itself to one’s person; the determination to shun it in dread permits not a moment’s ease. Apprehensive, one is like someone handling boiling water [?] and fearing injury. How could one permit any delay in stopping it? Such is the sincerity of hating evil when one truly knows it to be evil.
Ah! If one is sincere in loving goodness, there is no need to fear that one will fail to practice it; if one is sincere in hating evil, there is no need to fear that one might commit it. Yet unless one’s knowledge has reached its fullest extent and one’s intentions are sincere, who can attain this? Indeed, among the disciples of the Sage, those such as Yan, Zeng, Min, and Ran surely experienced this principle. Thus it is said: …

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
吾聞其語吾見其人矣若隱居以求其志行義
以達其道者則非伊尹太公之流莫與焉使顔
子而壽亦幾矣此夫子所以有未見之歎也噫
其真思賢也夫其亦有感於世道也夫
正己而不求於人則無怨

考試官教授蔣　批〔理明氣貫可以式矣〕
===
惟無所慕於外斯無所動於中蓋怨生於心有
所慕也君子既無慕於外矣則爆何自而動耶
中哉中庸論君子不願乎其外而申之如此意
謂物我相形而求望之心易生上下皆安而怨
尤之意自泯是故居上陵下是舍己而求於人
矣君子則知上之非泰而所以自治者為甚詳
故覆餗是懼而慮吾泰正之未端負乘是憂而
punctuated:
吾聞其語，吾見其人矣。若隱居以求其志，行義以達其道者，則非伊尹、太公之流莫與焉。使顔子而壽，亦幾矣。此夫子所以有未見之歎也。噫！其真思賢也夫！其亦有感於世道也夫！

正己而不求於人，則無怨。

惟無所慕於外，斯無所動於中。蓋怨生於心有所慕也。君子既無慕於外矣，則爆何自而動耶？中哉！中庸論君子不願乎其外，而申之如此。意謂物我相形，而求望之心易生；上下皆安，而怨尤之意自泯。是故居上陵下，是舍己而求於人矣。君子則知上之非泰，而所以自治者為甚詳。故覆餗是懼，而慮吾泰正之未端；負乘是憂，而
translation_en:
…“I have heard such words, and I have seen such men.” But as for those who live in seclusion to pursue their aspirations and practice righteousness to realize their Way, only men of the kind of Yi Yin and Taigong can rank among them. Had Master Yan lived longer, he too would have come close. This is why the Master sighed that he had never seen such a man. Ah! How truly he longed for worthy men! How deeply he must also have felt about the state of the world!

“He rectifies himself and seeks nothing from others; thus he has no resentment.”
By Wang Hua.
Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The meaning and argument of the phrases before and after this topic are interconnected. Writers often fail to appreciate this closely and depart considerably from the original purport. Reading this essay, one cannot help feeling refreshed. It deserves a high recommendation.〕
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: 〔The principles of the Doctrine of the Mean are subtle and precise; unless a writer searches deeply,〕〔he cannot understand them. The author of this essay has surely attained understanding and cannot be regarded as an ordinary scholar.〕
Examiner Jiang, Professor, comments: 〔The principles are clear and the vital force runs throughout. It can serve as a model.〕

Only when one covets nothing external will nothing stir within. Resentment arises because the heart covets something. Since the gentleman covets nothing external, from what could an outburst [?] arise? How fitting [?]! The Doctrine of the Mean discusses how the gentleman does not desire anything beyond his own position, and elaborates upon it in this way. Its meaning is that when external things and oneself are compared, a disposition to seek and expect readily arises; when those above and below are content in their positions, feelings of resentment and blame naturally disappear. Thus, to occupy a superior position and domineer over those below is to neglect oneself and make demands upon others. The gentleman knows that a superior position is no occasion for arrogance, and so attends most closely to governing himself. He therefore fears overturning the cauldron’s food, worrying that his own rectitude [?] is not yet properly established; he is anxious about carrying a burden while riding in a carriage, and …

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
勉吾道德之奉至惟知盡其在我而已而其在
人者固有所不暇求焉在下援上是自畧而詳
於人矣君子則知下之非約而所以自反者爲
甚備故出位爲戒而拳拳於義命之安踰節爲
恥而勉勉於貞介之守但知正其在己而已而
其在外者則有所不敢望焉不求於人如此夫
何怨乎誠以陵下不應怨斯生矣惟其無求於
下則不復見下之非而無所惡於下焉援上不
副怨斯作矣惟其不求於上則不復見上之非
===
而無所惡於上焉不驕不亢順適於物我兩忘
之天方寸坦然而不平之念固無自而生也不
諂不憂從容於義命相安之境胸次悠然而不
足之意固無自而形也是則不難於無所怨而
難於無所求此君子所以不願乎其外也道之
不可離也不於是而見哉抑不怨不亢學者事
也而他日夫子乃以自況且謂上達由於此焉
是豈可以易視也哉盖原其始固居易俟命之
事而要其終則樂天知命之境其實不越正己
punctuated: 勉吾道德之奉至，惟知盡其在我而已，而其在人者，固有所不暇求焉。在下援上，是自畧而詳於人矣。君子則知下之非約，而所以自反者爲甚備，故出位爲戒，而拳拳於義命之安；踰節爲恥，而勉勉於貞介之守。但知正其在己而已，而其在外者，則有所不敢望焉。不求於人如此，夫何怨乎？誠以陵下不應，怨斯生矣；惟其無求於下，則不復見下之非，而無所惡於下焉。援上不副，怨斯作矣；惟其不求於上，則不復見上之非，而無所惡於上焉。不驕不亢，順適於物我兩忘之天，方寸坦然而不平之念固無自而生也；不諂不憂，從容於義命相安之境，胸次悠然而不足之意固無自而形也。是則不難於無所怨，而難於無所求，此君子所以不願乎其外也。道之不可離也，不於是而見哉？抑不怨不亢，學者事也，而他日夫子乃以自況，且謂上達由於此焉，是豈可以易視也哉？盖原其始，固居易俟命之事，而要其終，則樂天知命之境，其實不越正己
translation_en: …and strive to bring my cultivation of moral virtue to its utmost [?]. He knows only to fulfill what lies within himself; as for what depends on others, he has no leisure to seek it. To reach upward toward those above while occupying a low position is to give scant attention to oneself and exacting attention to others. The gentleman knows that a low position need not constrain him, and so his self-examination is most thorough. Thus he guards against stepping beyond his position and earnestly rests content with righteousness and his allotted fate; he regards overstepping his proper bounds as shameful and diligently maintains his integrity. He knows only to rectify what lies within himself; as for what lies outside him, he does not dare set his hopes upon it. Seeking nothing from others in this way, what cause has he for resentment? Indeed, when one domineers over those below and they do not respond, resentment arises. Only because he seeks nothing from those below does he cease to see their faults and have nothing to dislike in them. When one reaches upward toward those above and they fail to meet one's expectations, resentment arises. Only because he seeks nothing from those above does he cease to see their faults and have nothing to dislike in them. Neither arrogant nor overbearing, he rests at ease in a natural state in which both external things and the self are forgotten. His heart is tranquil, and thoughts of injustice have no source from which to arise. Neither flattering nor anxious, he moves calmly in a realm where righteousness and his allotted fate are reconciled. His breast is at ease, and feelings of insufficiency have no source from which to take shape. Thus the difficulty lies not in having no resentment, but in seeking nothing. This is why the gentleman does not desire what lies outside his position. Is it not here that we see that the Way cannot be departed from? Moreover, to be without resentment or overbearing pride is the work of the learner; yet on another occasion the Master used this to describe himself, and further said that attaining higher understanding proceeded from it. How could this be regarded lightly? Tracing it to its beginning, it is indeed a matter of dwelling in ease and awaiting one's allotted fate; considering its culmination, it is the state of delighting in Heaven and understanding one's allotted fate. In substance, it goes no further than rectifying oneself…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
無求而已矣道豈多乎哉先儒謂中庸一書其
用無窮皆實學也信夫
君子之於物也愛之而弗仁於民也仁之
而弗親親親而仁民仁民而愛物
尹寵
同考試官教諭高　批〔此理一分殊之學非見到者不能言子能言之有味足見所養矣〕
同考試官學正趙　批〔作孟子義者詞多重複擇焉而詳無踰此篇者矣〕
同考試官教授汪　批〔說理明白而詞氣舂容是善作者〕
===
考試官教諭何　批〔說親仁愛三字甚明白〕
考試官教授蔣　批〔文有關鍵可取〕
大賢論君子之仁不混於所施而必循其序焉
甚矣理一而分殊也君子之仁曷嘗混於所施
而不循其序哉昔孟子之意謂夫天下之分固
有不同而君子之仁不能無等是故物爲吾與
固有愛之理也君子雖不能不取而取之有時
punctuated:
無求而已矣，道豈多乎哉？先儒謂《中庸》一書，其用無窮，皆實學也。信夫！

君子之於物也，愛之而弗仁；於民也，仁之而弗親。親親而仁民，仁民而愛物。

尹寵

同考試官教諭高　批〔此理一分殊之學，非見到者不能言。子能言之有味，足見所養矣。〕

同考試官學正趙　批〔作孟子義者，詞多重複，擇焉而詳，無踰此篇者矣。〕

同考試官教授汪　批〔說理明白，而詞氣舂容，是善作者。〕

考試官教諭何　批〔說親仁愛三字甚明白。〕

考試官教授蔣　批〔文有關鍵，可取。〕

大賢論君子之仁，不混於所施，而必循其序焉。甚矣，理一而分殊也！君子之仁曷嘗混於所施而不循其序哉？昔孟子之意，謂夫天下之分固有不同，而君子之仁不能無等。是故物爲吾與，固有愛之理也。君子雖不能不取，而取之有時，
translation_en:
…seeking nothing, that is all. How could the Way require much more? Earlier Confucian scholars said that the Doctrine of the Mean has inexhaustible applications and consists entirely of practical learning. How true!

“With regard to things, the gentleman cherishes them but does not treat them with benevolence; with regard to the people, he treats them with benevolence but does not treat them as his own kin. He loves his kin and extends benevolence to the people; he treats the people with benevolence and extends his care to things.”

Yin Chong

Comment by Associate Examiner Gao, Instructor: 〔This is the learning of the unity of principle and the differentiation of its particular manifestations. Only someone who has attained true insight can articulate it. Your ability to express it with depth and savor amply demonstrates your cultivation.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Director of Studies: 〔Those who compose expositions on the meaning of the Mengzi often repeat themselves. In selecting what to discuss and explaining it fully, no essay surpasses this one.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Professor: 〔The reasoning is clear, and the language and tone are composed and ample [?]. This is the work of a skilled writer.〕

Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: 〔The three terms—affection for kin, benevolence, and care—are explained very clearly.〕

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: 〔The essay has effective structural connections and merits approval.〕

The great worthy discusses the gentleman’s benevolence: it does not confound the recipients of its application, but invariably follows its proper order. How profound is the unity of principle amid the differentiation of its particular manifestations! When has the gentleman’s benevolence ever confounded its recipients and failed to follow its proper order? The meaning of Mengzi’s words was that distinctions in the world are indeed diverse, and the gentleman’s benevolence therefore cannot be without gradations. Thus, things are our companions, and there is inherently a principle requiring that we cherish them. Although the gentleman cannot avoid taking them, he takes them at the proper times…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
不能不用而用之有節愛之而已不以施之人
者施于物焉民吾同胞固有仁之道也君子則
庶欲其富而養之有制愚欲其明而教之有方
仁之而已不以待乎親者待其民焉夫以仁之
而弗親者非薄於民也以親爲一體而民則同
類者也故篤近舉遠必仁施一家而後有平章
之政息逮九族而後有脩和之治寸理貫通之
中而燦然内外之有序焉曷嘗以民而先於親
乎愛之而弗仁者非嗇於物也以民吾同胞而
===
物則異類者也故由重逮輕必功加百姓而餘
息始及於庶類惠先群黎而餘澤始被於萬物
至仁兼覆之内而秩然貴賤之有倫焉曷嘗以
物而先於民乎吁於一視同仁之中而有稱物
平施之則此君子之仁所以無弊也歟嗟夫是
道也吾儒大中至正之矩也奈何墨氏兼愛而
害吾等楊氏爲我而病吾博甚至愛一牛而功
或不至於百姓泣有罪而忍宗廟之不血食者
焉去道不亦遠乎然則如之何必智以明之義
punctuated:
不能不用，而用之有節，愛之而已，不以施之人者施于物焉。民吾同胞，固有仁之道也。君子則庶欲其富，而養之有制；愚欲其明，而教之有方。仁之而已，不以待乎親者待其民焉。夫以仁之而弗親者，非薄於民也，以親爲一體，而民則同類者也。故篤近舉遠，必仁施一家，而後有平章之政；息逮九族，而後有脩和之治。寸理貫通之中，而燦然内外之有序焉，曷嘗以民而先於親乎？愛之而弗仁者，非嗇於物也，以民吾同胞，而物則異類者也。故由重逮輕，必功加百姓，而餘息始及於庶類；惠先群黎，而餘澤始被於萬物。至仁兼覆之内，而秩然貴賤之有倫焉，曷嘗以物而先於民乎？
吁！於一視同仁之中，而有稱物平施之則，此君子之仁所以無弊也歟！嗟夫！是道也，吾儒大中至正之矩也。奈何墨氏兼愛而害吾等，楊氏爲我而病吾博，甚至愛一牛而功或不至於百姓，泣有罪而忍宗廟之不血食者焉！去道不亦遠乎？然則如之何？必智以明之，義
translation_en:
…He cannot avoid using things, yet uses them with restraint. He merely cares for them, without extending to things what he bestows upon human beings. The people are our siblings, and there is inherently a way of treating them with benevolence. When they are numerous, the gentleman wishes them to prosper and provides for them through established arrangements; when they are ignorant, he wishes them to gain understanding and instructs them by appropriate methods. He merely treats them with benevolence, without treating the people as he treats his own kin. To treat them benevolently without the intimacy reserved for kin is not to slight the people: one’s kin form a single body with oneself, whereas the people belong to the same human kind. Thus, in showing deep affection for those nearby and extending it to those far away, benevolence must first reach one’s own household before there can be government that brings harmonious order; favor [?] must reach the nine degrees of kinship before there can be rule that cultivates harmony. Within the all-pervading principle [?], the distinction between inner and outer circles remains resplendently ordered. How could the people ever take precedence over one’s kin? To care for things without treating them with benevolence is not to be ungenerous toward things: the people are our siblings, whereas things belong to other kinds. Thus, in proceeding from the weightier to the lighter, beneficial achievements must reach the common people before the remaining favor [?] extends to the various other kinds of beings; kindness must first reach the multitude before its remaining bounty spreads to all things. Within the encompassing shelter of utmost benevolence, the more and less worthy have their orderly ranks. How could things ever take precedence over the people?
Ah! Within an equal regard and shared benevolence toward all, there is nevertheless a rule of weighing each recipient and bestowing appropriately. Is this not why the gentleman’s benevolence is free from defects? Alas! This Way is the standard of supreme balance and utmost correctness among us Confucians. Why, then, does Mozi’s universal love undermine our gradations, while Yangzi’s devotion to self impairs our breadth of concern? There are even those who cherish a single ox while their beneficial achievements may fail to reach the common people, or who weep for the guilty yet bear to see their ancestral temples deprived of blood sacrifices! Are they not far removed from the Way? What, then, should one do? One must use wisdom to understand it, and righteousness…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
以裁之而後行
易
乾元用九天下治也
呂夔
同考試官教諭楊　批〔題本是君道剛而能柔而作者多以剛柔二字互換言之昧本旨矣此作獨〕
〔為有見而詞致精確是之取爾〕
考試官教諭何　批〔觀此作亦見善言治道不獨善說經而已〕
===
考試官教授蔣　批〔詞整意足〕
惟君道剛而能柔則治化無不成矣夫君道主
剛而其用則柔也孰謂天下之治有不成於此
乎文言此節再申象傳之意謂夫乾之在人為
君而乾元則君之道也九之於陽為老而用九
則老之變也是蓋君人者政令一施有以威天
下而使之服然必審時度理以即乎人情之所
安焉紀綱一布有以慵天下而使之從然必虛
心取善以求乎至理之所在焉勇以進道斷以
punctuated:
以裁之，而後行。

易
乾元用九，天下治也。
呂夔
同考試官教諭楊批〔題本是君道剛而能柔，而作者多以剛柔二字互換言之，昧本旨矣。此作獨〕〔為有見，而詞致精確，是之取爾。〕
考試官教諭何批〔觀此作，亦見善言治道，不獨善說經而已。〕
考試官教授蔣批〔詞整意足。〕

惟君道剛而能柔，則治化無不成矣。夫君道主剛，而其用則柔也，孰謂天下之治有不成於此乎？文言此節再申象傳之意，謂夫乾之在人為君，而乾元則君之道也。九之於陽為老，而用九則老之變也。是蓋君人者，政令一施，有以威天下而使之服，然必審時度理，以即乎人情之所安焉；紀綱一布，有以慵天下而使之從，然必虛心取善，以求乎至理之所在焉。勇以進道，斷以
translation_en:
…to regulate it, and only then put it into practice.

Book of Changes
“When the primal power of Qian employs the nines, all under Heaven is well governed.”
Lü Kui

Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: 〔The topic is fundamentally about the ruler’s Way being firm yet capable of yielding. Most writers, however, speak interchangeably of firmness and yielding, obscuring the original meaning. This composition alone〕〔shows insight, and its expression is precise. This is why it was selected.〕
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: 〔This composition also demonstrates skill in discussing the Way of government, beyond merely explaining the classic well.〕
Examiner Jiang, Professor, comments: 〔The language is well ordered and the meaning fully developed.〕

Only when the ruler’s Way is firm yet capable of yielding will governance and moral transformation attain complete success. The ruler’s Way rests chiefly on firmness, but its application is yielding. Who could say that good government throughout the realm would fail to arise from this? This section of the Commentary on the Words of the Text reiterates the meaning of the Commentary on the Images. It means that Qian, in human affairs, represents the ruler, while Qian’s primal power represents the ruler’s Way. Nine is mature yang, and employing the nines is the transformation of mature yang.

Thus, when one who rules others issues policies and commands, he has the means to overawe all under Heaven and make them submit. Yet he must examine the circumstances and weigh what is right, so as to accord with what people find acceptable. Once he establishes the principles and framework of government, he has the means to stir [?] all under Heaven and make them comply. Yet he must remain open-minded and adopt what is good, seeking where ultimate principle resides. With courage he advances the Way; with decisiveness he…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
成功而出之以巽順之從容蓋剛健而中正者
也奚有於過乎強以守正義以制事而文之以
禮樂之和平蓋剛善而中節者也焉有所倚乎
夫君道剛而能柔如此而天下豈有不治哉蓋
過剛則傷於厲而道難行矣今也剛中有柔則
政令皆順乎理而四方于是乎承式焉太剛則
失於猛而治難成矣今也剛能濟則紀綱皆
合乎度而萬國于是乎向風焉德威所及自將
不肅而成道行斯世而功澤及民也天下有不
===
化中者乎道化所加自將不嚴而治正爲民表
而事爲民則也天下有不化成者乎是則君道
之所主在剛而剛德之所用在柔君道之無不
備則治道之無不成也文言申象傳之意而以
是言之其旨遠哉大抵剛而能柔天之法也君
道以之安而且貞地之德也臣道以之君道主
成而不欲矜己驕物臣道無成而不可枉道屈
身天下之治豈不在於是乎故曰天地交而萬
物通也上下交而其志同也讀易者引而伸之
punctuated: 成功，而出之以巽順之從容，蓋剛健而中正者也，奚有於過乎？強以守正，義以制事，而文之以禮樂之和平，蓋剛善而中節者也，焉有所倚乎？夫君道剛而能柔如此，而天下豈有不治哉？蓋過剛則傷於厲，而道難行矣。今也剛中有柔，則政令皆順乎理，而四方于是乎承式焉。太剛則失於猛，而治難成矣。今也剛能濟，則紀綱皆合乎度，而萬國于是乎向風焉。德威所及，自將不肅而成，道行斯世，而功澤及民也，天下有不化中者乎？道化所加，自將不嚴而治，正爲民表，而事爲民則也，天下有不化成者乎？是則君道之所主在剛，而剛德之所用在柔；君道之無不備，則治道之無不成也。文言申象傳之意，而以是言之，其旨遠哉！大抵剛而能柔，天之法也，君道以之；安而且貞，地之德也，臣道以之。君道主成，而不欲矜己驕物；臣道無成，而不可枉道屈身。天下之治，豈不在於是乎？故曰：「天地交而萬物通也，上下交而其志同也。」讀易者引而伸之
translation_en: …to bring achievement to completion, yet expressing this through the composure of yielding compliance: this is strength and vigor joined with centrality and correctness. How could there be excess? Firm in upholding what is right, using righteousness to regulate affairs, yet adorning these with the harmony of rites and music: this is good firmness that accords with the proper measure. How could there be any partiality? If the ruler’s Way is firm yet capable of yielding in this manner, how could all under Heaven fail to be well governed? Excessive firmness causes harm through severity, making the Way difficult to put into practice. But when firmness contains yielding, governmental commands all accord with principle, and the four quarters accordingly accept them as their standard. Overbearing firmness errs through ferocity, making good government difficult to achieve. But when firmness can be tempered [?], the guiding principles and regulations all accord with proper measure, and the myriad states accordingly turn toward its influence. Wherever virtuous authority reaches, achievement will naturally come without sternness: the Way will prevail in this age, and its accomplishments and benefits will reach the people. Could anyone under Heaven fail to be transformed toward the mean [?]? Wherever the Way’s transforming influence extends, order will naturally come without severity: rectitude will provide the people with a model, and actions will provide them with a rule. Could anyone under Heaven fail to be transformed and perfected? Thus the ruler’s Way rests on firmness, while firm virtue operates through yielding. When the ruler’s Way is complete in every respect, the Way of government achieves everything. The Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) elaborates the meaning of the Commentary on the Images (Xiangzhuan) in these terms: how far-reaching its purport is! Broadly speaking, being firm yet capable of yielding is Heaven’s pattern, which the ruler’s Way follows; being settled and steadfast is Earth’s virtue, which the minister’s Way follows. The ruler’s Way presides over achievement, yet must not exalt the self or treat others arrogantly. The minister’s Way claims no achievement of its own, yet must not bend the Way or debase oneself. Does not good government throughout the world depend on this? Thus it is said: “Heaven and Earth interact, and the myriad things communicate; those above and those below interact, and their purposes are shared.” Those who read the Book of Changes and extend its implications…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
抑可見其廣大悉備矣
極數知來之謂占通變之謂事
林瓊
同考試官教諭楊　批　極數知來通變雖分占事而實一事也士子逐句生詞多欠通貫得此篇讀之
喜其條理分明而氣脉不斷益深於易者歟
考試官教諭何　批　作易義如此可謂精矣
考試官教授蔣　批　觀此作不惟見道寓於陰
陽之妙而揲蓍用易之方如指諸掌
===
求易以前用而占所由名推易以致用而事所
由名盖占因數得事以占通也即其未定已決
之間豈不有陰陽之道哉大傳論一陰一陽之
謂道而推之占事如此謂夫道之體用不外乎
陰陽而易之占事分屬乎陰陽是故有易必有
占也占何為而著耶盖揲蓍求卦之餘即陰陽
之數究其或老或少以觀所值之何卦因老少
之數考其變與不變以求所得之何爻由是以
卦辭之所告而決在我之疑則未來之吉凶洞
punctuated:
抑可見其廣大悉備矣。

極數知來之謂占，通變之謂事。

林瓊

同考試官教諭楊批：極數知來、通變，雖分占事，而實一事也。士子逐句生詞，多欠通貫。得此篇讀之，喜其條理分明而氣脉不斷，益深於易者歟！

考試官教諭何批：作易義如此，可謂精矣。

考試官教授蔣批：觀此作，不惟見道寓於陰陽之妙，而揲蓍用易之方，如指諸掌。

求易以前用，而占所由名；推易以致用，而事所由名。盖占因數得，事以占通也。即其未定已決之間，豈不有陰陽之道哉？大傳論「一陰一陽之謂道」，而推之占事如此。謂夫道之體用不外乎陰陽，而易之占事分屬乎陰陽。是故有易必有占也。占何為而著耶？盖揲蓍求卦之餘，即陰陽之數，究其或老或少，以觀所值之何卦；因老少之數，考其變與不變，以求所得之何爻。由是以卦辭之所告而決在我之疑，則未來之吉凶洞
translation_en:
…one may thus also perceive its vastness and complete comprehensiveness.

“To fathom the numbers and know what is to come is called divination; to comprehend change and act accordingly is called undertaking affairs.”

Lin Qiong 林瓊

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: Fathoming the numbers to know what is to come and comprehending change are distinguished as divination and undertaking affairs, yet in reality they constitute a single activity. Candidates often compose phrases sentence by sentence, without connecting them into a coherent whole. On reading this essay, I delighted in its clear organization and uninterrupted flow. Surely its author has attained a deeper understanding of the Book of Changes!

Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: An interpretation of the Book of Changes written like this may indeed be called penetrating.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: Reading this composition, one sees not only the subtlety of the Way embodied in yin and yang; the method of manipulating yarrow stalks and putting the Book of Changes to use is also as clear as something pointed out in one’s palm.

Consulting the Book of Changes in anticipation of its application [?] is what gives divination its name; extending the Book of Changes into practical application is what gives undertaking affairs its name. Divination is obtained through numbers, while affairs are carried through by means of divination. Between what remains unsettled and what has already been decided, is not the Way of yin and yang present? The Great Commentary discusses how “one yin and one yang are called the Way,” and extends this principle to divination and affairs in this manner. This means that the substance and operation of the Way do not go beyond yin and yang, and that divination and affairs in the Book of Changes belong respectively to yang and yin. Thus, wherever there is the Book of Changes, there must be divination. How, then, does divination become manifest? The remainders from manipulating the yarrow stalks to seek a hexagram are the numbers of yin and yang. One investigates whether they are old or young to see which hexagram has been encountered; on the basis of these old and young numbers, one examines which change and which do not, to determine which line has been obtained. Then, through what the hexagram statement declares, one resolves one’s doubts, and future good or ill fortune becomes clearly…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
然可以前知矣以爻辭之所示而通在已之志
則未至之悔吝昭然可以逆覩矣是蓋諏筮問
易之時故謂之占焉占則事之未定而屬乎陽
者也乃若有占必有事也事何爲而行耶蓋極
數知來之後于其凶吉之所在推而行之惟道
之是從因其悔吝之所向順而止之惟時之是
尚故夫事變無常而辭則有常也必率辭揆方
行典禮於會通之中事情不一而占則惟一也
必玩占觀變成變化於擬議之際是蓋成務定
===
業之時故謂之事焉事則占之已决而屬乎陰
者也吁陰陽雖寓于占事之間而其所以然者
則神之所爲也夫豈倚於陰陽者哉雖然此執
易之用處言爾若神以知來知以藏往則又聖
人之心易也聖人以其心易之妙而寓之揲蓍
求卦之間所以前民之用而使之得與聖人之
能也此其所以爲陰陽不測之神歟然則學易
者宜何如亦曰卦爻之所以變通者在人人之
所以能神而明之者在德
punctuated:
然可以前知矣。以爻辭之所示而通在已之志，則未至之悔吝昭然可以逆覩矣。是蓋諏筮問易之時，故謂之占焉。占則事之未定而屬乎陽者也。乃若有占必有事也，事何爲而行耶？蓋極數知來之後，于其凶吉之所在，推而行之，惟道之是從；因其悔吝之所向，順而止之，惟時之是尚。故夫事變無常，而辭則有常也，必率辭揆方，行典禮於會通之中；事情不一，而占則惟一也，必玩占觀變，成變化於擬議之際。是蓋成務定業之時，故謂之事焉。事則占之已决而屬乎陰者也。
吁！陰陽雖寓于占事之間，而其所以然者，則神之所爲也，夫豈倚於陰陽者哉？雖然，此執易之用處言爾。若神以知來，知以藏往，則又聖人之心易也。聖人以其心易之妙，而寓之揲蓍求卦之間，所以前民之用，而使之得與聖人之能也。此其所以爲陰陽不測之神歟？然則學易者宜何如？亦曰：卦爻之所以變通者在人人之所以能神而明之者在德。
translation_en:
…can clearly be known beforehand. By comprehending one’s own intentions through what the line statements disclose, one can plainly foresee occasions for regret and humiliation before they arrive. This is the moment of consulting the milfoil stalks and questioning the Book of Changes, and so it is called divination. Divination concerns affairs that are not yet settled and belongs to yang. Now, wherever there is divination, there must also be action. How, then, is action undertaken? After fully exploring the numbers and thereby knowing what is to come, one proceeds to act on what they indicate as inauspicious or auspicious, following only the Way; in accordance with the direction they indicate toward regret or humiliation, one restrains one’s action, attending only to what the time requires. Thus, although changing affairs have no fixed pattern, the statements do have constancy: one must follow the statements and assess the proper course, carrying out established rites amid the convergence and interplay of circumstances. Although the circumstances of affairs are diverse, the divination gives a single determination: one must ponder the divination and observe change, bringing transformations to completion through deliberation. This is the moment of accomplishing tasks and establishing undertakings, and so it is called action. Action concerns what divination has already determined and belongs to yin.
Ah! Although yin and yang reside within divination and action, what makes them so is the working of the numinous. How could this depend upon yin and yang? Nevertheless, this speaks only of the application of the Changes [?]. As for knowing what is to come through numinous insight and storing up what has passed through wisdom, this is the Changes within the sage’s mind. The sage embodies the subtle workings of this inner Changes in the process of manipulating milfoil stalks and seeking hexagrams, thereby guiding the people’s use of it and enabling them to share in the sage’s capacities. Is this not what makes it the numinous working unfathomable through yin and yang? How, then, should those who study the Changes proceed? Let it simply be said: the transformation and free interaction of hexagrams and lines depend upon human beings; the human capacity to apprehend them numinously and illuminate them depends upon virtue.

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
書
德懋懋官功懋懋賞用人惟己改過不吝
王崇智
同考試官訓導張　批〔題本平易作者失之補綴典實精當獨見此篇〕
考試官教諭何　批〔措語冲淡而文思自新佳作也〕
考試官教授蔣　批〔辭格嚴整程式之文也〕
大臣稱聖君有用人得其當者有處己得其當
===
者蓋用人處己難乎其盡道也聖君於此而各
得其當焉其德之足人聽聞者與昔仲虺作誥
以釋湯之慚意謂惟本於心者極其純故著於
行者盡其善彼義理充足而有可久之德人固
有懋於德者矣官之不懋非命德也王則懋之
以官尊位重祿而迪簡於王庭崇階峻級而有
服於大僚度德定位寧有不稱其德者乎勲庸
顯著而有可大之業人固有懋於功者矣賞之
不懋非報功也王則懋之以賞車服是庸而賚
punctuated:
書

德懋懋官，功懋懋賞，用人惟己，改過不吝。

王崇智

同考試官訓導張　批〔題本平易，作者失之補綴，典實精當，獨見此篇。〕
考試官教諭何　批〔措語冲淡，而文思自新，佳作也。〕
考試官教授蔣　批〔辭格嚴整，程式之文也。〕

大臣稱聖君，有用人得其當者，有處己得其當者。蓋用人處己，難乎其盡道也。聖君於此而各得其當焉，其德之足人聽聞者與！昔仲虺作誥，以釋湯之慚，意謂惟本於心者極其純，故著於行者盡其善。彼義理充足而有可久之德，人固有懋於德者矣。官之不懋，非命德也。王則懋之以官，尊位重祿而迪簡於王庭，崇階峻級而有服於大僚。度德定位，寧有不稱其德者乎？勲庸顯著而有可大之業，人固有懋於功者矣。賞之不懋，非報功也。王則懋之以賞，車服是庸而賚
translation_en:
Book of Documents

“Those eminent in virtue he encouraged with office; those eminent in achievement he encouraged with rewards. He employed others as though they were himself, and corrected his faults without reluctance.”

Wang Chongzhi

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: 〔The topic is straightforward, but writers have erred by patching material together. Only this essay displays precise and appropriate use of classical precedents.〕
Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: 〔The wording is restrained and unadorned, yet the conception is fresh. A fine work.〕
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: 〔Its diction and structure are rigorous and orderly: an essay that serves as a model.〕

A great minister praises a sage ruler for employing others appropriately and for conducting himself appropriately. For in employing others and conducting oneself, it is difficult to fulfill the Way completely. Yet the sage ruler achieves what is appropriate in each: how fully his virtue merits being heard of by others! In former times, Zhonghui composed his Announcement to dispel Tang’s shame. His meaning was that only when what is rooted in the heart is supremely pure can what manifests itself in conduct be wholly good.

There are men whose grasp of moral principles is complete and whose virtue can endure: such men are indeed eminent in virtue. To fail to encourage them with office would be to fail to appoint men according to their virtue. The king therefore encourages them with office. With honored positions and generous stipends, they are selected for service at the royal court; with exalted ranks and lofty grades, they serve in high office. When virtue is assessed and positions assigned accordingly, could any appointment fail to match its recipient’s virtue?

There are men whose meritorious service is conspicuous and whose accomplishments can grow great: such men are indeed eminent in achievement. To fail to encourage them with rewards would be to fail to recompense achievement. The king therefore encourages them with rewards, granting carriages and ceremonial robes in recognition of their service and bestowing …

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
與之也厚土田是錫而褒寵之也隆論功行賞
寧有不稱其功者乎爵惟其德賞惟其功用人
之當如此至若善之在人固所必用矣一或忌
焉則善猶在人也惟王善不自用人之有善而
中心好之人之有技而若己有之忘私順理肯
自廣以狹人耶過之在己固所當改矣一或吝
焉則過猶在我也惟王過不憚改悔悟之深惟
恐其留滯也懲創之至惟恐其潛滋也以公滅
私肯恥過以作非耶善無不容過無不改處己
===
之當如此是則處人己而各得其當非純乎天
德者不能也其君天下也夫何慚之有哉大抵
人君一心萬化之原苟心有未純固無以為處
事之地用人處己之間必至於顛倒眩瞀其害
有不可勝言者矣湯於聲色貨利之私一切屏
之而不邇不殖宜其用人處己而各得其當如
此也卒之兆民彰信而延商家六百年之命脉
者孰謂無所自耶
時人斯其惟皇之極
punctuated:
與之也厚，土田是錫，而褒寵之也隆。論功行賞，寧有不稱其功者乎？爵惟其德，賞惟其功，用人之當如此。至若善之在人，固所必用矣；一或忌焉，則善猶在人也。惟王善不自用，人之有善而中心好之，人之有技而若己有之，忘私順理，肯自廣以狹人耶？過之在己，固所當改矣；一或吝焉，則過猶在我也。惟王過不憚改，悔悟之深，惟恐其留滯也；懲創之至，惟恐其潛滋也。以公滅私，肯恥過以作非耶？善無不容，過無不改，處己之當如此。是則處人己而各得其當，非純乎天德者不能也。其君天下也，夫何慚之有哉？大抵人君一心，萬化之原。苟心有未純，固無以為處事之地；用人處己之間，必至於顛倒眩瞀，其害有不可勝言者矣。湯於聲色貨利之私，一切屏之，而不邇不殖，宜其用人處己而各得其當如此也。卒之兆民彰信，而延商家六百年之命脉者，孰謂無所自耶？

時人斯其惟皇之極。
translation_en:
…bestowing generously upon them; he grants them lands and fields, lavishing honor and favor upon them. When he assesses achievements and distributes rewards, could any reward fail to match the achievement? Rank is granted solely according to virtue, and rewards solely according to merit. Such is his appropriateness in employing others.

As for the goodness found in others, it certainly ought to be put to use. Yet if one feels any jealousy of it, that goodness remains theirs alone. Only the king, possessing goodness, does not rely solely on himself: when others possess goodness, he loves it from his heart; when others possess a skill, it is as though he possessed it himself. Forgetting selfish concerns and following moral principle, would he aggrandize himself by belittling others? As for faults in oneself, they certainly ought to be corrected. Yet if one is at all reluctant to relinquish them, those faults remain within oneself. Only the king does not shrink from correcting his faults. So profound is his remorse and awakening that he fears only that his faults may linger; so thorough is his resolve to take warning and reform that he fears only that they may secretly grow. Eliminating selfishness through public-mindedness, would he let shame over a fault lead him into further wrongdoing? He embraces every goodness and corrects every fault. Such is his appropriateness in governing himself.

Thus, to deal appropriately with both others and oneself is possible only for one whose heavenly virtue is pure. In ruling all under Heaven, what could he have to be ashamed of? In general, the ruler’s single mind is the source of all transformation. If his mind lacks purity in any respect, he has no foundation for handling affairs. In employing others and governing himself, he will inevitably fall into confusion and inverted judgment, with harm beyond telling. Tang banished all selfish desires for music, sensual pleasures, wealth, and profit, neither approaching such pleasures nor amassing such wealth. It is fitting that he should have been so consistently appropriate in employing others and governing himself. In the end, the myriad people manifestly trusted him, and the lifeblood of the Shang ruling house continued for six hundred years. Who could say that this had no source?

“These people will then conform to the sovereign’s supreme standard.”

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
王化
同考試官訓導張　批〔此篇不爲惟極所窘且詞氣老健是善作者〕
考試官教諭何　批〔有條理有詞氣傑作也〕
考試官教授蔣　批〔不同衆作〕
盡被化之民有從化之速甚矣民未有導之而
不從者也皇極之民速於從化如此謂非造就
之至能若是哉昔箕子衍皇極之疇以告武王
此以造就庶民者言之意謂君民之分雖殊而
===
感應之機甚速故皇極之民方賀之可成者蒙
君念之受之而接引之也勸無小無大皆納於
甄陶之內詞色之有徵者感君錫之以福而激
勸之也至無遠無近皆入於化育之中舊染之
汙脫然以去自有以消其傾邪狹小之念己私
不復生於心也本心之善油然而生自有以趨
乎公平正大之體己私不復見於事也欣慕愛
樂有不動而化之機大而綱常倫理無不循其
天理之當然優柔厭飫有不戒以孚之妙小而
punctuated:
王化
