考試官教諭何　批〔有條理，有詞氣，傑作也。〕
考試官教授蔣　批〔不同衆作。〕

盡被化之民，有從化之速。甚矣，民未有導之而不從者也！皇極之民速於從化如此，謂非造就之至，能若是哉？昔箕子衍皇極之疇以告武王，此以造就庶民者言之。意謂君民之分雖殊，而感應之機甚速。故皇極之民，方賀之可成者，蒙君念之、受之而接引之也，勸無小無大，皆納於甄陶之內；詞色之有徵者，感君錫之以福而激勸之也，至無遠無近，皆入於化育之中。舊染之汙，脫然以去，自有以消其傾邪狹小之念，己私不復生於心也；本心之善，油然而生，自有以趨乎公平正大之體，己私不復見於事也。欣慕愛樂，有不動而化之機，大而綱常倫理，無不循其天理之當然；優柔厭飫，有不戒以孚之妙，小而
translation_en:
Wang Hua 王化

Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This essay is not constrained by the words ‘only the supreme standard.’ Its language and spirit are mature and vigorous: this is a skilled writer.”
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “Well ordered and forcefully expressed—a masterful work.”
Examiner Jiang, Director of Studies, comments: “Unlike the common run of essays.”

The people who fully receive the transforming influence are swift to follow it. How striking it is that people, once guided, never fail to follow! If the people under the August Standard respond to transformation so swiftly, could this happen without the utmost accomplishment in cultivating them? In former times, Jizi elaborated the section on the August Standard for King Wu. Here he spoke of cultivating the common people. His meaning was that, although ruler and people occupy distinct stations, the impulse of influence and response acts with great speed. Thus, among the people under the August Standard, those capable of accomplishment who are turning toward goodness [?] receive the ruler’s consideration and acceptance, by which he welcomes and guides them. Encouraged, great and small alike are all brought within his molding influence. Those whose words and expressions offer evidence of goodness are moved by the ruler’s bestowal of blessings, through which he stimulates and encourages them. They come, from far and near alike, and all enter within his transforming nurture.

The defilement of former habits falls away entirely, thereby dispelling their crooked and narrow thoughts; selfishness no longer arises in their hearts. The goodness of their original hearts wells up naturally, thereby drawing them toward an impartial, just, upright, and magnanimous disposition; selfishness no longer appears in their actions. Their glad admiration, love, and delight contain the workings of transformation without being stirred to action: in matters as great as the cardinal bonds, constant virtues, and ethical relationships, all follow what Heavenly principle properly requires. Through gentle cultivation and thorough assimilation comes the wondrous attainment of trust without admonition: in matters as small as…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
事物言動無不由乎人道之極致去其偏以復
其全君此極也民此極也舉一世而同歸皡皡
乎偏爲爾德矣豈曰保之云乎反其異而要其
同君所建也民所趨也合萬姓而一致熙熙乎
順帝之則矣豈曰近之云乎是則民不同也而
所同者心心不同也而所同者理此民之趨極
自有不容已者矣人君可不知所以盡造就之
道也哉雖然君身者天下之本身不正則極不
建而感化之機息矣故舜之執中湯之建中武
===
之建極其義一也後世之君興學設教亦皆有
政卒未見其成教化之功者無本故爾故箕子
衍皇極首言君當作極以端其本而後及其造
就人才之道本末先後自不可誣矣治天下之
法要不外是
詩
淑人君子其帶伊絲其帶伊絲其弁伊騏
胡偉
同考試官教諭高　批〔此題舊以德稱其服□□〕
punctuated:
事物言動，無不由乎人道之極致。去其偏以復其全，君此極也，民此極也，舉一世而同歸，皡皡乎偏爲爾德矣，豈曰保之云乎？反其異而要其同，君所建也，民所趨也，合萬姓而一致，熙熙乎順帝之則矣，豈曰近之云乎？是則民不同也，而所同者心；心不同也，而所同者理。此民之趨極，自有不容已者矣。人君可不知所以盡造就之道也哉？雖然，君身者天下之本，身不正則極不建，而感化之機息矣。故舜之執中、湯之建中、武之建極，其義一也。後世之君，興學設教，亦皆有政，卒未見其成教化之功者，無本故爾。故箕子衍皇極，首言君當作極以端其本，而後及其造就人才之道，本末先後，自不可誣矣。治天下之法，要不外是。
詩
淑人君子，其帶伊絲；其帶伊絲，其弁伊騏。
胡偉
同考試官教諭高批〔此題舊以德稱其服□□〕
translation_en:
…in their dealings with things, their speech, and their actions, all follow the highest perfection of the human Way. Removing their partiality to restore their wholeness, ruler and people alike take this as their ultimate standard. The entire age returns together to it, vast and harmonious, making your virtue prevail everywhere [?]. Could this be described merely as preserving that standard? Reversing their divergences and seeking their common ground, the ruler establishes what the people strive toward. The myriad families unite in a single purpose, joyfully following the Lord on High’s rule. Could this be described merely as drawing near? Thus, although the people differ, what they share is the heart; although their hearts differ, what they share is principle. There is, then, something in the people’s movement toward the ultimate standard that cannot be restrained. Can the ruler fail to understand how to fulfill the work of nurturing them?
Nevertheless, the ruler’s own person is the foundation of all under Heaven. If his person is not upright, the ultimate standard is not established, and the workings of moral influence cease. Thus Shun’s holding fast to the Mean, Tang’s establishing the Mean, and King Wu’s establishing the ultimate standard all have the same meaning. Rulers of later ages also adopted policies to promote schools and establish instruction. That they ultimately failed to accomplish moral transformation through teaching was simply because they lacked this foundation. Hence, when Jizi expounded the Royal Ultimate, he first said that the ruler must serve as the ultimate standard, thereby setting the foundation right, and only afterward addressed the means of nurturing talented people. The distinction between root and branches, and their proper sequence, cannot be gainsaid. The essentials of governing all under Heaven extend no further than this.
Book of Odes
“The good man, the gentleman—his girdle is of silk. His girdle is of silk; his cap is patterned like a piebald horse.”
Hu Wei
Comment by Associate Examiner Gao, Instructor: “Previously, this topic has been interpreted as virtue being commensurate with the clothing □□…”

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
殊失本旨此篇體認明白詞氣亦足以發宜
在高等
同考試官學正越　批　國風題本難發明能
作如此亦不凡矣
同考試官教授汪　批　七篇皆明爽可愛真
作手也
考試官教諭何　批　發揮傳意明白
考試官教授將　批　得旨
詩人美君子必表其所服之有常焉夫儀莫難
===
於不忒也君子之服飾有常度焉心之專一可
見矣詩人得不深美之哉鳲鳩之詩美君子用
心均平專一而作也至此謂夫威儀固心德之
所形服飾亢威儀之所係彼淑人君子其心如結
而善已造於可欲之境其德不爽而名無愧於
君子之稱則其威儀之著寧不符其中之所存
哉自其服飾言之孰於身者帶也帶固有常制
矣心不一者或未免於有差我君子衣服有常
而其帶則伊絲焉縞素為質而渾然純朴之內
punctuated:
殊失本旨，此篇體認明白，詞氣亦足以發，宜在高等。
同考試官學正越批：國風題本難發明，能作如此，亦不凡矣。
同考試官教授汪批：七篇皆明爽可愛，真作手也。
考試官教諭何批：發揮傳意明白。
考試官教授將批：得旨。
詩人美君子，必表其所服之有常焉。夫儀莫難於不忒也。君子之服飾有常度焉，心之專一可見矣，詩人得不深美之哉？《鳲鳩》之詩，美君子用心均平專一而作也。至此，謂夫威儀固心德之所形，服飾亢威儀之所係。彼淑人君子，其心如結，而善已造於可欲之境；其德不爽，而名無愧於君子之稱。則其威儀之著，寧不符其中之所存哉？自其服飾言之，孰於身者，帶也。帶固有常制矣，心不一者，或未免於有差。我君子衣服有常，而其帶則伊絲焉。縞素為質，而渾然純朴之內
translation_en:
…greatly misses the original purport. This essay apprehends it clearly, and its language and vigor suffice to bring it out. It deserves a high ranking.
Associate Examiner Yue, Instructor (xuezheng), comments: Topics from the Airs of the States are inherently difficult to elucidate. To write like this is no ordinary accomplishment.
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor (jiaoshou), comments: All seven essays are clear, lucid, and pleasing. Truly an accomplished writer.
Examiner He, Instructor (jiaoyu), comments: Clearly develops the meaning of the commentary.
Examiner Jiang [?], Instructor (jiaoshou), comments: Grasps the purport.
When the poet praises the gentleman, he invariably draws attention to the constancy of his attire. In deportment, nothing is harder than remaining free from error. The gentleman’s clothing and ornaments follow constant standards, making visible the single-mindedness of his heart. How could the poet fail to praise him deeply? The poem “The Cuckoo” (Shijiu) was composed to praise the gentleman’s even-handedness and single-mindedness. At this point it means that dignified deportment is indeed the outward manifestation of the heart’s virtue, while clothing and ornaments are what that deportment depends upon [?]. That good man, that gentleman: his heart is as firmly bound as a knot, and his goodness has already attained the condition of being worthy of desire; his virtue is without fault, and his reputation is worthy of the designation “gentleman.” How, then, could his outward deportment fail to accord with what he holds within? Speaking of his attire, what is fastened about his body [?] is the sash. The sash certainly has an established form, yet those whose hearts lack unity may not escape deviations. Our gentleman is constant in his attire, and his sash is of silk. Plain white silk forms its substance, and within its wholly unadorned simplicity…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
存玄華為飾而燦然文采之外見等威以辨而
冉之於身者有章焉戴於首者弁也弁固有常
度矣心之不專者或不免於有忒我君子其帶
伊絲而其弁則伊騏焉其製以皮雖美而得中
正之宜其色青黑雖華而無靡麗之飾禮制以
嚴而頍然於首者可觀焉戴斯弁也則束斯帶
矣常度不失而足以表儀乎朝著孰謂非其心
之所形哉服此帶也則冠此弁矣儀度有常而
足以起敬於觀瞻孰謂非其德之所見哉吁以
===
專一之心著而為不忒之儀如此詩人以以正是
四國稱之豈溢美哉嗟夫衣服身章也君子每
於此乎觀德焉故頌周公者以赤舄為言記孔
子者備衣服之制蓋服之不衷身之災也彼有
聚鷸冠備赤芾者亦獨何哉鳲鳩君子其亦聖
賢之徒矣惜其姓名不傳徒仰高風於千載之
下
明昭有周式序在位
尹寵
punctuated:
存，玄華為飾，而燦然文采之外見。等威以辨，而冉之於身者有章焉。戴於首者弁也，弁固有常度矣。心之不專者，或不免於有忒。我君子其帶伊絲，而其弁則伊騏焉。其製以皮，雖美而得中正之宜；其色青黑，雖華而無靡麗之飾。禮制以嚴，而頍然於首者可觀焉。戴斯弁也，則束斯帶矣，常度不失，而足以表儀乎朝著，孰謂非其心之所形哉？服此帶也，則冠此弁矣，儀度有常，而足以起敬於觀瞻，孰謂非其德之所見哉？吁！以專一之心，著而為不忒之儀如此，詩人以「以正是四國」稱之，豈溢美哉？嗟夫！衣服，身章也，君子每於此乎觀德焉。故頌周公者以赤舄為言，記孔子者備衣服之制。蓋服之不衷，身之災也。彼有聚鷸冠、備赤芾者，亦獨何哉？鳲鳩君子，其亦聖賢之徒矣。惜其姓名不傳，徒仰高風於千載之下。
明昭有周，式序在位。
尹寵。
translation_en:
…resides within; dark ornamentation supplies the decoration, and brilliant patterned beauty appears without. Distinctions of rank and dignity are made clear, and what is worn upon the body [?] displays an ordered pattern. What is worn upon the head is the ceremonial cap, and the cap assuredly has its prescribed dimensions. Those whose hearts lack single-mindedness may fail to avoid deviations. Our gentleman’s belt is of silk, and his cap is dark-patterned. Made of hide, it is beautiful yet accords with what is fitting and correct; blue-black in color, it is splendid yet has no extravagantly gorgeous ornament. The ritual regulations are strictly observed, and the cap standing prominently upon his head is worthy of admiration. When he wears this cap, he fastens this belt. Never departing from the prescribed standards, he is fit to serve as a model at court: who could say that this is not the outward expression of his heart? When he wears this belt, he dons this cap. Constant in his dignified bearing, he inspires reverence in those who behold him: who could say that this is not the manifestation of his virtue? Ah! His single-minded heart manifests itself in such faultless deportment. When the poet praises him with the words, “Thereby he sets right these four quarters,” could this be excessive praise? Alas! Clothing is the body's outward distinction, and gentlemen regularly discern virtue through it. Thus those who praised the Duke of Zhou spoke of his red shoes, and those who recorded Confucius’s conduct gave a full account of the rules governing his clothing. For clothing that does not accord with what is fitting brings calamity upon its wearer. What, then, of those who assemble kingfisher feathers for their caps or furnish themselves with red knee-aprons? The gentleman of “The Cuckoo” must likewise have belonged among the sages and worthies. It is regrettable that his name has not been transmitted; a thousand years later, we can only look up to his lofty example.
“Brilliantly illustrious is Zhou; in due order it arranges those in office.”
Yin Chong.

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭髙　批〔巡狩黜陟典禮讀詩者多不考能舉其要而言之足見好古之學〕
同考試官學正越　批〔作典禮文字須雅重詳盡此作得之〕
同考試官教授汪　批〔寫當時式序氣象如在目前〕
考試官教諭何　批〔得周王巡狩之意〕
考試官教授蔣　批〔明贍可取〕
周人美當代之盛公黜陟之典甚矣一代之興
===
不偶然也周王巡狩之初而首舉黜陟之典焉
其永保天命也宜哉此巡狩而朝會祭告之樂
歌也至此若曰維我武王繼夏商之統君天下
之大誕膺景命而天眷於是乎方隆允陟元后
而天下於是乎大定殲濁之政既除而風氣為
之開明四海永清煥乎成功之光顯也維新之
化大布而人文以之宣朗土宇昄章赫乎治勢
之昭明也夫以一代更化之初正人心攷觀之
際武王寧不有以吞其望哉誠以天下諸侯固
punctuated:
同考試官教諭髙，批〔巡狩黜陟典禮，讀詩者多不考，能舉其要而言之，足見好古之學。〕
同考試官學正越，批〔作典禮文字，須雅重詳盡，此作得之。〕
同考試官教授汪，批〔寫當時式序氣象，如在目前。〕
考試官教諭何，批〔得周王巡狩之意。〕
考試官教授蔣，批〔明贍可取。〕
周人美當代之盛，公黜陟之典。甚矣，一代之興不偶然也！周王巡狩之初，而首舉黜陟之典焉，其永保天命也宜哉！此巡狩而朝會祭告之樂歌也。至此若曰：「維我武王，繼夏商之統，君天下之大，誕膺景命，而天眷於是乎方隆；允陟元后，而天下於是乎大定。殲濁之政既除，而風氣為之開明，四海永清，煥乎成功之光顯也；維新之化大布，而人文以之宣朗，土宇昄章，赫乎治勢之昭明也。夫以一代更化之初，正人心攷觀之際，武王寧不有以吞其望哉？誠以天下諸侯固
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: “Readers of the Odes often fail to investigate the prescribed rites and procedures for royal inspection tours and the demotion and promotion of officials. The ability to identify their essentials and discuss them adequately demonstrates a scholarly devotion to antiquity.”
Associate Examiner Yue, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Writing about prescribed rites and procedures must be refined, dignified, detailed, and comprehensive. This composition achieves these qualities.”
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “It depicts the circumstances of ordering those in office at that time as though they were before our eyes.”
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “It captures the intent of the Zhou king’s inspection tours.”
Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “Clear and rich in content; worthy of selection.”
The people of Zhou praised the flourishing state of their age and the impartial administration of demotion and promotion. How profoundly this shows that the rise of a dynasty is no accident! At the outset of his inspection tour, the king of Zhou gave first priority to the prescribed procedures for demotion and promotion. How fitting that he should preserve Heaven’s Mandate forever! This is a ceremonial song for court assemblies and sacrificial announcements during an inspection tour. At this point it is as though it says: “Our King Wu succeeded to the line of Xia and Shang and ruled the vast realm. He received the great Mandate, and Heaven’s favor thereupon grew abundant. He duly ascended as sovereign, and all under Heaven thereupon attained great stability. Once the corrupt administration [?] had been abolished, prevailing customs became enlightened; all within the Four Seas was forever purified. Resplendent was the manifest glory of his achievement! The transforming influence of renewal spread widely, and human culture thereby shone forth. The realm was vast and illustrious: brilliant was the radiance of its well-ordered government! At the beginning of a dynasty’s renewal of governance, precisely when people were scrutinizing and observing it, could King Wu have failed to find a way to fulfill their expectations [?]? For among the feudal lords of the realm there certainly …

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
有懋德者矣而不順者不能無也淑慝不分何
以徵有位乎於是振威福之權而式序之焉庶
邦冢君固有懋功者矣而不敬者未必無也賢
否不別何以勵臣工乎於是舉賞罰之典而明
試之焉有功者進有德者陟於是乎慶之而加
地進律之賞行矣衰對之際孰不知所勸耶怠
事者黜犯禮者退於是乎讓之而貶爵削地之
罰舉矣薄震之餘孰不知所畏耶吁舉廢墜之
大典警久玩之人心武王保天命之道孰有加於
===
是哉抑嘗考之虞周巡狩黜陟之典雖詳略不
同然其賞罰明信所以綱維天下控御諸侯使
人人力於事功以求庶績咸熙之意則無不同
此固萬世保天下之要道也後世考課之法雖
源於此要之無聖人之公甚者或以好惡參之
又何怪乎予奪不明治功不古若哉可慨也夫
春秋
冬公次于滑〔莊公三年〕
邢淳
punctuated:
有懋德者矣，而不順者不能無也。淑慝不分，何以徵有位乎？於是振威福之權，而式序之焉。庶邦冢君固有懋功者矣，而不敬者未必無也。賢否不別，何以勵臣工乎？於是舉賞罰之典，而明試之焉。有功者進，有德者陟，於是乎慶之，而加地進律之賞行矣。衰對之際，孰不知所勸耶？怠事者黜，犯禮者退，於是乎讓之，而貶爵削地之罰舉矣。薄震之餘，孰不知所畏耶？吁！舉廢墜之大典，警久玩之人心，武王保天命之道，孰有加於是哉？抑嘗考之，虞周巡狩黜陟之典，雖詳略不同，然其賞罰明信，所以綱維天下，控御諸侯，使人人力於事功，以求庶績咸熙之意，則無不同。此固萬世保天下之要道也。後世考課之法雖源於此，要之無聖人之公，甚者或以好惡參之，又何怪乎予奪不明，治功不古若哉？可慨也夫！

春秋

冬，公次于滑。〔莊公三年〕

邢淳
translation_en:
…there were those who diligently cultivated virtue, yet there could not fail to be some who were disobedient. Unless the good and the wicked were distinguished, how could those holding office be assessed? Thus he exercised his authority to punish and reward, bringing them into due order. Among the rulers of the various states there were certainly those who diligently pursued meritorious service, yet there might also be some who lacked reverence. Unless the worthy and the unworthy were distinguished, how could his servants be spurred to exertion? Thus he applied the established rules of reward and punishment and clearly tested their performance. Those with achievements were advanced, and those with virtue were promoted. He thereupon rewarded them, granting additional territory and higher ceremonial standing. On the occasion of their audience [?], who would not know what to strive for? Those who neglected their duties were dismissed, and those who violated ritual propriety were demoted. He thereupon censured them, imposing reductions in rank and territory. After this display of awe-inspiring authority, who would not know what to fear? Ah! He restored great institutions that had fallen into disuse and roused minds long accustomed to heedlessness. What could surpass this way by which King Wu preserved Heaven’s Mandate?

I have also examined the institutions governing inspection tours, dismissals, and promotions under Shun and the Zhou. Although they differed in the fullness of their provisions, their rewards and punishments were alike clear and trustworthy. Their purpose was the same: to hold the realm together, keep the feudal lords under control, and make everyone exert himself in service so that all undertakings might flourish. This is indeed the essential way to preserve the realm for all ages. Although later methods of evaluating officials originated here, they ultimately lacked the impartiality of the sages; in worse cases, personal likes and dislikes were allowed to intrude. Why, then, be surprised that rewards and deprivations were improperly assigned and that achievements in government fell short of those of antiquity? How lamentable!

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In winter, the duke encamped at Hua.” 〔Third year of Duke Zhuang〕

Xing Chun

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導余　批〔題本平易作者頗多陳腐可厭惟此篇文健辭新寫出一舉兩善之〕
〔意宜冠本房〕
考試官教諭何　批〔說出聖人汲汲恤患復〕
〔讎之情真佳作也〕
考試官教授蔣　批〔胡傳意正如此作〕
國君見義而怠於有為春秋所以譏之也蓋恤
患復讎天下之大義也魯君有見於此而為之
不果春秋得不深譏之哉慨昔齊襄恃强而并
===
紀我莊承告以興師是亦天下之義舉也而春
秋書次以譏之何哉誠以魯之於紀有婚姻之
好者也公誠念患在倒懸之急則纓冠往救此
其時也尚何計其後乎魯之於齊有君父之讎
者也公誠知不共戴天之義則枕戈待旦此其
日也又遑恤其他乎況斯時也紀聞我之救至
則死守之心益堅併謀協力安知不遂却齊師
而存紀之祀邪齊聞我之義舉則貪暴之心自
沮志隳氣餒安知不遂為魯屈而雪我之耻邪
punctuated:
同考試官訓導余，批〔題本平易，作者頗多陳腐可厭，惟此篇文健辭新，寫出一舉兩善之〕〔意，宜冠本房。〕
考試官教諭何，批〔說出聖人汲汲恤患復〕〔讎之情，真佳作也。〕
考試官教授蔣，批〔胡傳意正如此作。〕
國君見義而怠於有為，春秋所以譏之也。蓋恤患復讎，天下之大義也。魯君有見於此而為之不果，春秋得不深譏之哉？慨昔齊襄恃强而并紀，我莊承告以興師，是亦天下之義舉也。而春秋書次以譏之，何哉？誠以魯之於紀，有婚姻之好者也。公誠念患在倒懸之急，則纓冠往救，此其時也，尚何計其後乎？魯之於齊，有君父之讎者也。公誠知不共戴天之義，則枕戈待旦，此其日也，又遑恤其他乎？況斯時也，紀聞我之救至，則死守之心益堅，併謀協力，安知不遂却齊師而存紀之祀邪？齊聞我之義舉，則貪暴之心自沮，志隳氣餒，安知不遂為魯屈而雪我之耻邪？
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The topic itself is straightforward, and many writers have produced stale and tiresome treatments. This essay alone has vigorous prose and fresh diction, bringing out the idea of accomplishing two worthy ends through a single undertaking. It should rank first in this examining section.”
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “It expresses the Sage’s urgent concern to relieve distress and avenge a wrong. Truly an excellent composition.”
Examiner Jiang, Professor, comments: “The meaning of Hu’s Commentary is precisely as this essay presents it.”
When a ruler recognizes what is right but is remiss in acting upon it, the Spring and Autumn Annals censures him for this. Relieving distress and avenging wrongs are great obligations binding upon all under Heaven. If the ruler of Lu recognized this but failed to carry his action through, could the Spring and Autumn Annals refrain from censuring him severely?
Alas, formerly Duke Xiang of Qi relied upon his strength to annex Ji. Our Duke Zhuang received an appeal and raised an army: this, too, was a righteous undertaking under Heaven. Yet the Spring and Autumn Annals records that he “halted,” thereby censuring him. Why? Lu and Ji were bound by ties of marriage. Had the duke truly considered that Ji’s distress was as urgent as that of someone hanging upside down, this was the moment to tie on his cap and rush to its rescue. Why still calculate the consequences? As for Lu’s relations with Qi, there was the wrong done to its ruler and the duke’s father to avenge. Had the duke truly understood the obligation not to share the same Heaven with such an enemy, this was the day to sleep with his spear for a pillow, awaiting dawn. How could he have had leisure to worry about anything else?
Moreover, at that moment, had Ji heard that our relief forces were arriving, its resolve to defend itself to the death would have become still firmer. By combining plans and joining forces, might they not have driven back Qi’s army and preserved Ji’s ancestral sacrifices? Had Qi heard of our righteous undertaking, its appetite for violent conquest would naturally have been checked, its resolve broken and its spirit weakened. Might it not then have yielded to Lu, allowing us to wipe away our disgrace?

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
奈何信義不篤徉為救患之虚聲而陰有自全
之詭計假鄭為辭至滑而止遂使堂堂之陣變
而為退縮之兵矣為義不終外竊赴急之虚名
而内畏大敵之難究託人自解及鄭而留遂使
正正之旗轉而為逍遥之師矣彼千里伐戎以
恤燕齊僕亦人耳可以魯之於紀而不念於此
乎三國遷蔡以復讎楚子亦人耳可以魯之於
齊而不競於此乎經故書次以譏之聖人垂教
之意遠矣自是而後紀遂大去其國未必非魯
===
驕齊之志而益其暴也盖莊公於君父之讎尚
且忘之况於紀乎使其能以復讎為心則必舉
國以戰戰雖不勝而此心亦自白於天下况諸
侯之中豈無聞義而起者而未必不勝邪奈何
其私勝公微而不克自振也豈非無浩然之氣
者乎
滕子來朝〔桓公二年〕杞子來朝〔僖公二十有七年〕
劉朝卿
同考試官訓導余 批 春秋大義數十此題二義
punctuated:
奈何信義不篤，徉為救患之虚聲，而陰有自全之詭計，假鄭為辭，至滑而止，遂使堂堂之陣變而為退縮之兵矣！為義不終，外竊赴急之虚名，而内畏大敵之難究，託人自解，及鄭而留，遂使正正之旗轉而為逍遥之師矣！彼千里伐戎以恤燕，齊僕亦人耳，可以魯之於紀而不念於此乎？三國遷蔡以復讎，楚子亦人耳，可以魯之於齊而不競於此乎？經故書次以譏之，聖人垂教之意遠矣！自是而後，紀遂大去其國，未必非魯驕齊之志而益其暴也。盖莊公於君父之讎尚且忘之，况於紀乎？使其能以復讎為心，則必舉國以戰，戰雖不勝，而此心亦自白於天下；况諸侯之中，豈無聞義而起者，而未必不勝邪？奈何其私勝公微，而不克自振也？豈非無浩然之氣者乎？

滕子來朝〔桓公二年〕，杞子來朝〔僖公二十有七年〕。
劉朝卿

同考試官訓導余批：春秋大義數十，此題二義
translation_en:
Why, then, was he so lacking in good faith and righteousness? He made a false show of relieving distress while secretly devising a scheme to preserve himself. Using Zheng as his excuse, he stopped upon reaching Hua, thus turning his imposing battle formations into retreating troops! He failed to carry his righteous undertaking through: outwardly he appropriated the empty reputation of hastening to another’s aid, while inwardly fearing the difficulty of dealing fully with a powerful enemy [?]. Invoking others to excuse himself, he halted on reaching Zheng, thus turning his orderly banners into an army idling at ease!

That Qi Pu [?], who marched a thousand li against the Rong to relieve Yan, was merely a man like any other. Given Lu’s relationship with Ji, could its ruler fail to take this example to heart? The ruler of Chu, too, who moved Cai to avenge an injury involving three states [?], was merely a man like any other. Given Lu’s relationship with Qi, could its ruler fail to strive to match this example? The Classic therefore records that he “encamped,” in order to censure him. Profound indeed was the sage’s intention in transmitting this lesson!

After this, the ruler of Ji finally abandoned his state altogether. This may well have been because Lu encouraged Qi’s arrogance and intensified its violence. Indeed, Duke Zhuang had forgotten even the obligation to avenge his ruler and father; how much less would he care about Ji? Had he set his heart on vengeance, he would surely have mobilized the entire state for war. Even if he had failed to win, his purpose would thereby have been made plain to all under Heaven. Moreover, could there have been no other feudal lords who would rise upon hearing of his righteous cause? Victory might well have been possible. Why did his private interests prevail and his public duty grow faint, leaving him unable to rouse himself? Was he not a man lacking the vast, overflowing vital force of righteousness?

“The Viscount of Teng came to pay court.” 〔Second year of Duke Huan.〕 “The Viscount of Qi came to pay court.” 〔Twenty-seventh year of Duke Xi.〕
Liu Chaoqing

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor: “The Spring and Autumn Annals contains several dozen great principles. This topic involves two principles…”

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
具馬作者不冗則悔反戾經旨求其據案斷罪
使大義煥然復明無踰此篇
考試官教諭何　批　深得謹嚴之旨
考試官教授蔣　批　雄健可録
脩禮而昧大倫者春秋既重其貶脩禮而紊大
防者春秋亦重其貶此可見春秋之法嚴於治
亂賊之黨而謹華夷之辨也且滕本侯爵經於
朝桓而稱子者何哉誠以君臣者天下之大倫
况爲諸侯而可以昧之乎彼桓公與聞鍾巫之
===
故天理所不容王法所不赦者滕嘗脩好於隱
公既不能申先發後聞之義舉聲罪致討之師
惟斷絶朝聘以自别於亂賊亦不失爲正道也
夫何膏車秣馬奔趨於鄰國之先捧帛執玉朝
覲於嗣服之始王法不之畏也天倫不之恤也
噫諸侯與之會盟者尚加貶以著罪况行朝禮
者乎三綱由是而淪九法由是而斁滕君黨惡
之罪不容誅矣是故降而稱子比諸夷狄何其
惡之深乎盖春秋爲誅亂討賊而作其法尤嚴
punctuated:
具馬，作者不冗則悔，反戾經旨。求其據案斷罪，使大義煥然復明，無踰此篇。
考試官教諭何批：深得謹嚴之旨。
考試官教授蔣批：雄健可録。
脩禮而昧大倫者，《春秋》既重其貶；脩禮而紊大防者，《春秋》亦重其貶。此可見《春秋》之法，嚴於治亂賊之黨，而謹華夷之辨也。且滕本侯爵，經於朝桓而稱子者，何哉？誠以君臣者，天下之大倫，况爲諸侯而可以昧之乎？彼桓公與聞鍾巫之故，天理所不容，王法所不赦者。滕嘗脩好於隱公，既不能申先發後聞之義，舉聲罪致討之師，惟斷絶朝聘，以自别於亂賊，亦不失爲正道也。夫何膏車秣馬，奔趨於鄰國之先；捧帛執玉，朝覲於嗣服之始？王法不之畏也，天倫不之恤也。噫！諸侯與之會盟者，尚加貶以著罪，况行朝禮者乎？三綱由是而淪，九法由是而斁，滕君黨惡之罪不容誅矣。是故降而稱子，比諸夷狄，何其惡之深乎！盖《春秋》爲誅亂討賊而作，其法尤嚴
translation_en:
…both are present [?]. Writers are either prolix or obscure [?], running counter to the purport of the Classic. For weighing the evidence and determining guilt, thereby making the great principles shine clearly once again, nothing surpasses this essay.
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “It grasps profoundly the purport of meticulousness and severity.”
Examiner Jiang, Professor, comments: “Forceful and vigorous; worthy of inclusion.”
Those who observe ritual but disregard the great human relationships are sternly degraded in the Spring and Autumn Annals; those who observe ritual but confound the great boundary are likewise sternly degraded. This shows that the law of the Spring and Autumn Annals is severe in punishing the accomplices of rebels and traitors, and scrupulous in distinguishing the Chinese from the barbarians. Now Teng originally held the rank of marquis. Why does the Classic call its ruler a viscount when he pays court to Duke Huan? Truly, the relationship between ruler and minister is one of the great relationships under Heaven. How, then, could a ruler of a domain disregard it? Duke Huan was privy to the affair at Zhongwu—something that Heaven’s principles could not tolerate and royal law could not pardon. Teng had previously maintained friendly relations with Duke Yin. Even if he could not uphold the principle of taking action first and reporting afterward, raising an army to proclaim the offender’s crimes and punish him, merely severing court visits and diplomatic missions to distinguish himself from rebels and traitors would still have accorded with the proper way. Why, then, did he grease his carriage and feed his horses, hastening there ahead of the neighboring states, bearing silk and holding jade to pay court at the very beginning of the new ruler’s succession? He had no fear of royal law and no concern for Heaven’s ordained relationships. Alas! Even the rulers who met and covenanted with Duke Huan were degraded to expose their guilt; how much more so one who performed the rites of paying court! Through this, the Three Bonds sank into ruin and the nine norms fell into decay. The ruler of Teng’s guilt in siding with evil exceeded what execution could requite. Thus he was demoted and called a viscount, ranked alongside the barbarians: how profound was the abhorrence of him! For the Spring and Autumn Annals was composed to punish rebels and chastise traitors, and its law is especially severe…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
於亂賊之黨使人人知亂賊之爲大惡而莫之
與則亂賊之黨孤而悖逆之禍止矣大倫不以
正乎乃若杞本伯爵經於朝僖而稱子者何哉
蓋以華夷者天下之大防况爲諸侯而可以紊
之乎彼東夷僻處荒服之外正朔所不加禮教
所不及者杞則迫近於其國既不能用我衣冠
禮樂之風變彼被髪左衽之俗惟謹守王度以
自別於夷狄亦不失爲賢君也夫何禮儀辭命
皆法外夷之規模器具文物盡棄先王之制度
===
不覺自變於夷也不知自反於夏也意諸侯與
之會盟者尚特書以致謹况用夷禮者乎中國
胥爲夷狄人類化爲禽獸杞君用夷之罪不可
逭矣是故降而稱子視諸夷狄何其待之嚴乎
蓋春秋爲攘夷尊周而作也尤惡夫用夷之禮
使人人知用夷之爲大罪而莫之敢則夷狄之
勢亦孤而猾夏之禍止矣大防不以正乎噫一
字之貶嚴於斧鉞而君臣夷夏之分可以明於
萬世春秋之作豈小補哉抑非天子不制度不
punctuated: 於亂賊之黨。使人人知亂賊之爲大惡而莫之與，則亂賊之黨孤，而悖逆之禍止矣，大倫不以正乎？乃若杞本伯爵，經於朝僖而稱子者，何哉？蓋以華夷者，天下之大防，况爲諸侯而可以紊之乎？彼東夷僻處荒服之外，正朔所不加，禮教所不及者。杞則迫近於其國，既不能用我衣冠禮樂之風，變彼被髪左衽之俗，惟謹守王度，以自別於夷狄，亦不失爲賢君也。夫何禮儀辭命皆法外夷之規模，器具文物盡棄先王之制度？不覺自變於夷也，不知自反於夏也。意，諸侯與之會盟者，尚特書以致謹，况用夷禮者乎？中國胥爲夷狄，人類化爲禽獸，杞君用夷之罪不可逭矣。是故降而稱子，視諸夷狄，何其待之嚴乎！蓋春秋爲攘夷尊周而作也，尤惡夫用夷之禮。使人人知用夷之爲大罪而莫之敢，則夷狄之勢亦孤，而猾夏之禍止矣，大防不以正乎？噫！一字之貶，嚴於斧鉞，而君臣夷夏之分可以明於萬世，春秋之作豈小補哉？抑非天子不制度，不
translation_en:
…toward the accomplices of rebels and traitors. If everyone understands that rebellion and treason are great evils and refuses to support them, rebels and traitors will be isolated, and the calamity of insubordination will cease. Would not the cardinal relationships thereby be set right?

Now Qi originally held the rank of earl. Why, then, does the Classic call its ruler a viscount when recording his court visit to Duke Xi? The distinction between the Chinese and the barbarians is a great boundary under Heaven. How could a ruler of a state be permitted to confound it? Those eastern barbarians dwell remotely beyond the outermost zone of submission, where the royal calendar does not apply and ritual instruction does not reach. Qi lies close to their territory. Even if its ruler could not use our traditions of proper dress, ritual, and music to transform their customs of wearing their hair loose and fastening their garments on the left, he could still have been a worthy ruler simply by scrupulously observing royal standards and thereby distinguishing himself from the barbarians. Why, then, did his ceremonies and diplomatic language all imitate foreign barbarian patterns, while his implements and cultural forms entirely abandoned the institutions of the former kings? He unwittingly transformed himself into a barbarian and did not know to return to Chinese ways. Ah[?], even meetings and covenants between the lords and barbarians receive explicit mention to enforce caution; how much more serious is adopting barbarian rites! The central states would all become barbarian, and humankind would turn into birds and beasts. The ruler of Qi cannot escape punishment for his crime of adopting barbarian practices. Thus he is demoted and called a viscount, treated as one of the barbarians. How sternly he is dealt with!

The Spring and Autumn Annals was written to repel the barbarians and honor Zhou, and it particularly condemns the adoption of barbarian rites. If everyone understands that adopting barbarian practices is a great crime and none dares do so, barbarian power will likewise be isolated, and the calamity of their disrupting the Chinese realm will cease. Would not the great boundary thereby be set right?

Ah! Demotion by a single word is more severe than the executioner's axe, and the distinctions between ruler and subject, barbarian and Chinese, can thereby be made clear for all generations. Could the writing of the Spring and Autumn Annals have been of merely slight benefit? Yet, unless one is the Son of Heaven, one does not establish institutions, nor…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
謂禮仲尼以匹夫而專進退諸侯亂名實矣不
亦過乎殊不知世道衰微暴行交作仲尼有德
無位不得如聖世君臣用兵討賊行天子之法
於當年也故假魯史用五刑討亂賊以垂天子
之法於後世其事雖殊其理一耳不然夫子何
以曰知我者其惟春秋乎罪我者其惟春秋乎
禮記
貧者不以貨財為禮老者不以筋力為禮
王勲
同考試官教授陳　批〔此題不以字中含以𦤺〕
〔為禮之意此篇獨能發之是用錄出〕
考試官教諭何　批〔認理明透〕
考試官教授蔣　批〔典實可取〕
禮有不責人所不能辨者有不責人所不能行
者夫禮近人情也則夫貧者老者又何過責以
成其禮乎且聖人制禮固所以防範乎人而於
其行禮則未嘗厚望於人彼其家無所藏而或
不免於俯仰之累用無所給而或不免於饑寒
punctuated:
謂禮。仲尼以匹夫而專進退諸侯，亂名實矣，不亦過乎？殊不知世道衰微，暴行交作，仲尼有德無位，不得如聖世君臣用兵討賊，行天子之法於當年也。故假魯史，用五刑，討亂賊，以垂天子之法於後世。其事雖殊，其理一耳。不然，夫子何以曰：「知我者，其惟春秋乎！罪我者，其惟春秋乎！」

禮記
貧者不以貨財為禮，老者不以筋力為禮。
王勲
同考試官教授陳，批〔此題不以字中含以𦤺〕〔為禮之意此篇獨能發之是用錄出〕
考試官教諭何，批〔認理明透〕
考試官教授蔣，批〔典實可取〕

禮有不責人所不能辨者，有不責人所不能行者。夫禮近人情也，則夫貧者、老者，又何過責以成其禮乎？且聖人制禮，固所以防範乎人，而於其行禮，則未嘗厚望於人。彼其家無所藏，而或不免於俯仰之累；用無所給，而或不免於饑寒
translation_en:
…pronounce on ritual [?]. Zhongni, as a commoner, took it upon himself to advance or demote the feudal lords, thereby confusing names and realities. Was this not going too far? Such an objection entirely misses the fact that the moral order was declining and acts of violence were breaking out everywhere. Zhongni possessed virtue but held no office. He could not, like the rulers and ministers of a sagely age, deploy troops to punish rebels and enforce the Son of Heaven’s law in his own day. He therefore drew upon the historical records of Lu, employing the Five Punishments to chastise rebels and malefactors and transmit the Son of Heaven’s law to later generations. Although the actions differed, their underlying principle was the same. Otherwise, why would the Master have said, “Those who understand me will surely do so through the Spring and Autumn Annals! Those who condemn me will surely do so through the Spring and Autumn Annals!”

Record of Rites
“The poor are not required to fulfill ritual obligations through goods and wealth; the elderly are not required to fulfill ritual obligations through physical exertion.”
By Wang Xun.
Associate Examiner Chen, a Prefectural Confucian School Instructor, comments: “Within the words ‘not through’ in this topic lies the meaning of thereby bringing about the fulfillment of ritual obligations. This essay alone brings that out, and for this reason it has been selected for inclusion.”
Examiner He, a County Confucian School Instructor, comments: “His grasp of the principle is clear and penetrating.”
Examiner Jiang, a Prefectural Confucian School Instructor, comments: “Grounded in the classics and substantial; worthy of selection.”

In ritual, there are things people are not required to furnish when they lack the means [?], and things people are not required to perform when they lack the ability. Ritual accords with human feelings. Why, then, should excessive demands be placed upon the poor and the elderly in order for them to fulfill their ritual obligations? Moreover, the sages established ritual to regulate people’s conduct, yet they never imposed excessive expectations upon people in its performance. Some have nothing stored in their households and may be unable to escape the burden of supporting parents above and children below; they have nothing to meet their expenses and may be unable to escape hunger and cold…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
之憂世固有貧者矣貧而不以貨財爲禮者誠
以無財不可以爲悅而財非貧者所能辦也斟
酌於行禮之間而無拘於一定之制如禮之隆
也貨財必豐稱其家之有無雖當豐而殺也蓋
有所不計焉禮之大也貨財必奢量其財之羸
詘雖當奢而儉也蓋在所不較焉是非因其貧
而顧使失禮之中也禮主於敬心苟敬矣則儀
物不備者非禮之訾也故不責以貨財爲禮者
正所以得乎中焉所謂不責人之所不能辦者
===
如此黄耇台背而血氣之旣衰耋耄期頤而筋
力之已憊人固有老者矣老而不以筋力爲禮
者誠以非强有力者不足以行禮而力非老者
所能勉也權宜於用禮之時而不限以一定之
則如燕禮之行文固繁矣因其力之所至而坐
立之則雖曰少有所逸亦在所略焉朝禮之行
儀固備矣量其力之所能而几杖之設雖曰微
近於簡亦在所容焉是非因其老而顧使失禮
之中也禮本於敬心苟敬矣則節文不足者非
punctuated:
之憂，世固有貧者矣。貧而不以貨財爲禮者，誠以無財不可以爲悅，而財非貧者所能辦也。斟酌於行禮之間，而無拘於一定之制。如禮之隆也，貨財必豐，稱其家之有無，雖當豐而殺也，蓋有所不計焉。禮之大也，貨財必奢，量其財之羸詘，雖當奢而儉也，蓋在所不較焉。是非因其貧而顧使失禮之中也。禮主於敬，心苟敬矣，則儀物不備者，非禮之訾也。故不責以貨財爲禮者，正所以得乎中焉。所謂不責人之所不能辦者，如此。

黄耇台背，而血氣之旣衰；耋耄期頤，而筋力之已憊，人固有老者矣。老而不以筋力爲禮者，誠以非强有力者不足以行禮，而力非老者所能勉也。權宜於用禮之時，而不限以一定之則。如燕禮之行，文固繁矣，因其力之所至，而坐立之則，雖曰少有所逸，亦在所略焉。朝禮之行，儀固備矣，量其力之所能，而几杖之設，雖曰微近於簡，亦在所容焉。是非因其老而顧使失禮之中也。禮本於敬，心苟敬矣，則節文不足者，非
translation_en:
…the worry of hunger and cold: there are indeed poor people in the world. That the poor are not required to furnish goods and wealth in performing rites is truly because, although without wealth one cannot give pleasure, wealth is something the poor cannot procure. Discretion is exercised in the performance of rites, without rigid adherence to fixed prescriptions. For an elaborate rite, material offerings must be abundant; yet, taking account of what a household possesses or lacks, reducing them even where abundance is prescribed is something that may pass without scrutiny. For a great rite, material expenditure must be lavish; yet, assessing the household’s financial means, frugality even where lavishness is prescribed is something that may pass without objection. This does not mean that, because people are poor, they are thereby allowed to depart from the proper measure of ritual. Reverence governs ritual. If the heart is reverent, incomplete ceremonial provisions are no fault in the observance of ritual. Thus, not demanding goods and wealth for the performance of rites is precisely how the proper measure is attained. This is what is meant by not demanding of people what they cannot procure.

With yellowed features and mottled backs, their vital energies already declining; in advanced old age, reaching even a hundred years and requiring care, their physical strength already exhausted: there are indeed elderly people in the world. That the elderly are not required to exert physical strength in performing rites is truly because only those who are strong and vigorous can fully carry them out, while strength is something the elderly cannot force themselves to possess. Circumstances are accommodated when rites are performed, without confinement to fixed rules. For example, the ceremonial forms of the banquet rite are indeed numerous; yet the rules for sitting and standing are adjusted to what their strength permits. Even if this affords them a little ease, it is something that may be passed over. The ceremonies of court audience are indeed fully prescribed; yet, according to what their strength allows, armrests and staffs are provided. Even if this verges somewhat on informality, it is something that may be permitted. This does not mean that, because people are old, they are thereby allowed to depart from the proper measure of ritual. Reverence is the foundation of ritual. If the heart is reverent, deficiencies in ceremonial forms are not…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
禮之失也不以筋力為禮者正所以合乎中焉
所謂不責人之所不行者如此夫惟不以貨財
為禮則無財亦可以為悅而禮行於貧者矣不
以筋力為禮則無力亦可以自盡而禮行於老
者矣君子之順人情也有如是夫抑考兎首瓠
葉之微或亦可以伸敬一坐再至之節一皆所
以為禮然則貧者老者之無責於財力也宜哉
故知禮有經權以財以力者雖禮之經而不責
備於貧與老者則禮之權也經權不失其宜然
後盡乎人情而禮行於天下矣議禮者當有達
於經權之義
===
民有德而五穀昌
宋章
同考試官教授陳　批　此題有德在聖人制禮
之前未涉綱紀上說作者體認不真率多一
槩牽搭甚以作舉之疵十日之際庶本旨此篇
詞氣舂容而理亦不失是宜錄之
考試官教諭何　批　文理醇正非衆作可及
punctuated:
禮之失也。不以筋力為禮者，正所以合乎中焉。所謂不責人之所不行者，如此。夫惟不以貨財為禮，則無財亦可以為悅，而禮行於貧者矣；不以筋力為禮，則無力亦可以自盡，而禮行於老者矣。君子之順人情也，有如是夫！抑考兎首瓠葉之微，或亦可以伸敬；一坐再至之節，一皆所以為禮。然則貧者老者之無責於財力也，宜哉！故知禮有經權：以財以力者，雖禮之經，而不責備於貧與老者，則禮之權也。經權不失其宜，然後盡乎人情，而禮行於天下矣。議禮者，當有達於經權之義。

民有德而五穀昌
宋章

同考試官教授陳　批：此題有德在聖人制禮之前，未涉綱紀上說。作者體認不真，率多一槩牽搭，甚以作舉之疵。十日之際，庶本旨。此篇詞氣舂容，而理亦不失，是宜錄之。

考試官教諭何　批：文理醇正，非衆作可及。
translation_en:
…a failure of ritual propriety. To refrain from making physical strength the measure of ritual performance is precisely to accord with the proper mean. This is what is meant by not demanding of people what they cannot perform. Only when material wealth is not made the measure of ritual performance can those without wealth also give satisfaction, allowing ritual to be practiced among the poor. When physical strength is not made its measure, those without strength can likewise do their utmost, allowing ritual to be practiced among the aged. Such is the gentleman’s accommodation of human feelings! Consider, moreover, how even such humble offerings as rabbit heads and gourd leaves may express reverence. The observance of sitting once and bowing down twice also serves to fulfill ritual propriety. How fitting, then, that the poor and the aged should not be held accountable for wealth and strength! Thus we know that ritual has both constant rules and discretionary adaptations. Although using wealth and strength belongs to its constant rules, not demanding full performance from the poor and the aged belongs to its discretionary adaptations. Only when both are applied appropriately can human feelings be fully accommodated and ritual practiced throughout the world. Those who discuss ritual should understand the meaning of constant rules and discretionary adaptations.

“When the People Possess Virtue, the Five Grains Flourish”
Song Zhang 宋章

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen 陳, Prefectural School Professor: The possession of virtue in this topic precedes the sages’ establishment of ritual; it does not yet concern the ordering principles of society. The writers have not grasped this accurately, and most indiscriminately force connections, making this a serious fault in their examination compositions [?]. Within the span of ten days, [this comes] close to the original purport [?]. This essay’s diction and cadence are measured and ample, and its reasoning does not go astray. It therefore deserves inclusion.

Comment by Examiner He 何, County School Instructor: The writing and reasoning are pure and correct, beyond what the other compositions can attain.

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授蔣　批〔謂有德〕〔處得旨〕
人性全而物性遂大當之世然也夫古樂未易
作也大當之世人物各遂其性焉則樂之作也
有由然哉昔子夏告魏文侯之意若曰人徒以
古樂擬諸世俗之音而不知古樂作於大當之
後是故民德本厚有誘斯化矣惟上世之民陶
至和之化忠信誠慤足乎己而無待於外凡所
以相與者一皆有德之人渾淪淳厚出乎身而
孚於人凡所以相接者一皆有德之輩全其固
===
有之天而敦龎之俗居然可見也究其本然之
性而澆漓之風泯然無迹也民之有德如此民
豈有不和乎五穀不熟民有不育矣惟上古之
世協陰陽之和旱澇不復爲灾而泰也稍也與
與然未有苗而不秀者矣昆蟲不復爲害而稷
也麥也菽也粟栗然未有秀而不實者矣百室
盈止仰事俯育之有賴而家獲有年之利百穀
用成養生送死之有給而人享豐登之慶五穀
之昌如此物寧有不和乎夫以人物既和則天
punctuated:
考試官教授蔣批：〔謂有德〕〔處得旨〕

人性全而物性遂，大當之世然也。夫古樂未易作也。大當之世，人物各遂其性焉，則樂之作也有由然哉！昔子夏告魏文侯之意，若曰：人徒以古樂擬諸世俗之音，而不知古樂作於大當之後。是故民德本厚，有誘斯化矣。惟上世之民，陶至和之化，忠信誠慤足乎己，而無待於外。凡所以相與者，一皆有德之人；渾淪淳厚出乎身，而孚於人。凡所以相接者，一皆有德之輩。全其固有之天，而敦龎之俗居然可見也；究其本然之性，而澆漓之風泯然無迹也。民之有德如此，民豈有不和乎？五穀不熟，民有不育矣。惟上古之世，協陰陽之和，旱澇不復爲灾，而泰也、稍也，與與然未有苗而不秀者矣；昆蟲不復爲害，而稷也、麥也、菽也，粟栗然未有秀而不實者矣。百室盈止，仰事俯育之有賴，而家獲有年之利；百穀用成，養生送死之有給，而人享豐登之慶。五穀之昌如此，物寧有不和乎？夫以人物既和，則天
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: 〔In discussing “possessing virtue,”〕〔he captures the purport.〕

Human nature is fully realized and the natures of other things attain fulfillment: such is an age of great accord. Ancient music was not easily created. In an age of great accord, people and other things each fulfill their natures; surely the creation of music thus has its grounds! The meaning of what Zixia once told Marquis Wen of Wei was as follows: people merely compare ancient music with popular tunes, without knowing that ancient music was created only after great accord had been attained. Thus, the people’s virtue was fundamentally substantial; given guidance, they were transformed. The people of high antiquity were molded by the transforming influence of perfect harmony. Loyalty, trustworthiness, sincerity, and integrity were sufficient within themselves, requiring nothing from outside. All those with whom they associated were people possessing virtue. Undivided simplicity and generosity issued from their persons and inspired trust in others. All those with whom they interacted were likewise people possessing virtue. They preserved intact their innate endowment from Heaven, and customs of sincerity and generosity were plainly evident. They fully realized their original nature, and shallow, degenerate practices vanished without a trace. With the people possessing virtue to this extent, how could they fail to be harmonious?

If the five grains do not ripen, some among the people cannot be sustained. In high antiquity, the harmony of yin and yang was duly coordinated. Droughts and floods no longer caused disaster, and the tai and shao crops [?] grew luxuriantly: no shoots failed to come into ear. Insects no longer caused harm, and millet, wheat, and beans grew thickly [?]: nothing that came into ear failed to bear grain. The hundred households were full; with dependable means to support elders and nurture children, every family gained the benefits of a fruitful year. The hundred grains ripened; with sufficient provision to nourish the living and bury the dead, everyone enjoyed the blessings of an abundant harvest. With the five grains flourishing to this extent, how could other things fail to be harmonious? Now, since people and other things were already harmonious, then Heaven …

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
地之和應之美古樂之作不有基於是歟嗟夫
樂之爲道所以和天地之氣平天下之情然其
始也則必本於天地四時人物之和而後作焉
後世不復知此故齊宣王惟好世俗之樂而魏
文侯獨悅鄭衛之音其於古樂所謂闕於天地
民物之和而作之可以贊其和者不復可與言
矣故周子曰古以平心今以助欲古以宣化今
以長怨者其有感於是夫
第貳塲
===
論
千聖相傳心法之要
王化
同考試官訓導張　批〔論至性理便難措詞況聖人心法之精微則更難矣塲中士子非之能言但細讀之則覺詞徒費而旨尚晦者多矣此作精實明當是爲於道有見者而氣昌詞健復脫時文陋習主司得子寧不知重〕
考試官教諭何　批〔近時學者作論不泛及以爲博則刻削以爲奇均爲失體此篇咀嚼道腴發〕
punctuated:
地之和應之，美古樂之作，不有基於是歟？嗟夫！樂之爲道，所以和天地之氣，平天下之情。然其始也，則必本於天地四時人物之和，而後作焉。後世不復知此，故齊宣王惟好世俗之樂，而魏文侯獨悅鄭衛之音。其於古樂所謂闕於天地民物之和而作之，可以贊其和者，不復可與言矣。故周子曰：「古以平心，今以助欲；古以宣化，今以長怨。」者，其有感於是夫！

第貳塲

論
千聖相傳心法之要
王化

同考試官訓導張，批〔論至性理，便難措詞，況聖人心法之精微，則更難矣。塲中士子非之能言，但細讀之，則覺詞徒費而旨尚晦者多矣。此作精實明當，是爲於道有見者，而氣昌詞健，復脫時文陋習。主司得子，寧不知重？〕

考試官教諭何，批〔近時學者作論，不泛及以爲博，則刻削以爲奇，均爲失體。此篇咀嚼道腴，發〕
translation_en:
…the harmony of Earth responds to it. Does not the creation of the beautiful music of antiquity have its foundation here? Ah! The Way of music serves to harmonize the vital energies of Heaven and Earth and bring balance to the feelings of all under Heaven. Yet its creation must first be grounded in the harmony of Heaven and Earth, the four seasons, human beings, and all other creatures. Later generations no longer understood this. Thus King Xuan of Qi delighted only in popular music, while Marquis Wen of Wei took pleasure only in the melodies of Zheng and Wei. With such men one could no longer discuss ancient music—what is described as being created in the absence of harmony [?] among Heaven and Earth, the people, and all creatures, yet capable of furthering that harmony. Thus Master Zhou said: “In antiquity it calmed the heart; today it stimulates desire. In antiquity it spread moral transformation; today it fosters resentment.” Surely these words arose from his reflections on this!

Second Session

Discourse
The Essentials of the Method of the Mind Transmitted through a Thousand Sages
Wang Hua

Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “When a discourse touches on human nature and principle, it becomes difficult to find the right words; how much harder, then, to express the subtle profundities of the sages’ method of the mind! The candidates in the examination hall are unable to speak of it [?]; yet on close reading, one finds many whose words are merely wasted while their meaning remains obscure. This composition is precise, substantial, clear, and sound: its author has insight into the Way. Its vigor is abundant and its language robust; moreover, it escapes the vulgar habits of contemporary examination prose. Having found you, how could the presiding examiners fail to value you?”

Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “When scholars nowadays write discourses, they either range indiscriminately over subjects to appear learned or labor over refinements to appear original. Both approaches violate the proper form. This essay savors the rich substance of the Way and expresses…”

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
言有味且氣格渾厚而詞能稱之其才識迥出於人者矣
考試官教授將　批　上下數千年心學講明切
至引證精確且其文斂華含美不欲自露而識
者自知其為佳也錄之以戒夫躁淺者
論曰聖人以道相傳而及於萬世者要亦於理
欲之間致意焉爾夫道以心傳而達之言行政
事之間莫非心之用也然而天理人欲之機于
是乎伏焉使吾存省之功一時而或間則心莫
能純而政以之雜矣聖人知其然故於存心制
行之間既欲極盡其力而聽言行政之際亦不
敢少有忽焉察之精而守之約使天理極於純
全之妙而人欲略無毫髮之萌則德無不盛而
治無不隆矣前聖後聖所以相傳心法於無窮
者孰有要於此也乎朱子曰千聖相傳心法之
要愚請申之夫萬古一理千聖一心聖人心法
之傳遠矣使無其要焉則上何所授以寄精微
之旨下何所承以造極致之妙而千萬世之下
又何所憑據以為心領神會之地哉雖曰一心
punctuated:
言有味，且氣格渾厚，而詞能稱之，其才識迥出於人者矣。

考試官教授將，批：上下數千年，心學講明切至，引證精確，且其文斂華含美，不欲自露，而識者自知其為佳也。錄之以戒夫躁淺者。

論曰：聖人以道相傳而及於萬世者，要亦於理欲之間致意焉爾。夫道以心傳，而達之言行政事之間，莫非心之用也。然而天理人欲之機，于是乎伏焉。使吾存省之功一時而或間，則心莫能純，而政以之雜矣。聖人知其然，故於存心制行之間，既欲極盡其力，而聽言行政之際，亦不敢少有忽焉。察之精而守之約，使天理極於純全之妙，而人欲略無毫髮之萌，則德無不盛，而治無不隆矣。前聖後聖所以相傳心法於無窮者，孰有要於此也乎？朱子曰：「千聖相傳心法之要。」愚請申之。夫萬古一理，千聖一心，聖人心法之傳遠矣。使無其要焉，則上何所授以寄精微之旨，下何所承以造極致之妙，而千萬世之下，又何所憑據以為心領神會之地哉？雖曰一心……
translation_en:
…his words have savor. Moreover, his vigor and bearing are substantial and mellow, and his language measures up to them. His talent and discernment far surpass those of others.

Examiner Jiang, Professor, comments: Across several thousand years, the learning of the mind is elucidated with precision and thoroughness, and the supporting citations are exact. Moreover, the writing restrains its brilliance and holds its beauty within, seeking no display; discerning readers will recognize its excellence for themselves. It is included here to admonish the impetuous and superficial.

The discourse states: When sages transmit the Way to one another and extend it to ten thousand generations, the essential point is simply to attend to the distinction between principle and desire. The Way is transmitted through the mind and expressed in speech, conduct, and affairs of government; all these are functions of the mind. Yet within them lie the incipient movements of heavenly principle and human desire. Should our work of preserving and examining the mind lapse even for a moment, the mind cannot remain pure, and government consequently becomes adulterated. Knowing this, the sages seek to exert themselves to the utmost in preserving the mind and regulating conduct; when listening to words and administering government, they likewise dare not be even slightly negligent. They discern with precision and hold fast to what is essential, bringing heavenly principle to the consummate subtlety of complete purity and allowing not the slightest germ of human desire to arise. Thus virtue invariably flourishes, and government invariably prospers. In the methods of cultivating the mind transmitted without end from earlier sages to later sages, what could be more essential than this? Master Zhu speaks of “the essentials of the methods of cultivating the mind transmitted among the thousand sages.” I venture to elaborate upon this.

Throughout all antiquity there is one principle; among the thousand sages there is one mind. The transmission of the sages’ methods of cultivating the mind extends far back. If these had no essential core, what could earlier sages impart to convey their subtle and refined meaning? What could later sages receive to attain their consummate profundity? And a thousand or ten thousand generations later, what could people rely upon as a basis for inward comprehension and spiritual understanding? Although we speak of one mind…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
也而心有萬用雖曰一理也而理有萬殊求之
萬殊萬用之間膠擾紛錯不勝其煩矣謂其必
有要焉是固然矣然亦豈於此心之外別有隱
僻高虛之論以自摽異於人邪盖聖人之心純
一而不貳者也聖人之政純粹而不雜者也求
之百世之上與百世之下無不同也何也其所
以相傳者固如此也然其擇守維持之功則有
毫釐頃刻不容少緩焉者是則聖人心法之要
也何也聖人之心其未發也有所謂存養之功
===
焉其已發也有所謂省察之功焉其見於言行
政事之間也又有所謂保守戒飭之功焉治其
內而不遺其外舉其精而不畧其粗所以極夫
天理之全而絕夫人欲之盡者也故其德曰天
德道曰王道而非後世之所能及矣是故舜之
戒禹曰人心惟危道心惟微惟精惟一允執厥
中而必繼之以無稽之言勿聽弗詢之謀勿庸
慎乃有位敬脩其可願四海困窮天祿永終孔
子之告顏淵既曰克己復禮為仁一日克己復
punctuated:
也，而心有萬用；雖曰一理也，而理有萬殊。求之萬殊萬用之間，膠擾紛錯，不勝其煩矣。謂其必有要焉，是固然矣。然亦豈於此心之外，別有隱僻高虛之論，以自摽異於人邪？盖聖人之心，純一而不貳者也；聖人之政，純粹而不雜者也。求之百世之上與百世之下，無不同也。何也？其所以相傳者固如此也。然其擇守維持之功，則有毫釐頃刻不容少緩焉者，是則聖人心法之要也。
何也？聖人之心，其未發也，有所謂存養之功焉；其已發也，有所謂省察之功焉；其見於言行政事之間也，又有所謂保守戒飭之功焉。治其內而不遺其外，舉其精而不畧其粗，所以極夫天理之全而絕夫人欲之盡者也。故其德曰天德，道曰王道，而非後世之所能及矣。
是故舜之戒禹曰：「人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中。」而必繼之以「無稽之言勿聽，弗詢之謀勿庸」，「慎乃有位，敬脩其可願」，「四海困窮，天祿永終」。孔子之告顏淵，既曰：「克己復禮為仁。一日克己復
translation_en:
…yet the mind has myriad functions. Though we speak of a single principle, principle has myriad differentiations. To seek it amid these myriad differentiations and functions is to encounter such tangled confusion that their complexity becomes overwhelming. To say that there must be an essential point is certainly correct. Yet could there be, outside this mind, some obscure, abstruse, lofty, and empty doctrine by which one distinguishes oneself from others? The sage’s mind is wholly unified and undivided; the sage’s government is pure and unmixed. Whether we look a hundred generations into the past or a hundred generations into the future, it is everywhere the same. Why? Because what sages transmit to one another is inherently like this. Yet their work of discerning, holding fast, and sustaining admits not the slightest relaxation, even for an instant. This is the essential point of the sages’ method of cultivating the mind.
Why is this so? Before the sage’s mind is aroused, there is what is called the work of preserving and nourishing it. Once it is aroused, there is what is called the work of examination and scrutiny. When it manifests itself in speech, conduct, and affairs of government, there is also what is called the work of safeguarding it and maintaining vigilance. They regulate what is within without neglecting what is without, and attend to the refined without overlooking the coarse. By these means they bring Heavenly principle to its fullest realization and extinguish human desires completely. Hence their virtue is called Heavenly virtue, and their Way is called the Kingly Way: these are beyond the reach of later ages.
Thus Shun’s admonition to Yu states: “The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. Be discerning, be single-minded, and truly hold fast to the Mean.” He necessarily followed this with: “Do not listen to unsubstantiated words; do not employ plans that have not been considered in consultation”; “Be cautious in your position, and reverently cultivate what is worthy of desire”; and “If all within the Four Seas fall into distress and poverty, Heaven’s emolument will end forever.” When Kongzi instructed Yan Yuan, he said: “To overcome oneself and return to ritual propriety is benevolence. If for a single day one overcomes oneself and returns to…”

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
禮天下歸仁焉爲仁由己而由人乎哉而又申
之曰非禮勿視非禮勿聽非禮勿言非禮勿動
旣告之以損益四代之禮樂而又申之曰放鄭
聲遠佞人鄭聲淫佞人殆嗚呼盡之矣盖精一
之要克復之功所以審天人於一心之發愼理
欲於一念之微者密矣而聽言處事之間安危
存亡之戒視聽言動之際謹於非禮之目則又
所以絶夫人欲之盡以極乎天理之全者至矣
四代禮樂之制其即有位可願之道鄭聲佞人
===
之害其即窮困永終之弊是又所以使天理無
一息之間而人欲無一隙之投者不可復加矣
盖天下之事本於心而發之於處己接人政事
禮樂之大治心要矣而處己接人政事禮樂一
有忽焉則亦豈得爲盡善而亦豈聖人之心哉
是故聖人所以德已盛而自强之心不息治已
至而憂勤之心無窮舜禹孔顔親相授受於一
堂之上不過如此則千聖相傳之心法宜無要
於此者矣盖舜之告禹非舜之私言也以其傳
punctuated:
禮，天下歸仁焉。爲仁由己，而由人乎哉？」而又申之曰：「非禮勿視，非禮勿聽，非禮勿言，非禮勿動。」旣告之以損益四代之禮樂，而又申之曰：「放鄭聲，遠佞人。鄭聲淫，佞人殆。」嗚呼，盡之矣！
盖精一之要、克復之功，所以審天人於一心之發、愼理欲於一念之微者密矣。而聽言處事之間，安危存亡之戒；視聽言動之際，謹於非禮之目，則又所以絶夫人欲之盡，以極乎天理之全者至矣。四代禮樂之制，其即有位可願之道；鄭聲佞人之害，其即窮困永終之弊。是又所以使天理無一息之間，而人欲無一隙之投者，不可復加矣。
盖天下之事本於心，而發之於處己接人、政事禮樂之大。治心要矣，而處己接人、政事禮樂一有忽焉，則亦豈得爲盡善，而亦豈聖人之心哉？是故聖人所以德已盛而自强之心不息，治已至而憂勤之心無窮。舜禹孔顔親相授受於一堂之上，不過如此，則千聖相傳之心法，宜無要於此者矣。盖舜之告禹，非舜之私言也，以其傳
translation_en:
…ritual propriety, all under Heaven will turn to humaneness. Practicing humaneness depends on oneself—could it depend on others?” He further elaborated: “Do not look at what is contrary to ritual propriety; do not listen to what is contrary to ritual propriety; do not speak what is contrary to ritual propriety; do not act contrary to ritual propriety.” Having instructed him about what to discard and what to retain in the rites and music of the four dynasties, he further elaborated: “Banish the music of Zheng and keep glib talkers at a distance. The music of Zheng is licentious, and glib talkers are dangerous.” Ah, this says it all!
The essentials of refinement and single-mindedness, and the work of overcoming oneself and returning to ritual propriety, provide meticulous means of distinguishing Heaven from the human element as the mind stirs, and of carefully discerning principle and desire in the subtlest beginnings of a thought. Moreover, when listening to words and handling affairs, there are admonitions concerning security and danger, preservation and ruin; when looking, listening, speaking, and acting, there is vigilance concerning each prohibition against what violates ritual propriety. These are the ultimate means of utterly eliminating human desires and fully realizing heavenly principle. The institutions of rites and music of the four dynasties embody precisely the way expressed in “be careful concerning those who hold office” and “reverently cultivate what is worthy of being desired.” The harm caused by the music of Zheng and glib talkers is precisely the evil expressed in “distress and poverty” and “ending forever”—the distress of the realm and the end of Heaven’s emolument. These means of ensuring that heavenly principle is uninterrupted for even a single breath, and that human desires find not a single opening through which to enter, admit of no further improvement.
All affairs under Heaven are rooted in the mind and find expression in personal conduct, dealings with others, and the great matters of government, rites, and music. Governing the mind is essential; yet if there is any neglect in personal conduct, dealings with others, government, rites, or music, how could this count as perfect goodness? And how could it be the mind of a sage? This is why, though a sage’s virtue is already abundant, his resolve to strengthen himself never ceases; though his government has reached perfection, his concern and diligence never end. Even if Shun, Yu, Confucius, and Yan Hui personally transmitted and received instruction together in one hall, it would amount to no more than this. Thus, among the teachings of the mind transmitted from sage to sage, none could be more essential than this. What Shun told Yu was not merely Shun’s own pronouncement: he took what had been transmitted to him…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
之堯者而傳之禹也孔子之告顏淵非孔子之
私言也以其傳之禹者而傳之顏子也自後曾
子傳之則曰致知誠意謹於惡善之分曰治國
平天下嚴於好惡之正此心此理也子思傳之
則曰戒懼謹獨密於存省之功曰中和位育要
夫推致之極此法此要也又非特曾子子思而
已也百世以俟而不惑萬古以心而相感凡為
吾聖人之徒者孰能外此心法而別有所事邪
惜乎孟軻氏死而不得其傳矣兩漢以来非無
===
願治之主而莫克有志於是焉是故其下者徒
求之政而不得於心也不免流於雜霸雜夷之
習但隨世以就功名而莫知所謂本末始終之
序是以功業卑污規摹狹陋而多有愧於隆古
吾聖人之道果如是之淺近而無用乎其高者
知求諸心而不得其要也不免蔽於老子浮屠
之說謂心無所主而能應變莫知所謂存養省
察之功是以內外乖離不相為用而反有害於
政事吾聖人之道亦如是之偏詖而無實乎斯
punctuated: 之堯者而傳之禹也。孔子之告顏淵，非孔子之私言也，以其傳之禹者而傳之顏子也。自後曾子傳之，則曰致知誠意，謹於惡善之分；曰治國平天下，嚴於好惡之正：此心此理也。子思傳之，則曰戒懼謹獨，密於存省之功；曰中和位育，要夫推致之極：此法此要也。又非特曾子子思而已也。百世以俟而不惑，萬古以心而相感，凡為吾聖人之徒者，孰能外此心法而別有所事邪？惜乎孟軻氏死而不得其傳矣！兩漢以来，非無願治之主，而莫克有志於是焉。是故其下者徒求之政，而不得於心也，不免流於雜霸雜夷之習，但隨世以就功名，而莫知所謂本末始終之序。是以功業卑污，規摹狹陋，而多有愧於隆古。吾聖人之道果如是之淺近而無用乎？其高者知求諸心，而不得其要也，不免蔽於老子浮屠之說，謂心無所主而能應變，莫知所謂存養省察之功。是以內外乖離，不相為用，而反有害於政事。吾聖人之道亦如是之偏詖而無實乎？斯
translation_en:
…what he had received from Yao and transmitted it to Yu. What Kongzi told Yan Yuan was not his private teaching: he transmitted to Master Yan what had been transmitted to Yu. Thereafter, when Zengzi transmitted it, he spoke of extending knowledge and making intentions sincere, carefully distinguishing evil from good; and of governing the state and bringing peace to all under Heaven, rigorously ensuring that likes and dislikes were correct. It was this same mind and this same principle. When Zisi transmitted it, he spoke of vigilance, apprehension, and care when alone, making the work of preserving and examining the mind meticulous; and of equilibrium and harmony, through which Heaven and Earth take their proper places and all things are nourished, seeking the utmost extension of their effects. It was this same method and this same essential teaching. Nor was this confined to Zengzi and Zisi. One may await a sage a hundred generations hence without doubt; across all ages, minds respond to one another. Who among the followers of our sages could set aside this method of the mind and pursue some other undertaking? Alas, when Meng Ke died, no one received this transmission!

Since the two Han dynasties, there have certainly been rulers who desired good government, yet none could set their resolve upon this. Thus, those of the lesser sort sought it merely in government and failed to grasp it in the mind. Inevitably, they drifted into practices mingled with those of hegemons and foreign peoples, merely following the age in pursuit of achievement and fame, without understanding the proper sequence of root and branch, beginning and end. Consequently, their accomplishments were base, their scope narrow, and in many respects they fell shamefully short of high antiquity. Could the Way of our sages really be so shallow and useless?

Those of the higher sort knew to seek it in the mind, but failed to grasp its essentials. Inevitably, they were blinded by the teachings of Laozi and Buddhism, claiming that the mind could respond to changing circumstances without anything governing it, and knowing nothing of the work of preserving, nurturing, examining, and scrutinizing it. Consequently, the inner and outer realms became estranged and failed to serve one another; indeed, this harmed affairs of government. Could the Way of our sages likewise be so one-sided and devoid of substance? At this…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
時也所謂千聖相傳心法之要盖不復講矣然
而道本始不存也心未始不同也世有聖人之
徒出焉則豈終不可傳哉百世之下周子之所
謂幾程子之所謂敬則超然有契乎此者矣盖
幾者動之微敬者德之聚幾可成誠明神妙之
功敬可為脩身立政之本其為言愈約而意愈
切矣朱子謂幾為第一親切工夫又謂敬為聖
學始終之要所以闡明微旨者益親切矣然則
契聖心於絕學之後啓斯文於將墜之餘萬世
公論必以道統之傳歸之數君子者豈無謂哉
===
表
擬宋以唐介知諫院謝表〔嘉祐元年 四月初五日〕
王室
同考試官訓導張　批　表有事實語亦典雅所
謂麗而則也
考試官教諭何　批　雖唐子方自作不過如此
考試官教授蔣　批　得宋表體
伏以
punctuated:
時也，所謂千聖相傳心法之要，盖不復講矣。然而道本始不存也，心未始不同也。世有聖人之徒出焉，則豈終不可傳哉？百世之下，周子之所謂幾、程子之所謂敬，則超然有契乎此者矣。盖幾者動之微，敬者德之聚。幾可成誠明神妙之功，敬可為脩身立政之本，其為言愈約而意愈切矣。朱子謂幾為第一親切工夫，又謂敬為聖學始終之要，所以闡明微旨者益親切矣。然則契聖心於絕學之後，啓斯文於將墜之餘，萬世公論必以道統之傳歸之數君子者，豈無謂哉？
表
擬宋以唐介知諫院謝表〔嘉祐元年 四月初五日〕
王室
同考試官訓導張批：表有事實，語亦典雅，所謂麗而則也。
考試官教諭何批：雖唐子方自作，不過如此。
考試官教授蔣批：得宋表體。
伏以：
translation_en:
…at that time, the essential teaching concerning the mind, handed down through a thousand sages, was apparently no longer discussed. Yet the Way originally did not exist [?], while the mind has never ceased to be the same. If followers of the sages should emerge in the world, how could this teaching remain forever incapable of transmission? A hundred generations later, what Master Zhou called incipience and what Master Cheng called reverent attentiveness attained an extraordinary accord with it. Incipience is the subtle beginning of movement; reverent attentiveness is the gathering together of virtue. Through incipience one can achieve sincerity, illumination, and spiritual subtlety; reverent attentiveness can provide the foundation for cultivating oneself and establishing government. The more concise their words, the more pertinent their meaning. Master Zhu called incipience the foremost and most immediately relevant practical effort, and also called reverent attentiveness the essential principle of sagely learning from beginning to end. His elucidation of these subtle meanings was still more directly pertinent. Thus, in recovering accord with the sages’ minds after their learning had been interrupted, and opening the way for this cultural tradition when it was on the verge of collapse, these gentlemen surely had good reason to receive the credit, in the public judgment of all ages, for transmitting the succession of the Way.

Memorial

A simulated memorial of thanks on behalf of Tang Jie of the Song upon his appointment to administer the Bureau of Remonstrance. 〔First year of Jiayou, fourth month, fifth day.〕
By Wang Shi.
