title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
保氏舊官叅
廊廟股肱之列諫垣華秩實
朝廷耳目之司責任匪輕選掄宜慎臣介雕
蟲末技章句腐儒名偶玷於賢科跡遂登
於仕路驅馳下邑慚無撫字之勞薦歷中
臺愧負激揚之任勵平生自守之志上期
不負於所知慕先哲敢諫之風下欲不孤
於所學擬奪宣徽之使而心實慮其瀆療
因攻宰輔之私而言遂傷於激直犯
===
雷霆之怒宜服嚴刑弘
天地之仁止施薄竄護送勞於中使編置移於
近州望已絕於
賜環憂尚懸於投杼詎意光生腐草温轉寒灰
賜告趣歸廢替再瞻於
日月傳宣入對朽株重沐於陽春此盖伏遇
乾健離明
堯仁禹儉崇儒好學衍聖賢道統之傳惜費
punctuated:
保氏舊官，叅廊廟股肱之列；諫垣華秩，實朝廷耳目之司。責任匪輕，選掄宜慎。臣介，雕蟲末技，章句腐儒，名偶玷於賢科，跡遂登於仕路。驅馳下邑，慚無撫字之勞；薦歷中臺，愧負激揚之任。勵平生自守之志，上期不負於所知；慕先哲敢諫之風，下欲不孤於所學。擬奪宣徽之使，而心實慮其瀆療；因攻宰輔之私，而言遂傷於激直。犯雷霆之怒，宜服嚴刑；弘天地之仁，止施薄竄。護送勞於中使，編置移於近州。望已絕於賜環，憂尚懸於投杼。詎意光生腐草，温轉寒灰！賜告趣歸，廢替再瞻於日月；傳宣入對，朽株重沐於陽春。

此盖伏遇乾健離明，堯仁禹儉，崇儒好學，衍聖賢道統之傳，惜費
translation_en:
…The ancient office of Guardian stood among the court’s supporting ministers; the distinguished rank in the remonstrance service is indeed charged with serving as the court’s ears and eyes. Its responsibilities are weighty, and selection should be careful. Your servant Jie possesses only trifling literary skills, a pedantic scholar of textual phrases. By chance my name gained an undeserved place among successful examination candidates, and thus I entered official service. Serving diligently in a subordinate district, I was ashamed to have accomplished little in caring for the people; subsequently serving in the Censorate, I was ashamed to have failed my responsibility to condemn the wicked and commend the worthy. I strengthened my lifelong resolve to maintain my integrity, hoping above to prove worthy of those who recognized me; I admired the ancient worthies’ courage in remonstrance, wishing below to remain true to what I had learned. I sought to have the Commissioner of Palace Services deprived of his appointment, my heart truly concerned about his abuses [?]. In attacking the chief minister’s pursuit of private interests, however, my words became excessively vehement and blunt. Having provoked Your Majesty’s thunderous anger, I deserved severe punishment; yet, extending benevolence as vast as heaven and earth, you imposed only mild banishment. A palace envoy was put to the trouble of escorting me, and my assigned place of residence was transferred to a nearby prefecture. I had already abandoned hope of receiving the jade ring that signaled recall, while anxiety over slander—the tale of the mother throwing down her shuttle—still hung over me. Who could have imagined light arising from rotting grass, or warmth returning to cold ashes! An appointment document was bestowed to hasten my return, and I, dismissed from office, once more beheld the sun and moon of imperial majesty. Summoned by imperial command to an audience, I, a rotten stump, again received the warmth of spring.

This was because I humbly encountered Your Majesty, vigorous as Heaven and radiant as Fire, benevolent as Yao and frugal as Yu. You honor Confucian scholars and delight in learning, extending the transmission of the sages’ and worthies’ succession to the Way, sparing in expenditure…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
弭兵培
社稷靈長之祚
道無私覆
明出至公察臣之罪雖本狂愚原臣之心實
出忠愛謂流離遠外将事體之周知以經
歷憂危必志氣之堅定
寵以
新命責其後功榮出不虞慮慚弗稱因念
盛朝諫院之設葢欲闕維蔽以專責成
===
皇上諫員之除亦惟任忠賢以求獻納養慷慨
敢言之氣期雍熙至治之休苟或有負於
時未免取譏於後臣敢不矢心論議仰承
録用之心畢力敷陳勉盡平生之志伏願
明先萬里不攅立仗之良
聰闢四門無取鳴陽之異諫行言聽上下同乎
一心業盛德成
宫府合為一體懋慶
明良之會載賡喜起之歌臣無任瞻
punctuated: 弭兵，培社稷靈長之祚。道無私覆，明出至公。察臣之罪，雖本狂愚；原臣之心，實出忠愛。謂流離遠外，将事體之周知；以經歷憂危，必志氣之堅定。寵以新命，責其後功。榮出不虞，慮慚弗稱。因念盛朝諫院之設，葢欲闕維蔽以專責成。皇上諫員之除，亦惟任忠賢以求獻納。養慷慨敢言之氣，期雍熙至治之休。苟或有負於時，未免取譏於後。臣敢不矢心論議，仰承録用之心；畢力敷陳，勉盡平生之志。伏願明先萬里，不攅立仗之良；聰闢四門，無取鳴陽之異。諫行言聽，上下同乎一心；業盛德成，宫府合為一體。懋慶明良之會，載賡喜起之歌。臣無任瞻
translation_en:
…quelling warfare and nurturing the enduring blessings of the altars of soil and grain. Your Way shelters all impartially; your discernment proceeds from perfect fairness. You perceived that your servant’s offense arose from rash foolishness, yet, examining his intentions, found that they truly sprang from loyalty and love. You considered that wandering in distant exile would bring comprehensive knowledge of affairs, and that experiencing anxiety and peril would surely strengthen his resolve. You favored him with a new appointment, charging him to achieve results hereafter. This honor came unexpectedly; I fear, with shame, that I may prove unequal to it.

I reflect that our flourishing dynasty established its remonstrance office to address shortcomings and obstructions [?], assigning it definite responsibility for results. Your Majesty likewise appoints remonstrance officials solely to entrust loyal and worthy men with offering counsel. You nurture a spirited readiness to speak boldly, anticipating the blessings of harmonious and consummate government. Should I fail the needs of the present age, I could hardly escape the censure of posterity. How could your servant dare not devote himself wholeheartedly to deliberation, reverently answering your intention in employing him, and exert every effort in presenting his views, striving to fulfill his lifelong aspiration?

I humbly wish that your discernment may anticipate affairs ten thousand li away, and that you may not gather fine horses merely to stand among the ceremonial guards [?]; that your hearing may open to all four quarters, without seeking the rarity of a phoenix singing on the sunny slope. With remonstrances acted upon and counsel heard, those above and below will share one heart; with undertakings flourishing and virtue perfected, palace and government offices will unite as one body. Joyfully celebrating the meeting of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers, I again take up the song of mutual delight and endeavor. Your servant cannot contain his feelings as he gazes toward…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉表陳
謝以
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
尹寵
同考試官教諭高　批〔我〕
宣廟五倫書布在天下士子服習久矣但風簷問責其錯舉君臣善
行則非胸中素有此書者不能此篇非惟事實無遺
而且隱括相稱況他策與前二場俱超出人意表噫子
===
其齊魯之傑然者乎
同考試官學正越　批〔士子於〕
聖製一策駕說者多信實學難得也得子可以自慶子尚勉
哉吾將觀子之爲臣矣
同考試官教授汪　批〔明倫之學士子第一義也〕
求能推誦
punctuated:
天仰聖，激切屏營之至，謹奉表陳謝以聞。
第叁場
策
第一問
尹寵
同考試官教諭高批：〔我〕宣廟五倫書布在天下，士子服習久矣。但風簷問責其錯舉君臣善行，則非胸中素有此書者不能。此篇非惟事實無遺，而且隱括相稱，況他策與前二場俱超出人意表。噫！子其齊魯之傑然者乎！
同考試官學正越批：〔士子於〕聖製一策，駕說者多，信實學難得也。得子，可以自慶。子尚勉哉！吾將觀子之爲臣矣。
同考試官教授汪批：〔明倫之學士子第一義也〕求能推誦
translation_en:
…gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, with the utmost fervor and trembling apprehension, I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Yin Chong

Comment by Associate Examiner Gao, Instructor:
“The Book of the Five Human Relationships of our Emperor Xuanzong has circulated throughout the realm, and examination candidates have long studied and practiced its teachings. Yet when, beneath the wind-swept eaves of the examination hall, they are asked to cite a range of virtuous deeds by rulers and ministers, only those already thoroughly familiar with this book can do so. This essay not only omits none of the historical facts but also aptly condenses and arranges them. Moreover, his other policy essays and his work in the preceding two sessions all surpass expectations. Ah! Surely you are an outstanding talent of Qi and Lu!”

Comment by Associate Examiner Yue, Instructor:
“On the policy question concerning the imperially authored work, many candidates fabricate their explanations [?]; sound learning is indeed hard to find. Having found you, I may congratulate myself. Continue to exert yourself! I shall watch how you serve as a minister.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Professor:
“Learning that clarifies human relationships is the foremost obligation of scholars. To seek someone capable of expounding and reciting…”

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
聖謨援據今古歷舉盡倫之人如此篇者可多得乎
考試官教諭何　批〔五倫書君臣事目爲多此策約而取之比而同之條暢切當是爲〕
善待問者
考試官教授蔣　批〔觀此策事君爲臣之道略備矣如有用子執此以往可也〕
對五典五惇而天下之大經以正有君有
臣而天下之達道斯行夫人倫明於上小
民親於下五倫豈可不正哉然非明良相
===
逢君臣道合則所以紀綱人道建立人極
者又將責之誰乎此我
宣宗章皇帝五倫之書所以極夫五倫之全而
詳於君臣之道者意蓋有在也愚生竊嘗
伏讀而仰窺之矣其爲書也首載五倫總
論次列君道臣道父道子道夫婦之道兄
弟之道朋友之道父道之後附母與伯叔
叔母子道之後附女與婦兄弟之道附之
以宗族朋友之道附之以師生皆先述嘉
punctuated:
聖謨，援據今古，歷舉盡倫之人如此篇者，可多得乎？
考試官教諭何批〔五倫書君臣事目爲多，此策約而取之，比而同之，條暢切當，是爲〕善待問者。
考試官教授蔣批〔觀此策，事君爲臣之道略備矣。如有用子，執此以往可也。〕
對：五典五惇，而天下之大經以正；有君有臣，而天下之達道斯行。夫人倫明於上，小民親於下，五倫豈可不正哉？然非明良相逢、君臣道合，則所以紀綱人道、建立人極者，又將責之誰乎？此我宣宗章皇帝五倫之書所以極夫五倫之全，而詳於君臣之道者，意蓋有在也。愚生竊嘗伏讀而仰窺之矣。其爲書也，首載五倫總論，次列君道、臣道、父道、子道、夫婦之道、兄弟之道、朋友之道。父道之後，附母與伯叔、叔母；子道之後，附女與婦；兄弟之道，附之以宗族；朋友之道，附之以師生。皆先述嘉
translation_en:
…the imperial teachings, adducing evidence from past and present and enumerating people who fully fulfilled their human relationships as this essay does—can many such essays be found?
Examiner He, Instructor, comments: 〔“The Book of the Five Relationships contains more entries concerning rulers and ministers than other subjects. This policy essay selects and condenses them, compares them and draws out their common principles. Its exposition is clear, fluent, apt, and sound. This is〕someone well prepared to answer questions.”
Examiner Jiang, Professor, comments: 〔“This policy essay gives a broadly complete account of the way to serve a ruler and act as a minister. If someone employs you, you may take this as your guide and proceed.”〕
In reply: When the five constant duties are all earnestly upheld, the great norms of the world are set right; when there are rulers and ministers, the universally binding Way of the world is put into practice. When human relationships are made clear above, the common people below live in mutual affection. How, then, could the five relationships be left unrectified? Yet unless an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers meet, and ruler and ministers accord in the Way, who else can be charged with ordering human conduct and establishing the highest standard of humanity? This surely explains the intention behind our Emperor Xuanzong Zhang’s Book of the Five Relationships: it encompasses all five relationships in their entirety, while treating the way of rulers and ministers in particular detail. I, an unworthy student, have reverently read it and ventured to gain a glimpse of its meaning.
The book first presents a general discussion of the five relationships, then sets out the ways of rulers, ministers, fathers, sons, husbands and wives, elder and younger brothers, and friends. Following the way of fathers, it appends sections on mothers, paternal uncles, and the wives of younger paternal uncles; following the way of sons, it appends sections on daughters and daughters-in-law. To the way of brothers it appends that of the lineage, and to the way of friends it appends that of teachers and students. Each first recounts exemplary…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
言次著善行可謂極明且備矣然其中敘
述君臣之道視彼四倫尤爲詳盡者豈不
以君也者承天心而出治道臣也者承君
之化而致之民其分雖殊其道則合尤爲
有功於五倫者乎是故堯舜之廣運重華
湯文之懋昭敬止聖德不可加矣伯禹皐
陶之陳謨伊尹周公之作訓輔德豈可少
邪高宗之命說交脩武王之致齋問道聖
學不可尚矣孔子明堯舜禹湯文武之道
孟子述唐虞三代之德正學豈可無邪漢
===
明帝之遵奉制度我
太宗之恪遵成憲法祖之心盛矣張釋之秦廷
尉天下之平戴胄論法布國家之信守法
之心不可嘉乎唐堯有敷治之舉虞舜立
考績之法制治之謀遠矣伯禹之弼成五
服周公之設官分職經國之謀不可重乎
徧求傅巖之遺賢枉駕南陽之隱德高宗
先主之勞於求賢也韓信於國士無雙如
punctuated: 言，次著善行，可謂極明且備矣。然其中敘述君臣之道，視彼四倫尤爲詳盡者，豈不以君也者承天心而出治道，臣也者承君之化而致之民，其分雖殊，其道則合，尤爲有功於五倫者乎？是故堯舜之廣運重華，湯文之懋昭敬止，聖德不可加矣；伯禹皐陶之陳謨，伊尹周公之作訓，輔德豈可少邪？高宗之命說交脩，武王之致齋問道，聖學不可尚矣；孔子明堯舜禹湯文武之道，孟子述唐虞三代之德，正學豈可無邪？漢明帝之遵奉制度，我太宗之恪遵成憲，法祖之心盛矣；張釋之秦廷尉天下之平，戴胄論法布國家之信，守法之心不可嘉乎？唐堯有敷治之舉，虞舜立考績之法，制治之謀遠矣；伯禹之弼成五服，周公之設官分職，經國之謀不可重乎？徧求傅巖之遺賢，枉駕南陽之隱德，高宗先主之勞於求賢也；韓信於國士無雙，如
translation_en:
…words, and then records good deeds: it may be called supremely clear and comprehensive. Yet its account of the way of ruler and minister is especially detailed compared with those of the other four relationships. Is this not because the ruler receives Heaven’s intentions and brings forth the way of government, while the minister receives the ruler’s transforming influence and conveys it to the people? Though their respective duties differ, their ways converge, making an especially great contribution to the five human relationships.

Thus, in Yao’s far-reaching greatness and Shun’s renewed brilliance, and in Tang’s conspicuous virtue and King Wen’s reverent adherence to his proper place, sagely virtue could rise no higher. Yet could the counsels presented by Bo Yu and Gao Yao, and the instructions composed by Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, be dispensed with in assisting that virtue? Gaozong commanded Yue to join him in cultivating virtue, and King Wu observed ritual purification and inquired into the Way: sagely learning could not be surpassed. Yet could the correct learning exemplified by Confucius’s elucidation of the Way of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, and by Mencius’s exposition of the virtue of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties, be absent?

Emperor Ming of the Han observed the established institutions, and our Taizong scrupulously followed the established statutes: their resolve to emulate their ancestors was great indeed. Zhang Shizhi declared that the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement was the impartial standard for all under Heaven [?]; Dai Zhou argued that the laws proclaimed the state’s good faith. Should their resolve to uphold the law not be praised? Tang Yao undertook to extend orderly government, and Yu Shun established methods for evaluating officials’ performance: their plans for securing good government were far-reaching. Bo Yu helped establish the five service zones, and the Duke of Zhou instituted offices and apportioned duties. Should their plans for ordering the state not be held in high esteem?

Searching everywhere for the overlooked worthy at Fuyan, and deigning to visit the man of hidden virtue at Nanyang: these were the efforts Gaozong and the Former Lord made to seek worthy men. Han Xin was peerless among the outstanding men of the realm; Ru…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
晦有王佐之才蕭何玄齡不亦忠於薦舉
者乎貶王伾叔文於遠方罷章惇蔡卞於
要位憲宗哲宗之决於去邪也疏言李義
府之奸書奏任守忠之罪王義方司馬光
不亦敢於劾奏者乎漢宣帝美黃霸之治
賜爵賜金我
太祖表余闕之忠建祠肖像皆以褒嘉爲勸者
也睢陽堅守張巡實欲氣吞逆賊黃龍痛
飲岳飛誠爲盡忠報主非忠義之最者乎
===
漢文帝嘗止輦受言而假借納用唐太宗
知進諫誠難而求諫不怠皆以聽納爲德
者也董賢貴倖鮑宣直言其進以令諛陸
贄罷相陽城直疏其退之無罪非諫諍之
顯者乎仁民盛德如漢文帝憂鰥寡孤獨
之人而爲振貸之議我
太祖念凋弊荒蕪之苦而有寬免之詔是已使
臣之恤民者皆如劉寬之拯救寒困如恐
不及程顥之存心愛物於人有濟撫字者
punctuated: 晦有王佐之才，蕭何、玄齡不亦忠於薦舉者乎？貶王伾、叔文於遠方，罷章惇、蔡卞於要位，憲宗、哲宗之决於去邪也。疏言李義府之奸，書奏任守忠之罪，王義方、司馬光不亦敢於劾奏者乎？漢宣帝美黃霸之治，賜爵賜金；我太祖表余闕之忠，建祠肖像，皆以褒嘉爲勸者也。睢陽堅守，張巡實欲氣吞逆賊；黃龍痛飲，岳飛誠爲盡忠報主，非忠義之最者乎？漢文帝嘗止輦受言，而假借納用；唐太宗知進諫誠難，而求諫不怠，皆以聽納爲德者也。董賢貴倖，鮑宣直言其進以令諛；陸贄罷相，陽城直疏其退之無罪，非諫諍之顯者乎？仁民盛德，如漢文帝憂鰥寡孤獨之人，而爲振貸之議；我太祖念凋弊荒蕪之苦，而有寬免之詔，是已。使臣之恤民者，皆如劉寬之拯救寒困，如恐不及；程顥之存心愛物，於人有濟；撫字者
translation_en:
…[Du Ru]hui possessed the talent to assist a king. Were Xiao He and [Fang] Xuanling not devoted to recommending worthy men? Banishing Wang Pi and [Wang] Shuwen to distant regions and removing Zhang Dun and Cai Bian from important posts showed the resolve of Emperors Xianzong and Zhezong to eliminate the wicked. Submitting a memorial exposing Li Yifu’s treachery and reporting Ren Shouzhong’s crimes in writing—were Wang Yifang and Sima Guang not courageous in presenting impeachments? Emperor Xuandi of Han praised Huang Ba’s administration and bestowed noble rank and gold upon him. Our Taizu honored Yu Que’s loyalty by erecting a shrine and having his likeness made. Both used commendation to encourage others. In holding Suiyang firmly, Zhang Xun truly sought to overwhelm the rebels with his spirit; in aspiring to drink his fill at Huanglong, Yue Fei truly meant to repay his sovereign with complete loyalty. Were these not supreme examples of loyalty and righteousness?

Emperor Wendi of Han once stopped his imperial carriage to receive advice, treating the speaker generously and accepting and employing his counsel. Emperor Taizong of Tang knew that offering remonstrance was truly difficult, yet never tired of seeking it. Both regarded listening to and accepting counsel as a virtue. When Dong Xian enjoyed exalted status and imperial favor, Bao Xuan declared frankly that his advancement came through ingratiating flattery. When Lu Zhi was dismissed as chief minister, Yang Cheng submitted a forthright memorial stating that he had been removed without having committed any offense. Were these not conspicuous examples of remonstrance?

As for the great virtue of benevolence toward the people, Emperor Wendi of Han was concerned for widowers, widows, orphans, and the childless elderly, and proposed relief grants and loans. Our Taizu considered the suffering caused by impoverishment and the abandonment of cultivated land, and issued an edict granting remissions. These exemplify that virtue. If ministers charged with caring for the people were all like Liu Kuan, who rescued those suffering from cold and want as though afraid he might not reach them in time, or like Cheng Hao, who cherished all beings in his heart and brought aid to others; and if those charged with nurturing the people…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
皆如卓茂之勞心諄諄視民如子張載之
敦本善俗問民疾苦豈不有助哉馭夷長
策若周宣王之薄伐玁狁至于太原漢文
帝之通使南越藩臣奉貢是已使臣之將
畧也皆如韓信之入壁立幟壅水決囊徐
達之築臺設礮批亢擣虛備邊也皆如李
牧居鴈門單于不敢近邊張堪在漁陽匈
奴不敢犯塞豈不有補哉是則后克艱厥
后臣克艱厥臣黎民敏德人紀肇脩而父
===
子夫婦兄弟朋友之道皆於是而畢舉矣
嗚乎此我
宣宗經天緯地之文燦然大明於今
神功聖德之盛巍然追配乎古者也愚生欽江
河之深惟取於充量仰天地之大固難於
爲言惟執事其與進之幸甚
第二問
林瓊
同考試官教諭楊　批　考証尚書唐鑑故實
punctuated:
皆如卓茂之勞心諄諄，視民如子，張載之敦本善俗，問民疾苦，豈不有助哉？馭夷長策，若周宣王之薄伐玁狁，至于太原，漢文帝之通使南越，藩臣奉貢，是已。使臣之將畧也，皆如韓信之入壁立幟，壅水決囊，徐達之築臺設礮，批亢擣虛；備邊也，皆如李牧居鴈門，單于不敢近邊，張堪在漁陽，匈奴不敢犯塞，豈不有補哉？是則后克艱厥后，臣克艱厥臣，黎民敏德，人紀肇脩，而父子、夫婦、兄弟、朋友之道，皆於是而畢舉矣。
嗚乎！此我宣宗經天緯地之文，燦然大明於今，神功聖德之盛，巍然追配乎古者也。愚生欽江河之深，惟取於充量；仰天地之大，固難於爲言。惟執事其與進之，幸甚！
第二問
林瓊
同考試官教諭楊　批：考証《尚書》、《唐鑑》故實，
translation_en:
…if all were like Zhuo Mao, who devoted himself tirelessly to instructing the people and regarded them as his children, or Zhang Zai, who strengthened fundamental moral principles, improved customs, and inquired into the people’s hardships, would this not be of assistance? As for far-reaching strategies for managing the foreign peoples, examples are King Xuan of Zhou’s expedition against the Xianyun as far as Taiyuan, and Emperor Wen of Han’s exchange of envoys with Nanyue, whose ruler became a vassal and presented tribute. If ministers, in their generalship, were all like Han Xin, who entered the enemy’s camp and planted his banners, and dammed a river with sacks before releasing its waters, or Xu Da, who built platforms and emplaced cannon, struck at vital points, and attacked undefended positions; and if, in defending the frontier, they were all like Li Mu, whose presence in Yanmen kept the chanyu from daring to approach the border, or Zhang Kan, whose service in Yuyang kept the Xiongnu from daring to violate the frontier, would this not be beneficial? Then the ruler would appreciate the difficulty of being a ruler, and ministers the difficulty of being ministers; the common people would strive for virtue, and the fundamental human relationships would begin to be properly cultivated. The duties between fathers and sons, husbands and wives, elder and younger brothers, and friends would thereby all be fulfilled.
Ah! Such is our Emperor Xuanzong’s civil accomplishment in ordering Heaven and Earth, shining brilliantly down to the present; such is the grandeur of his divine achievements and sagely virtue, loftily matching those of antiquity. This ignorant student reveres the depth of the rivers, yet can draw only as much as his vessel holds; he looks up to the vastness of Heaven and Earth, yet finds it truly difficult to put into words. If you, honored examiners, would approve and advance him, he would be most fortunate!
Second Policy Question
Lin Qiong
Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: He examines and verifies historical precedents in the Book of Documents and the Mirror of the Tang …

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
正合二臣進勸之意末論周禮春秋相符處
亦是可以占子經史之學矣
考試官教諭何　批　羅氏之言人皆知之
至論要歸在正君心為儒臣進勸之資而知之
者鮮此策立議有據而辭足以發之得薦事
考試官教授蔣　批　取經史格言用發古
人之心出詞不費而意足良是策場法度彼
掇拾問目者可鑒矣
君其慎斯術以往
===
有帝王為學之要有帝王為學之本夫人
主之學係天下之治忽而人主之心關治
忽之本原學矣而無其要則用心於泛而
不知所以為治之資要矣而無所本則溺
意於外而不知所以出治之原故人君之
學莫病於泛而經史其要也莫病於外而
心術其本也知此則可以識先儒著論之
意臣工勸講之心而為明問復矣今夫六
經皆所以載道而道之存主者意也意有
punctuated:
正合二臣進勸之意。末論周禮春秋相符處，亦是可以占子經史之學矣。
考試官教諭何批：羅氏之言，人皆知之；至論要歸在正君心，為儒臣進勸之資，而知之者鮮。此策立議有據，而辭足以發之，得薦事。
考試官教授蔣批：取經史格言，用發古人之心，出詞不費而意足，良是策場法度。彼掇拾問目者可鑒矣。君其慎斯術以往。
有帝王為學之要，有帝王為學之本。夫人主之學係天下之治忽，而人主之心關治忽之本原。學矣而無其要，則用心於泛，而不知所以為治之資；要矣而無所本，則溺意於外，而不知所以出治之原。故人君之學，莫病於泛，而經史其要也；莫病於外，而心術其本也。知此，則可以識先儒著論之意、臣工勸講之心，而為明問復矣。今夫六經皆所以載道，而道之存主者意也。意有
translation_en:
…precisely accords with the intent of the two ministers in offering encouragement and counsel. The concluding discussion of the agreement between the Rites of Zhou and the Spring and Autumn Annals also allows one to gauge your learning in the classics and histories.

Examiner He, Instructor, comments: Everyone knows Master Luo’s words, but few understand that the essential purport of his argument lies in rectifying the ruler’s mind, thereby furnishing Confucian ministers with resources for encouragement and counsel. This policy essay grounds its argument in evidence, and its language adequately develops that argument. It merits recommendation [?].

Examiner Jiang, Professor, comments: You draw on exemplary sayings from the classics and histories to bring out the minds of the ancients. Your language is economical yet conveys the full meaning: this is indeed the proper method for policy essays in the examination hall. Those who merely pick up scraps from the questions should take this as a lesson. Carefully adhere to this method as you proceed.

There are essentials to imperial learning, and there is a foundation to imperial learning. The ruler’s learning bears upon order and disorder throughout the realm, while the ruler’s mind concerns their very source. If he studies without grasping the essentials, he applies his mind too diffusely and does not understand what supplies the resources for governing. If he grasps the essentials but has no foundation, he becomes absorbed in externals and does not understand the source from which good government proceeds. Thus, nothing is more detrimental to a ruler’s learning than diffuseness, and the classics and histories are its essentials; nothing is more detrimental than absorption in externals, and the cultivation of the mind is its foundation. Understanding this, one can recognize the intent with which earlier Confucian scholars composed their discussions and the purpose with which ministers offered counsel and instruction, and thus respond to your illuminating question. Now, the Six Classics all serve to convey the Way, and it is in intention that the Way resides and is sustained. Within intention there are…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
理欲善惡之分人主於是反之躬行之著
而謹諸念慮之微固讀經之大法也諸史
皆所以載事而事之鋪陳者迹也迹有安
危治亂之殊人主於此考其得失之異而
存夫鑒戒之心固讀史之大法也然而六
經之中尚書所載論人主善惡爲多今觀
其頌成湯聖知仁勇之錫醜夏德矯誣簡
附之行三風十愆反復乎懲惡之戒遜志
時敏丁寧乎樂善之規其要歸於使人鑒
===
善惡以正心焉爾人主讀經以是爲先則
六經可推類而次舉矣諸史之中唐書所
載論朝廷變故最盛今觀其叙家法雜夷
之非詳宮闈亂政之失君子小人之進退
見君德之盛衰藩鎮夷狄之强弱驗朝政
之得失其要歸於使人視變故以知謹焉
爾人主讀史以是爲先則諸史可循序而
徧及矣昔孫奭爲侍講掇取說命三篇爲
經筵進講之資者是時真宗漸有侈大之
punctuated: 理欲善惡之分。人主於是反之躬行之著，而謹諸念慮之微，固讀經之大法也。諸史皆所以載事，而事之鋪陳者迹也。迹有安危治亂之殊，人主於此考其得失之異，而存夫鑒戒之心，固讀史之大法也。然而六經之中，《尚書》所載，論人主善惡爲多。今觀其頌成湯聖知仁勇之錫，醜夏德矯誣簡附之行，三風十愆反復乎懲惡之戒，遜志時敏丁寧乎樂善之規，其要歸於使人鑒善惡以正心焉爾。人主讀經以是爲先，則六經可推類而次舉矣。諸史之中，《唐書》所載，論朝廷變故最盛。今觀其叙家法雜夷之非，詳宮闈亂政之失，君子小人之進退見君德之盛衰，藩鎮夷狄之强弱驗朝政之得失，其要歸於使人視變故以知謹焉爾。人主讀史以是爲先，則諸史可循序而徧及矣。昔孫奭爲侍講，掇取《說命》三篇爲經筵進講之資者，是時真宗漸有侈大之
translation_en:
…the distinction between principle and desire, good and evil. The ruler should therefore examine these in the manifest conduct of his own person and exercise care over the subtlest movements of his thoughts. This is indeed the fundamental method of reading the Classics. The histories all record events, and events are set forth through the traces they leave. These traces distinguish security from peril and order from disorder. The ruler should examine the differences between successes and failures and preserve a disposition to draw lessons and take warning. This is indeed the fundamental method of reading history.

Among the Six Classics, however, the Book of Documents devotes much of its contents to discussing good and evil in rulers. Consider how it praises the sage wisdom, benevolence, and courage bestowed upon Cheng Tang, and condemns the conduct of the Xia ruler: deception, false claims, slighting the worthy, and attaching himself to the powerful. Its treatment of the three pernicious customs and ten faults repeatedly warns against evil; its injunction to be humble in purpose and constantly diligent earnestly teaches delight in goodness. Its essential aim is simply to lead people to discern good and evil and thereby rectify their minds. If the ruler gives this book priority in reading the Classics, he can extend its lessons by analogy and take up the Six Classics in turn.

Among the histories, the Book of Tang is especially rich in accounts of upheavals at court. Consider how it recounts the faults of a ruling house whose traditions mingled with those of foreign peoples, and details the failings through which the palace quarters disrupted government. The advancement and dismissal of gentlemen and petty men reveal the flourishing or decline of the ruler’s virtue; the strength or weakness of regional military governors and foreign peoples tests the successes and failures of court government. Its essential aim is simply to lead people to observe upheavals and learn caution. If the ruler gives this book priority in reading history, he can proceed in order and eventually encompass all the histories.

Formerly, when Sun Shi served as Expositor-in-waiting, he selected the three chapters of “The Charge to Yue” as material for lectures at the Classics Colloquium. At that time, Emperor Zhenzong was gradually developing an inclination toward extravagance and grandeur…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
心爽蓋欲因說命以諷諫之耳使讀說命
所謂黷祀弗欽之訓則有以警夫天書之
祟干戈省躬之言則有以中夫親征之病
況其他格言無不有資治道者乎爽之意
急於正君亦羅氏著論之意也范祖禹爲
學士編集唐鑑一書爲深宮燕閒之覽者
是時哲宗方當幼冲之年祖禹蓋欲因唐
鑑以勸戒之爾使讀唐鑑所論九齡陸贄
之罷則知正人之去留不可不謹稅法兵
===
政之變則知舊章之紛更不可不慎況其
他行事無不有關治理者乎祖禹之心切
於正君亦羅氏立言之心也乃若林佑事
德宗於豐大之日彙集周禮名曰正典而
係之以衆論焉蓋是時德宗之心荒於欲
佑以周官節約之法戒之誠當世之通典
也而尚書之內亦有周官之法度焉無不
同矣胡安國事高宗於恢復之時進解春
秋名曰傳義而斷之以己意焉蓋是時高
punctuated: 心。爽蓋欲因《說命》以諷諫之耳。使讀《說命》所謂「黷祀弗欽」之訓，則有以警夫天書之祟；「干戈省躬」之言，則有以中夫親征之病。況其他格言，無不有資治道者乎？爽之意急於正君，亦羅氏著論之意也。范祖禹爲學士，編集《唐鑑》一書，爲深宮燕閒之覽者，是時哲宗方當幼冲之年，祖禹蓋欲因《唐鑑》以勸戒之爾。使讀《唐鑑》所論九齡、陸贄之罷，則知正人之去留不可不謹；稅法、兵政之變，則知舊章之紛更不可不慎。況其他行事，無不有關治理者乎？祖禹之心切於正君，亦羅氏立言之心也。乃若林佑事德宗於豐大之日，彙集《周禮》，名曰《正典》，而係之以衆論焉。蓋是時德宗之心荒於欲，佑以《周官》節約之法戒之，誠當世之《通典》也。而《尚書》之內，亦有《周官》之法度焉，無不同矣。胡安國事高宗於恢復之時，進解《春秋》，名曰《傳義》，而斷之以己意焉。蓋是時高
translation_en:
…such inclinations. Shuang [?; apparently Sun Shi, mentioned on the preceding page] presumably wished only to remonstrate indirectly with him through the “Charge to Yue.” If he read its admonition that “excessive sacrifices are irreverent,” this could alert him to the pernicious influence of the heavenly writings; its words about “weapons and armor” and “examining oneself” could strike at the fault of personally leading a military expedition. How much more was this true of its other exemplary sayings, all of which could aid the art of government! Shuang’s urgent desire to rectify his ruler was also Master Luo’s intention in composing his discourse.

When Fan Zuyu served as Academician, he compiled the Mirror of the Tang for the emperor to read at leisure in the inner palace. Emperor Zhezong was then still a child, and Zuyu presumably wished only to encourage and admonish him through the Mirror of the Tang. Reading its discussions of the dismissal of Jiuling and Lu Zhi would teach him that the retention or removal of upright men required care; reading about changes in taxation and military administration would teach him that established institutions must not be altered indiscriminately. How much more was this true of the other deeds it recorded, all of which bore upon good government! Zuyu’s earnest desire to rectify his ruler was also the purpose behind Master Luo’s words.

As for Lin You [?], who served Emperor Dezong in a time of prosperity and expansion, he compiled material from the Rites of Zhou, entitled it the Correct Compendium [?], and appended various discussions to it. At that time Dezong’s mind was lost in desires, and You admonished him through the principles of restraint and economy in the Offices of Zhou. This was indeed a Comprehensive Compendium suited to that age. Yet the Book of Documents also contains the rules and institutions of the Offices of Zhou: in this respect they are entirely alike.

Hu Anguo served Emperor Gaozong during the effort to restore the dynasty. He presented an interpretation of the Spring and Autumn Annals, entitled Commentary on Its Meaning, making judgments according to his own understanding. For at that time, Gao…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
宗之志忘乎警安國以春秋討賊之義導
之誠嘗時之春秋也而唐鑑之中亦有春
秋之意義焉無不合矣是知經史爲人君
進學之要雖其論學不同而同歸于正心
之旨臣工爲人君進學之助雖其勸講不
同而同歸于正君之心也雖然人君進學
固資經史矣使非有心體力行之功則雖
手不釋卷亦徒事乎虛文人臣勸學固用
經史矣使非其養望積誠之素則雖日侍
===
經筵亦徒應乎故事此蓋孟子責難陳善
之本心而朱子誠意正心之實學也愚生
不敏竊有志焉他日倘快利見之覩則豈
敢遂忘芹曝之忠哉
第三問
邢淳
同考試官訓導余　批〔詳考古人立論之異而以理斷之鋪叙之間高下如辨蒼素蓋不徒爲〕
勦說者也
punctuated:
宗之志忘乎警，安國以春秋討賊之義導之，誠嘗時之春秋也。而唐鑑之中亦有春秋之意義焉，無不合矣。是知經史爲人君進學之要，雖其論學不同，而同歸于正心之旨；臣工爲人君進學之助，雖其勸講不同，而同歸于正君之心也。雖然，人君進學固資經史矣，使非有心體力行之功，則雖手不釋卷，亦徒事乎虛文；人臣勸學固用經史矣，使非其養望積誠之素，則雖日侍經筵，亦徒應乎故事。此蓋孟子責難陳善之本心，而朱子誠意正心之實學也。愚生不敏，竊有志焉。他日倘快利見之覩，則豈敢遂忘芹曝之忠哉！

第三問
邢淳

同考試官訓導余　批〔詳考古人立論之異，而以理斷之。鋪叙之間，高下如辨蒼素，蓋不徒爲〕勦說者也。
translation_en:
…Gaozong had lost his vigilance, and An’guo guided him with the principle of punishing rebels set forth in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His work was truly the Spring and Autumn Annals of its time [?]. Moreover, the Mirror of the Tang also contains the meanings and principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals: the two accord in every respect. Thus we know that the classics and histories are essential to a ruler’s advancement in learning. Although their discussions of learning differ, they share the purpose of rectifying the mind. Officials assist the ruler’s advancement in learning; although their exhortations and lectures differ, they share the intention of rectifying the ruler’s mind.

Nevertheless, although a ruler must draw upon the classics and histories to advance his learning, without the effort of inwardly grasping their teachings and diligently putting them into practice, even never setting down his books would amount merely to empty literary formalities. Although ministers must use the classics and histories to encourage learning, without a longstanding foundation of cultivated standing and accumulated sincerity, even daily attendance at the Classics Colloquium would amount merely to observing established routine. This, indeed, is Mencius’s original intention in demanding difficult achievements of the ruler and setting goodness before him, and Master Zhu’s practical learning of making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind. Though I, an unworthy student, am slow of understanding, I privately aspire to this. If some day I should enjoy the good fortune of an audience with the sovereign, how could I dare forget the loyal wish to offer even such humble gifts as celery and the sun’s warmth?

Third Question
Xing Chun

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor: “He carefully examines the differences among the arguments of the ancients and judges them according to principle. In his exposition, distinctions of higher and lower merit are as clear as those between dark and white. He is certainly not merely a compiler of borrowed opinions.”

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭何　批　就事論事之文非獨難
於記憶且易失之軒輕之間此策條整詳明中
有餘度策場不當如是耶
考試官教授蔣　批　第士正以觀其博洽之
學斷制之才古之議論今之行事也其是非利
害亦有先儒所未論論而未允於時宜者此篇
敷辨詳明中理而知幾殆酌古準今之學歟
善持天下之議者必明天下之理而審天
下之勢焉夫理之在天下一而已矣理雖
===
一定而事物之變無窮變者勢也不變者
理也明理以求其當審勢以會其幾持此
以議天下之事則邦國之是以定而群言
之非以息矣非善持議者能之乎愚嘗讀
子史見古人留心治道者或平居有見形
之議論以垂訓或臨事有謀折衷群言以
濟時槩得明理審勢之道焉以平居論建
者言之若胡五峯以封建為公天下之大
端蓋以聖人之心以義處利而能均天下
punctuated:
考試官教諭何批：就事論事之文，非獨難於記憶，且易失之軒輕之間。此策條整詳明，中有餘度，策場不當如是耶？

考試官教授蔣批：第士正以觀其博洽之學、斷制之才。古之議論，今之行事也。其是非利害，亦有先儒所未論、論而未允於時宜者。此篇敷辨詳明，中理而知幾，殆酌古準今之學歟？

善持天下之議者，必明天下之理，而審天下之勢焉。夫理之在天下，一而已矣。理雖一定，而事物之變無窮。變者，勢也；不變者，理也。明理以求其當，審勢以會其幾，持此以議天下之事，則邦國之是以定，而群言之非以息矣。非善持議者能之乎？愚嘗讀子史，見古人留心治道者，或平居有見，形之議論以垂訓；或臨事有謀，折衷群言以濟時，槩得明理審勢之道焉。以平居論建者言之，若胡五峯以封建為公天下之大端，蓋以聖人之心，以義處利，而能均天下
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: Writing that discusses matters on their own terms not only makes considerable demands on memory, but also readily errs in assigning greater or lesser weight [?]. This policy essay is orderly, detailed, and clear, with judgment to spare. Should not work in the policy examination be like this?

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: Ranking candidates serves precisely to assess the breadth and thoroughness of their learning and their ability to judge and decide. What the ancients discussed concerns what we put into practice today. Among the questions of right and wrong, benefit and harm involved, some were never discussed by earlier Confucian scholars; others they discussed without adequately addressing the needs of the times. This essay expounds and discriminates in detail and with clarity, accords with principle, and recognizes the incipient signs of change. Is this not learning that weighs antiquity against the circumstances of the present?

Those adept at deliberating on the affairs of the realm must understand its principles and carefully assess its circumstances. Principle throughout the world is one, and nothing more. Although principle is fixed, the changes in affairs and things are inexhaustible. What changes is circumstance; what does not change is principle. Understand principle to seek what is appropriate; assess circumstances to grasp the incipient signs of change. Apply these to deliberations on the affairs of the realm, and what is right for the state will be established, while the errors of competing opinions will subside. Could anyone who is not adept at deliberation accomplish this? In my humble reading of the philosophical masters and the histories, I have seen that the ancients who devoted themselves to the way of governance sometimes gained insights in ordinary life and expressed them in discussions to leave instruction for posterity; sometimes, when confronted with affairs, they devised plans and adjudicated among competing opinions to meet the needs of their times. In general, they grasped the way of understanding principle and assessing circumstances. To speak of those who advanced proposals in ordinary life: Hu Wufeng regarded the establishment of hereditary fiefs as a fundamental means of making the realm common to all. This was because, with the mind of a sage, one handles material benefits according to righteousness and can distribute equitably throughout the realm …

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
之施也柳宗元謂封建非聖人之本意蓋
謂歷代之與所與共事而勢有不可去也
胡氏則深得聖人封建之心而宗元則止
見末世封建之弊二者固不可同日而語
矣朱晦庵謂井田之行須於亂世之後蓋
以人物鮮少可免奪富之嫌也張橫渠則
謂處之有術不刑一人而可服蓋以裁酌
得宜可行分田之政也二者固並行而不
悖矣漢文帝因緹縈之請代肉刑以笞法
===
固人君好生之仁也然未見勝殘之化而
已啓人易犯之心陳季雅論之是矣漢史
之美蓋未知先王以義制辟之意焉唐玄
宗從張說之議易府兵以宿衛固恤兵之
仁也然未免石壕之苦而已致兵農之分
范祖禹譏之當矣唐史之論蓋未知先王
容民畜衆之意焉程子謂行禮不可泥古
須視時之風氣蓋欲禮順人情者也周子
謂不復古禮則鮮能至治蓋欲以禮爲治
punctuated: 之施也。柳宗元謂封建非聖人之本意，蓋謂歷代之與所與共事，而勢有不可去也。胡氏則深得聖人封建之心，而宗元則止見末世封建之弊，二者固不可同日而語矣。朱晦庵謂井田之行須於亂世之後，蓋以人物鮮少，可免奪富之嫌也。張橫渠則謂處之有術，不刑一人而可服，蓋以裁酌得宜，可行分田之政也。二者固並行而不悖矣。漢文帝因緹縈之請，代肉刑以笞法，固人君好生之仁也。然未見勝殘之化，而已啓人易犯之心，陳季雅論之是矣。漢史之美，蓋未知先王以義制辟之意焉。唐玄宗從張說之議，易府兵以宿衛，固恤兵之仁也。然未免石壕之苦，而已致兵農之分，范祖禹譏之當矣。唐史之論，蓋未知先王容民畜衆之意焉。程子謂行禮不可泥古，須視時之風氣，蓋欲禮順人情者也。周子謂不復古禮，則鮮能至治，蓋欲以禮爲治
translation_en:
…in the distribution of benefits. Liu Zongyuan held that enfeoffment was not the sages’ original intention. His point was that successive dynasties and those with whom they shared the work of government [?] faced circumstances in which it could not be abolished. Master Hu thus deeply understood the sages’ intention in establishing enfeoffment, whereas Zongyuan saw only its abuses in later ages. The two certainly cannot be spoken of on equal terms.

Zhu Hui’an held that the well-field system could be implemented only after an age of disorder: with people and resources scarce, one could avoid the suspicion of dispossessing the rich. Zhang Hengqu, however, held that, with proper methods, one could secure compliance without punishing a single person: with suitably measured arrangements, a policy of distributing land could be implemented. These two views can certainly be followed together without contradiction.

Emperor Wen of Han, responding to Tiying’s petition, replaced mutilating punishments with beating. This was indeed a ruler’s benevolence in cherishing life. Yet before any transforming influence that overcame cruelty became evident, it had already encouraged people to offend more readily. Chen Jiya’s discussion of this was correct. The praise offered by the History of Han shows a failure to understand the former kings’ intention in determining punishments according to righteousness.

Emperor Xuanzong of Tang followed Zhang Yue’s proposal and replaced the militia system with palace guard troops. This was indeed benevolence in showing concern for soldiers. Yet it failed to avert suffering such as that at Shihao, while already bringing about the separation of soldiers from farmers. Fan Zuyu’s criticism was appropriate. The judgment of the History of Tang shows a failure to understand the former kings’ intention to embrace the people and nurture the multitude.

Master Cheng held that, in practicing ritual, one must not adhere rigidly to antiquity but must consider the prevailing customs of the time. His aim was for ritual to accord with human feelings. Master Zhou held that, without restoring ancient ritual, one could seldom attain perfect governance. His aim was to govern through ritual…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
者也要之程子欲酌古而行於今周子因
傷今而思乎古時則各有感而言者焉朱
子創貢舉之私議經書子史分年以試而
預示於其初呂與叔奏立取士之四科德
行明經文學政事而各試其一要之朱子
意在斟酌時王之制呂氏意欲盡行古人
之法論則各有為而發者焉此皆議之平
居者然非持理審勢之人未免失之偏見
矣而豈可為訓乎以臨事發謀者言之漢
===
世匈奴遠塞王恢欲誘致襲擊蓋啓釁招
侮之道而徒設馬邑之詐然能用韓安國
之議則和親不絕而邊塞可無虞焉其後
罕开合兵入寇趙充國請留田圖策盡以
全取勝之謀也而坐致先零之弊使用辛
武賢之言則羌虜不可擊而中國已先弊
焉宣帝議待單于之儀位諸侯王下丞相
御史之言禮之中也蕭望之欲以不臣待
之豈不亂夷夏之大分乎光宗欲祧僖宣
punctuated: 者也。要之，程子欲酌古而行於今，周子因傷今而思乎古，時則各有感而言者焉。朱子創貢舉之私議，經書子史分年以試，而預示於其初；呂與叔奏立取士之四科，德行、明經、文學、政事，而各試其一。要之，朱子意在斟酌時王之制，呂氏意欲盡行古人之法，論則各有為而發者焉。此皆議之平居者，然非持理審勢之人，未免失之偏見矣，而豈可為訓乎？以臨事發謀者言之，漢世匈奴遠塞，王恢欲誘致襲擊，蓋啓釁招侮之道，而徒設馬邑之詐；然能用韓安國之議，則和親不絕，而邊塞可無虞焉。其後罕开合兵入寇，趙充國請留田，圖策盡以全取勝之謀也，而坐致先零之弊；使用辛武賢之言，則羌虜不可擊，而中國已先弊焉。宣帝議待單于之儀，位諸侯王下，丞相、御史之言，禮之中也；蕭望之欲以不臣待之，豈不亂夷夏之大分乎？光宗欲祧僖宣
translation_en:
…those who wished to govern through ritual. In essence, Master Cheng wished to weigh ancient practices and apply them in the present, while Master Zhou, distressed by the present, looked back to antiquity. Each spoke in response to particular concerns of his time. Master Zhu put forward his personal proposals on recruitment by examination: the classics, philosophical writings, and histories would be examined in different years, with advance notice given at the outset. Lü Yushu memorialized proposing four categories for selecting officials—virtuous conduct, mastery of the classics, literary learning, and administrative affairs—with each candidate examined in one category. In essence, Master Zhu intended to make considered adjustments to the reigning sovereign’s institutions, while Lü intended to implement ancient methods in full. Each argument arose for a particular purpose. These were all proposals discussed in ordinary circumstances. Yet anyone who did not uphold principle and carefully assess circumstances would inevitably fall into partial views. How could such views serve as authoritative guidance?
Turning to plans proposed in response to events: under the Han, the Xiongnu were far beyond the frontier, and Wang Hui wished to lure them in and launch a surprise attack. This was a way to provoke conflict and invite affronts, and he merely contrived the deception at Mayi. Had Han Anguo’s proposal been adopted, marriage-based peace relations would have continued uninterrupted, and the frontier could have remained free from anxiety. Later, when the Han and Kai [?] joined forces and invaded, Zhao Chongguo requested that troops remain to farm. His plans were entirely directed toward achieving victory while preserving his forces, and he brought the Xianling to exhaustion without advancing to battle. Had Xin Wuxian’s advice been followed, the Qiang enemy could not have been struck effectively, while China itself would already have been exhausted.
When Emperor Xuan discussed the ceremonial treatment of the chanyu, the proposal of the Chancellor and the Imperial Counselor to rank him below the enfeoffed kings accorded with the proper measure of ritual. Xiao Wangzhi wished to treat him as someone who was not a subject: would this not have confused the fundamental distinction between the non-Chinese and the Chinese? Emperor Guangzong wished to remove the ancestral tablets of Xi and Xuan from their places in the ancestral temple…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
之主百世不遷侍講朱熹之言禮之正也
趙汝愚乃以私意欲之豈不拂天下之公
論乎靈州之議輔臣之言是也而李沆楊
億之論爲非馬綏州之議孫全照之言是
也而洪湛之論爲非馬誠以靈州不可城
綏州不可守也夏人之伐當從孫固之諫
种諤李憲伐之而五路之師潰矣遼人之
征當信种師道之言童貫征之而宋遼之
好絶矣誠以夏無可伐之機而遼非可征
===
之時也此皆發之臨事者然非據理觀變
之人未免失之私意矣而豈可爲用乎是
知人品有高下之殊而意見有得失之異
數子之内若朱子者則明聖賢大學之道
得義理中正之歸持論之正知言之精莫
有過者豈非後學之依歸者乎雖然窮養
而後達施理明而後議正學者果能如程
明道以聖人之道爲心范希文以天下之
重自任則何患乎時而無格言至論臨事
punctuated: 之主，百世不遷，侍講朱熹之言，禮之正也。趙汝愚乃以私意欲之，豈不拂天下之公論乎？靈州之議，輔臣之言是也，而李沆、楊億之論爲非馬？綏州之議，孫全照之言是也，而洪湛之論爲非馬？誠以靈州不可城，綏州不可守也。夏人之伐，當從孫固之諫；种諤、李憲伐之，而五路之師潰矣。遼人之征，當信种師道之言；童貫征之，而宋遼之好絶矣。誠以夏無可伐之機，而遼非可征之時也。此皆發之臨事者，然非據理觀變之人，未免失之私意矣，而豈可爲用乎？是知人品有高下之殊，而意見有得失之異。數子之内，若朱子者，則明聖賢大學之道，得義理中正之歸，持論之正、知言之精，莫有過者，豈非後學之依歸者乎？雖然，窮養而後達施，理明而後議正。學者果能如程明道以聖人之道爲心，范希文以天下之重自任，則何患乎時而無格言至論，臨事
translation_en:
…their spirit tablets should remain unmoved for a hundred generations: these words of Zhu Xi, the Expositor-in-waiting, accorded with correct ritual. Yet Zhao Ruyu wished to do this out of personal motives. Did this not run counter to the impartial judgment of all under Heaven? In the deliberations concerning Lingzhou, were the chief ministers’ words right, and the arguments of Li Hang and Yang Yi wrong [?]? In the deliberations concerning Suizhou, were Sun Quanzhao’s words right, and Hong Zhan’s argument wrong [?]? Indeed, Lingzhou could not be fortified, and Suizhou could not be held. In attacking the Xia, Sun Gu’s remonstrance should have been heeded; Zhong E and Li Xian attacked them, and the armies advancing along five routes collapsed. In campaigning against the Liao, Zhong Shidao’s words should have been trusted; Tong Guan campaigned against them, and the friendly relations between Song and Liao were severed. Indeed, there was no suitable opportunity to attack the Xia, and it was not the right time to campaign against the Liao.

These opinions were all expressed when confronting particular affairs. Yet those who do not ground themselves in principle and examine changing circumstances inevitably err through personal bias. How could their opinions be put to use? From this we know that people differ in the quality of their character, and that their opinions differ in being sound or mistaken. Among these men, Master Zhu understood the sages’ and worthies’ Way of the Great Learning and grasped the balanced and correct purport of moral principle. None surpassed him in the correctness of his arguments or the acuity of his discernment of others’ words. Was he not a guide for later students?

Nevertheless, one must cultivate oneself in obscurity before putting one’s learning into practice upon attaining office; one’s understanding of principle must be clear before one’s judgments can be correct. If students can truly take the sages’ Way to heart as Cheng Mingdao did, and assume responsibility for the weighty affairs of all under Heaven as Fan Xiwen did, why need they worry that their times will lack exemplary sayings and consummate judgments, or that, when confronting affairs …

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
而無善謀善斷也哉不然則雖或有偶中
焉者而亦不過暗合而已況又未必能中
也邪
第四問
王化
同考試官訓導張　批〔任人任法一策塲中類補綴成章支離不當人意求其議論斷制爲〕
〔古人捄弊者僅見此篇秋闈之冠端屬子矣〕
考試官教諭何　批〔初中塲得卷疑爲佳士上〕
〔晚見此策於󠄀泛中步驟典實評品精確讀之〕
===
〔令人爽然信乎爲佳士矣〕
考試官教授蔣　批〔任人任法裒以得人善〕
〔法歸之不窘逸於問目昌辭偉辯備蘇軾之論〕
〔所未備者其有用之文矣夫〕
用人以立政而患不能得其人持法以濟
時而患不能善其法盖得其人則寄託有
所資善其法則維持有所賴也不然則專
恣之釁作而拘畏之患生矣是豈有國者
punctuated:
而無善謀善斷也哉？不然，則雖或有偶中焉者，而亦不過暗合而已，況又未必能中也邪？

第四問
王化
同考試官訓導張　批〔任人任法一策，塲中類補綴成章，支離不當人意。求其議論斷制爲古人捄弊者，僅見此篇。秋闈之冠，端屬子矣。〕
考試官教諭何　批〔初中塲得卷，疑爲佳士，上晚見此策，於󠄀泛中步驟典實，評品精確，讀之令人爽然。信乎爲佳士矣！〕
考試官教授蔣　批〔任人任法，裒以得人善法歸之，不窘逸於問目。昌辭偉辯，備蘇軾之論所未備者，其有用之文矣夫！〕

用人以立政，而患不能得其人；持法以濟時，而患不能善其法。盖得其人，則寄託有所資；善其法，則維持有所賴也。不然，則專恣之釁作，而拘畏之患生矣。是豈有國者
translation_en:
…and lack sound plans and sound judgment when confronted with affairs? Otherwise, even if one occasionally hits the mark, this amounts merely to an accidental correspondence. How much less, then, can one be certain of hitting it!

Fourth Question
Wang Hua

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: 〔In the policy essays on relying on men and relying on laws, the candidates generally patched material together into compositions that were disjointed and unsatisfactory. Among essays whose arguments and judgments would remedy the failings of the ancients, I have seen only this one. First place in the autumn Provincial Examination assuredly belongs to you!〕

Comment by Examiner He, Instructor: 〔When I first received your script in the middle session [?], I suspected you were a man of talent. Later, on seeing this policy essay [?], I found that, amid its broad-ranging discussion, its exposition was grounded in authoritative learning and solid substance, and its assessments were precise. Reading it leaves one refreshed. You are indeed a man of talent!〕

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Professor: 〔On relying on men and relying on laws, you bring the discussion together and resolve it in finding the right men and making laws sound. You are neither constrained by the question nor stray beyond it [?]. Your splendid language and magnificent argument supply what Su Shi’s discourse left unsaid. Surely this is writing of practical use!〕

In employing men to establish government, the concern is that one may fail to find the right men; in upholding laws to meet the needs of the times, the concern is that one may fail to make those laws sound. For when the right men are found, there is a foundation for entrusting responsibilities; when laws are sound, there is something upon which the maintenance of order can depend. Otherwise, opportunities for arbitrary conduct arise, and the troubles caused by constraint and fear emerge. How could this, for those who rule a state…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
之利也哉此任人任法之難在古爲然而
執事下詢之意亦固患乎此也請述所聞
以對夫用人立政人國所當任矣任匪其
人則威柄移於小人而人始有不可任之
說焉立法濟時法固所當用矣任非其法
則政事壞於紛更而法始有不可任之說
焉以其任人者言之漢武帝任田蚡爲丞
相霍光爲大將軍均有心腹之寄也蚡以
驕侈之資竊威福之柄奏語至移日之久
===
薦人至二千石之貴此小人負權者之所
爲也光出入禁闥小心謹畏觀其擁昭立
宣有功社稷誠不孤大事之託者焉唐德
宗任崔祐甫爲門下侍郎陸贄爲中書侍
郎俱有股肱之託也祐甫見人才之壅滯
欲時望之畢收作相未二百日之久除官
至八百員之多此矯枉者之所爲也贄矢
心論議共濟時艱觀其論諫百篇皆本仁
義誠不負天子之知者焉宋神宗委心以
punctuated: 之利也哉？此任人任法之難，在古爲然，而執事下詢之意，亦固患乎此也。請述所聞以對。夫用人立政，人國所當任矣；任匪其人，則威柄移於小人，而人始有不可任之說焉。立法濟時，法固所當用矣；任非其法，則政事壞於紛更，而法始有不可任之說焉。以其任人者言之，漢武帝任田蚡爲丞相、霍光爲大將軍，均有心腹之寄也。蚡以驕侈之資，竊威福之柄，奏語至移日之久，薦人至二千石之貴，此小人負權者之所爲也。光出入禁闥，小心謹畏，觀其擁昭立宣，有功社稷，誠不孤大事之託者焉。唐德宗任崔祐甫爲門下侍郎、陸贄爲中書侍郎，俱有股肱之託也。祐甫見人才之壅滯，欲時望之畢收，作相未二百日之久，除官至八百員之多，此矯枉者之所爲也。贄矢心論議，共濟時艱，觀其論諫百篇，皆本仁義，誠不負天子之知者焉。宋神宗委心以
translation_en:
…be to the advantage of one who rules a state? Such was the difficulty of relying on men and relying on laws in antiquity; your purpose in condescending to inquire is surely likewise prompted by concern about this. Allow me to state what I have learned in reply.

When employing men to establish good government, men are indeed what one must rely upon [?]. But if those entrusted are unsuitable, the power of command passes to petty men, and people begin to say that men cannot be relied upon. When establishing laws to meet the needs of the times, laws are certainly what one must employ. But if the laws relied upon are unsuitable, governmental affairs are ruined by disorderly changes, and people begin to say that laws cannot be relied upon.

Consider reliance on men. Emperor Wu of Han appointed Tian Fen as Counselor-in-Chief and Huo Guang as General-in-Chief, entrusting both as his closest confidants. Arrogant and extravagant by nature, Tian Fen usurped the power to punish and reward. His presentations to the throne could last until the day had shifted, and those he recommended attained offices as exalted as the two-thousand-bushel rank. Such was the conduct of a petty man wielding power. Huo Guang entered and left the palace precincts with care, circumspection, and reverence. Consider how he supported Emperor Zhao and enthroned Emperor Xuan, rendering service to the state: he truly did not betray the trust placed in him concerning its great affairs.

Emperor Dezong of Tang appointed Cui Youfu as Vice Director of the Chancellery and Lu Zhi as Vice Director of the Secretariat, entrusting both as his indispensable aides. Seeing that talented men were blocked from advancement, Cui Youfu wished to recruit all those of established reputation in his day. In fewer than two hundred days as chief minister, he appointed as many as eight hundred officials. Such was the conduct of one seeking to correct an abuse. Lu Zhi devoted himself wholeheartedly to deliberation, helping to overcome the difficulties of the times. Consider his hundred essays of counsel and remonstrance: all were grounded in benevolence and righteousness. He truly did not disappoint the Son of Heaven’s recognition of his worth. Emperor Shenzong of Song placed his wholehearted trust in…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
任王安石可謂得君行政矣而安石乃汲
汲以富強爲務取祖宗之舊章而盡紛更
之寧不有負其君乎兩宮虛己以聽司馬
光可謂言聽計行矣而光能毅然以天下
自任取新法之害民者而盡剗革之寧非
有功於時乎是數者均之任人之專也任
得其人則善非其人則其弊也始有請謁
公行私邪黨盛如蘇軾之所論者焉以其
任法者言之蕭何曹參漢之良相也何定
===
律令而參以畫一守之當時承暴秦之後
二人所尚寬簡宜海內之民戴其清靜也
夫何張湯之用改諸律令務在深文而卒
成虛耗之風張湯豈得爲無責乎姚崇宋
璟唐之賢相也崇善應變而璟以守文輔
之當時值開元之盛二人同心輔佐宜天
下之民興於富庶也夫何裴光庭之相奏
諸選人俱用資格而聖書之稱宋景豈得
以無言乎章惇呂惠卿之進王安石引之
punctuated:
任王安石，可謂得君行政矣。而安石乃汲汲以富強爲務，取祖宗之舊章而盡紛更之，寧不有負其君乎？兩宮虛己以聽司馬光，可謂言聽計行矣。而光能毅然以天下自任，取新法之害民者而盡剗革之，寧非有功於時乎？是數者，均之任人之專也。任得其人則善，非其人則其弊也，始有請謁公行、私邪黨盛，如蘇軾之所論者焉。
以其任法者言之，蕭何、曹參，漢之良相也。何定律令，而參以畫一守之。當時承暴秦之後，二人所尚寬簡，宜海內之民戴其清靜也。夫何張湯之用，改諸律令，務在深文，而卒成虛耗之風，張湯豈得爲無責乎？姚崇、宋璟，唐之賢相也。崇善應變，而璟以守文輔之。當時值開元之盛，二人同心輔佐，宜天下之民興於富庶也。夫何裴光庭之相，奏諸選人俱用資格，而聖書之稱，宋景豈得以無言乎？章惇、呂惠卿之進，王安石引之
translation_en:
…entrusted Wang Anshi with office: Wang could indeed be said to have enjoyed his ruler’s confidence in conducting government. Yet Anshi busied himself with making the state wealthy and powerful, taking the established institutions of the imperial ancestors and changing them all indiscriminately. Did he not thereby fail his ruler? The two palaces humbly listened to Sima Guang: his words were indeed heeded and his plans carried out. Guang resolutely took responsibility for the realm, eliminating every one of the New Policies that harmed the people. Did he not render meritorious service to his age? These cases all exemplify exclusive reliance on particular men. If the right man is entrusted with responsibility, the result is good; if the wrong man, abuses arise. Then solicitation of favors proceeds openly, and factions of self-serving, corrupt men flourish, just as Su Shi argued.
As for reliance on laws, Xiao He and Cao Can were worthy chief ministers of the Han. He established the statutes and ordinances, and Can maintained them unchanged as a uniform system. Coming after the violent rule of Qin, both men valued leniency and simplicity. It was fitting that the people throughout the empire should cherish their tranquil government. Why, then, when Zhang Tang was employed, were the statutes and ordinances altered, with every effort directed toward harsh legal interpretation, ultimately bringing about a general state of depletion? Could Zhang Tang escape responsibility? Yao Chong and Song Jing were worthy chief ministers of the Tang. Chong excelled at responding to changing circumstances, while Jing complemented him by upholding established rules. During the flourishing Kaiyuan era, the two served together with one purpose. It was fitting that the people throughout the realm should prosper in wealth and numbers. Why, then, when Pei Guangting became chief minister, did he propose that all candidates for appointment be assessed by formal qualifications and seniority? And concerning the praise in the sage’s writings [?], could Song Jing remain without criticism? The advancement of Zhang Dun and Lü Huiqing came through Wang Anshi’s sponsorship…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
也多立黨與護持新法天下嚣然喪其樂
生之心故君子謂安石有流毒四海之罪
者此也蘇軾范純仁之用司馬光任之也
詳定役法條陳利害海內歡然甚於更生
之樂故君子謂光有旋乾轉坤之功者此
也是數者均之任法之專也任得其法則
善非其法則其弊也始有賢愚混滯僥倖
俗成如蘇軾之所論者焉是則任人之弊
吾不患其專恣而患不得其人任法之弊
===
吾不患其拘畏而患不得其法然則如之
何而可邪盖古之先王法不必煩惟其義
官不必備惟其人雖人法並任而任人為
多故凡法令科條雖設其大凡而操縱變
通之宜則付之人得其人則法無不善矣
如是則何專恣拘畏之患邪故曰有治人
無治法此固老生之常談而實為不易之
定論也惟執事裁之
第五問
punctuated:
也。多立黨與，護持新法，天下嚣然，喪其樂生之心。故君子謂安石有流毒四海之罪者，此也。蘇軾、范純仁之用，司馬光任之也。詳定役法，條陳利害，海內歡然，甚於更生之樂。故君子謂光有旋乾轉坤之功者，此也。是數者，均之任法之專也。任得其法則善，非其法則其弊也。始有賢愚混滯、僥倖俗成，如蘇軾之所論者焉。是則任人之弊，吾不患其專恣，而患不得其人；任法之弊，吾不患其拘畏，而患不得其法。然則如之何而可邪？盖古之先王，法不必煩，惟其義；官不必備，惟其人。雖人法並任，而任人為多。故凡法令科條，雖設其大凡，而操縱變通之宜，則付之人。得其人，則法無不善矣。如是，則何專恣拘畏之患邪？故曰：「有治人，無治法。」此固老生之常談，而實為不易之定論也。惟執事裁之。

第五問
translation_en:
… They gathered many partisans to uphold the New Policies, and all under Heaven clamored in discontent, losing their joy in life. This is why gentlemen say that Wang Anshi was guilty of spreading harm throughout the Four Seas. As for the employment of Su Shi and Fan Chunren, it was Sima Guang who entrusted them with office. They carefully settled the regulations for labor service and set out their benefits and drawbacks point by point. All within the seas rejoiced, with a joy greater even than that of receiving a new lease on life. This is why gentlemen say that Guang accomplished the feat of turning Heaven and Earth around.

These several cases alike involved exclusive reliance on laws. Such reliance is beneficial when the right laws are adopted; when they are not, abuses result. Then the worthy and foolish become indiscriminately mired together, and seeking advancement through lucky chances becomes customary, as Su Shi discussed. Thus, concerning the abuses of reliance on men, I do not fear their arbitrary self-indulgence, but rather the failure to obtain the right men. Concerning the abuses of reliance on laws, I do not fear constraint and timidity, but rather the failure to obtain the right laws.

What, then, should be done? The sage kings of antiquity did not require numerous laws, only that they be appropriate; nor did they require every office to be filled, only that the right men hold office. Though they relied on both men and laws, they relied more on men. Thus, while they laid down the broad outlines of laws, ordinances, and regulations, they entrusted to men the discretion to apply them strictly or leniently and adapt them to circumstances. With the right men, no law will fail to serve well. If this is so, what grounds are there to fear arbitrary self-indulgence or constraint and timidity? Hence the saying: “There are men who bring about good government; there are no laws that bring about good government.” This is admittedly the commonplace talk of old scholars, yet it is truly an unalterable conclusion. I respectfully submit it to your judgment.

Fifth Question

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
王勲
同考試官教授陳　批〔知人安民今日當務之急也子能考究斷制酌乎古而宜於今殆〕
〔非經生之腐者比矣高薦奚疑〕
考試官教諭何　批〔策問不著往事者欲答者自言之也士子於此多不暇及此獨參酌言之非〕
〔惟見其學之博亦可知其力之裕子固以是取子矣〕
考試官教授蔣　批〔特務一策條對詳整行之今日不無有補況他作稱是殆學之有用者乎〕
===
吏治當察在稽之於衆而審之於心民生
當安在體之以情而恤之以實夫吏司民
命是宜察矣然不稽之於衆未免自用不
廣不審之於心未免偏聽不公安能盡其
情僞乎民為邦本是宜安矣然不體之以
情未免處置失宜不恤之以實未免流離
失所安得遂其生全乎嗚呼此我
皇上所以屢下蠲逋賦復流移之詔節有訪賢
否備黜陟之命而委重於撫按之臣也夫
punctuated:
王勲

同考試官教授陳　批〔知人安民，今日當務之急也。子能考究斷制，酌乎古而宜於今，殆〕〔非經生之腐者比矣。高薦奚疑？〕

考試官教諭何　批〔策問不著往事者，欲答者自言之也。士子於此多不暇及，此獨參酌言之，非〕〔惟見其學之博，亦可知其力之裕。子固以是取子矣。〕

考試官教授蔣　批〔特務一策，條對詳整，行之今日，不無有補。況他作稱是，殆學之有用者乎！〕

吏治當察，在稽之於衆而審之於心；民生當安，在體之以情而恤之以實。夫吏司民命，是宜察矣。然不稽之於衆，未免自用不廣；不審之於心，未免偏聽不公，安能盡其情僞乎？民為邦本，是宜安矣。然不體之以情，未免處置失宜；不恤之以實，未免流離失所，安得遂其生全乎？嗚呼！此我皇上所以屢下蠲逋賦、復流移之詔，節有訪賢否、備黜陟之命，而委重於撫按之臣也。夫
translation_en:
Wang Xun

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Discerning men’s abilities and securing the people’s livelihood are the urgent tasks of today. You can investigate, assess, and decide, drawing judiciously on antiquity while adapting it to the present. Surely you cannot be compared with pedantic students of the Classics. What doubt can there be about recommending you highly?”

Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “The policy question omitted historical precedents because it intended respondents to supply them themselves. Most candidates had no time to attend to this, but this candidate alone weighed and discussed them. This reveals both the breadth of his learning and the ample capacity at his disposal. It is indeed on this basis that you are selected [?].”

Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “This particular policy essay [?] answers point by point, thoroughly and in good order. Putting its proposals into practice today would be of some benefit. Moreover, his other compositions measure up to it. Surely his learning has practical value!”

The administration of officials must be scrutinized: this requires consulting the many and carefully judging in one’s own mind. The people’s livelihood must be secured: this requires sympathetic understanding of their circumstances and tangible assistance. Officials hold the people’s lives in their charge, so they certainly ought to be scrutinized. Yet without consulting the many, one inevitably relies on one’s own judgment and lacks breadth; without careful judgment in one’s own mind, one inevitably listens to only one side and lacks impartiality. How, then, can one fully distinguish their sincerity from their deceit? The people are the foundation of the state, so they certainly ought to be given security. Yet without sympathetic understanding of their circumstances, measures will inevitably be ill suited to their needs; without tangible assistance, they will inevitably wander displaced and homeless. How, then, can they sustain their lives and remain unharmed?

Alas! This is why our Emperor has repeatedly issued edicts remitting tax arrears and restoring displaced people to their homes, and has from time to time commanded inquiries into officials’ worthiness or unworthiness in preparation for dismissals and promotions, entrusting these weighty responsibilities to grand coordinators and regional inspectors. Now, …

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
知人則哲能官人安民則惠黎民懷之是
蓋帝王為治之要道而亦臣子輔德之嘉
猷也粵自有虞肇黜陟幽明之典成周立
大明黜陟之法漢制郡守得自課第令長
刺史得課郡國守相而丞相御史得雜考
郡國之計畫天子則受丞相之要是平時
考課之法也其後漢安間遣杜喬周舉輩
分行州郡表賢良顯忠勤其貪汙有罪者
刺史二千石驛馬上之黒綬以下便輒收
===
舉是因時考察之法也而我
朝則兼用之矣今姑以山東吏治言之其得
失不可不察也是故欲求之毀譽則愛憎
競進而善惡混淆欲考之功狀則巧詐横
生而真偽相冒蓋太朴既散之後而綜核
難得名實之真其來遠矣昔我
太祖諭侍臣以人之得毀得譽未必能真但在
真知其賢與不肖折衷於君子之言焉
太宗諭吏部以人之勤職廉濫未必能明亦在
punctuated:
知人則哲，能官人；安民則惠，黎民懷之。是蓋帝王為治之要道，而亦臣子輔德之嘉猷也。粵自有虞肇黜陟幽明之典，成周立大明黜陟之法，漢制郡守得自課第令長，刺史得課郡國守相，而丞相、御史得雜考郡國之計畫，天子則受丞相之要，是平時考課之法也。其後漢安間，遣杜喬、周舉輩分行州郡，表賢良，顯忠勤。其貪汙有罪者，刺史、二千石，驛馬上之；黒綬以下，便輒收舉。是因時考察之法也。而我朝則兼用之矣。
今姑以山東吏治言之，其得失不可不察也。是故欲求之毀譽，則愛憎競進而善惡混淆；欲考之功狀，則巧詐横生而真偽相冒。蓋太朴既散之後，而綜核難得名實之真，其來遠矣。昔我太祖諭侍臣，以人之得毀得譽未必能真，但在真知其賢與不肖，折衷於君子之言焉。太宗諭吏部，以人之勤職廉濫未必能明，亦在
translation_en:
…To know people is to be discerning and thus able to appoint them to office; to bring peace to the people is to be benevolent, so that the common people cherish their ruler. This is the essential way by which emperors and kings govern, and also an excellent principle by which ministers assist their ruler’s virtue. From the time when Yu instituted the practice of demoting the unworthy and promoting the worthy, and the Zhou established rules for clearly administering demotions and promotions, such institutions have existed. Under the Han system, commandery governors could themselves assess and rank county magistrates and chiefs; regional inspectors could assess commandery governors and kingdom chancellors; and the Chancellor and Imperial Counselor could jointly examine the accounts and plans of the commanderies and kingdoms. The Son of Heaven then received the Chancellor’s summary. This was the regular system of performance evaluation. Later, during the Han’an reign period, Du Qiao, Zhou Ju, and others were dispatched on separate circuits through the regions and commanderies to commend the worthy and make known the loyal and diligent. Among officials guilty of corruption, cases involving regional inspectors and officials of two-thousand-bushel rank were reported to the throne by mounted relay; officials wearing black seal ribbons and those below them could be arrested and charged on the spot. This was a system of inspection undertaken as circumstances required. Our dynasty employs both systems.
Now, taking the administration of Shandong as an example, its successes and failures must be scrutinized. If one seeks to ascertain them through criticism and praise, affection and hatred compete to make themselves heard, and good and evil become confused. If one examines records of achievement, cunning and deception proliferate, and truth and falsehood pass for one another. Ever since primordial simplicity was lost, it has been difficult, through comprehensive scrutiny, to establish the truth of reputations and actual performance. This problem is of long standing. Formerly, our Taizu instructed his attendant ministers that the criticism or praise a person received was not necessarily truthful: what mattered was truly knowing whether he was worthy or unworthy, and weighing the matter according to the words of gentlemen. Taizong instructed the Ministry of Personnel that a person’s diligence in office, integrity, or corruption might not necessarily be apparent; this likewise depended on…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
察其衆所好惡而戒飭於御史之考焉
仁宗諭御史以人之謹身集事未必能全惟在
乎博訪公斷而明具於奏聞之疏焉今當
考察之任者能以
祖宗之言為法又如陸贄所謂稽其撫字本末
簾冐聽斷決滯禁禦風化教導諸事本之
以至公之心察之以至明之見詢之於衆
而不任夫已見斷之以心而不惑於浮言
則豈有不得其情而為
===
皇上知人之助乎乃若文王有懷保惠鮮之仁
宣王有勞來安集之政漢宣帝詔池籞未
御幸者假於貧民流民還歸者假公田貸
種食且勿筭事此宣帝恤民之實也宋仁
宗一遇災變必發倉廩賑貸不足則誘致
富人入粟災甚則出內帑金帛或留歲漕
或免租稅寬逋負休力役罷科率此仁宗
愛民之政也而我
朝則無行之矣今姑以山東民瘼言之其疾
punctuated:
察其衆所好惡，而戒飭於御史之考焉。仁宗諭御史，以人之謹身集事未必能全，惟在乎博訪公斷，而明具於奏聞之疏焉。今當考察之任者，能以祖宗之言為法，又如陸贄所謂稽其撫字本末、簾冐、聽斷、決滯、禁禦、風化、教導諸事，本之以至公之心，察之以至明之見，詢之於衆而不任夫已見，斷之以心而不惑於浮言，則豈有不得其情而為皇上知人之助乎？
乃若文王有懷保惠鮮之仁，宣王有勞來安集之政，漢宣帝詔池籞未御幸者假於貧民，流民還歸者假公田、貸種食，且勿筭事，此宣帝恤民之實也。宋仁宗一遇災變，必發倉廩賑貸；不足，則誘致富人入粟；災甚，則出內帑金帛，或留歲漕，或免租稅、寬逋負、休力役、罷科率，此仁宗愛民之政也。而我朝則無行之矣。今姑以山東民瘼言之，其疾
translation_en:
…to examine whom people collectively favor or dislike, and to issue admonitions concerning the censors’ evaluations. Renzong instructed the censors that an official might not be faultless in both personal conduct and the accomplishment of his duties: what mattered was to inquire widely, judge impartially, and set out the findings clearly in memorials to the throne. If those now charged with evaluating officials can take the ancestral emperors’ words as their standard and, as Lu Zhi said, investigate every aspect of officials’ care for the people—their integrity or rapacity [?], their hearing and adjudication of cases, their resolution of delayed business, their prevention and suppression of wrongdoing, their moral influence, and their instruction—and if they ground this work in complete impartiality, examine matters with the utmost discernment, consult the community rather than rely on their own opinions, and judge thoughtfully without being misled by idle talk, how could they fail to ascertain the true circumstances and help His Majesty discern men’s character?
As for King Wen, his benevolence embraced cherishing and protecting the people, showing them kindness, and aiding those in distress. King Xuan’s policies comforted and attracted the people, settling them in peace. Emperor Xuan of the Han ordered that ponds and enclosed preserves not visited by the emperor be lent to the poor, and that displaced people returning home be lent public land, seed, and food, and temporarily exempted from poll taxes and service obligations. These were concrete expressions of Emperor Xuan’s solicitude for the people. Whenever disaster struck, Renzong of the Song invariably opened the granaries to provide relief and loans. If these were insufficient, he encouraged the wealthy to contribute grain. When disaster was severe, he released gold and silk from the palace treasury; he might also retain locally the annual grain tribute, remit taxes, grant relief from arrears, suspend labor services, or abolish levies. These were Renzong’s policies of loving the people. Yet our dynasty has not put these into practice [?]. For the moment, speaking only of the sufferings of the people of Shandong, their afflictions…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
若不可不恤也是故民業棄矣而逋尚存
而追呼不休民田蕪矣額稅猶在而包陪
不已蓋自夾盜相仍之後而長吏多失撫
綏之道其弊久矣昔我
太祖諭省臣以中原兵難之後理宜賑恤雖國
用不足之對不能止焉
太宗諭戶部以南陽縣民逃徙理不宜捕雖賦
稅無所出之言不能動焉
仁宗諭戶部以登萊諸郡逋稅理宜寬貸雖國
===
用不足之言不能奪焉今任存問之寄者
誠能以
祖宗之仁為心而又如漢所遣使者問孤老錄
冤獄蠲逋貸閔疾苦舉幽隱除貪暴發之
以惻隱之心行之以惠愛之政察其情而
不拂其所欲體其心而不施其所惡則豈
有不遂其生而為
皇上安民之助乎雖然郭伋為潁川守招誘盜
賊遣歸附農末幾而戶口增盛杜詩為南
punctuated:
若不可不恤也。是故民業棄矣，而逋尚存，而追呼不休；民田蕪矣，額稅猶在，而包陪不已。蓋自夾盜相仍之後，而長吏多失撫綏之道，其弊久矣。昔我太祖諭省臣，以中原兵難之後，理宜賑恤，雖國用不足之對不能止焉。太宗諭戶部，以南陽縣民逃徙，理不宜捕，雖賦稅無所出之言不能動焉。仁宗諭戶部，以登萊諸郡逋稅，理宜寬貸，雖國用不足之言不能奪焉。
今任存問之寄者，誠能以祖宗之仁為心，而又如漢所遣使者，問孤老，錄冤獄，蠲逋貸，閔疾苦，舉幽隱，除貪暴，發之以惻隱之心，行之以惠愛之政，察其情而不拂其所欲，體其心而不施其所惡，則豈有不遂其生而為皇上安民之助乎？雖然，郭伋為潁川守，招誘盜賊，遣歸附農，末幾而戶口增盛；杜詩為南
translation_en:
…their suffering [?] cannot go unrelieved. Thus, although the people have abandoned their livelihoods, their arrears remain, and demands and summonses for payment never cease; although their fields lie waste, the assessed taxes remain, and the obligation to make up the shortfall [?] continues without end. Since successive outbreaks of banditry [?], many local administrators have failed to nurture and pacify the people. These abuses have persisted for a long time. Formerly, our Taizu instructed the ministers of the Secretariat that, after the warfare in the Central Plain, relief ought properly to be provided. Even their reply that state funds were insufficient could not stop him. Taizong instructed the Ministry of Revenue that the people who had fled Nanyang County ought not to be arrested. Even the argument that there would be no source of tax revenue could not move him. Renzong instructed the Ministry of Revenue that leniency ought to be granted regarding tax arrears in the prefectures of Dengzhou, Laizhou, and elsewhere. Even the argument that state funds were insufficient could not deflect him.
If those now entrusted with visiting and inquiring into the people's welfare could truly take the benevolence of our imperial ancestors to heart and, like the envoys dispatched under the Han, inquire after the orphaned and elderly, review cases of wrongful imprisonment, remit arrears and loans, show compassion for suffering, recommend worthy men living in obscurity, and remove greedy and brutal officials—initiating these measures from a compassionate heart and implementing them through benevolent government, examining the people's circumstances without frustrating their wishes, and understanding their hearts without imposing what they detest—how could they fail to enable the people to sustain their lives and help His Majesty bring them peace? Nevertheless, when Guo Ji was Grand Administrator of Yingchuan, he persuaded bandits to submit and sent them home to take up farming; before long [?], households and population increased and flourished. Du Shi served as Grand Administrator of Nan…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
陽守脩治陂池廣拓田土未幾而比屋贍
足若夫橫征毒於蛇苛政猛於虎則是盜
民之賊而驅民之流也吏治之關於民生
其切如此然則欲民生之安者豈不可不
嚴於吏治之察也乎
punctuated: 陽守，脩治陂池，廣拓田土，未幾而比屋贍足。若夫橫征毒於蛇，苛政猛於虎，則是盜民之賊，而驅民之流也。吏治之關於民生，其切如此。然則欲民生之安者，豈不可不嚴於吏治之察也乎？
translation_en: …as governor of Nanyang, repaired ponds and reservoirs and greatly expanded cultivated land; before long, household after household enjoyed ample provision. But when arbitrary exactions are more venomous than snakes and oppressive government fiercer than tigers, this amounts to robbing the people and driving them into displacement. So directly does the administration of officials affect the people’s livelihood. Then, if one wishes the people to live in security, how could one fail to scrutinize officials’ administration rigorously? [The final rhetorical question contains an apparent extra negative in the transcription: 豈不可不.]

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄後序
鄉試錄者鄉舉士名氏若
文及有事試事者也山東鄉
試錄成〔潔〕辱言於後夫山東
古齊魯鄒滕之國山川甲他
省然所產無甚殊異以發其
藏也而人之生也宜獨異焉
===
故古昔聖賢繼出漢唐以下
多名臣大儒今山川猶昔也
豈可謂無昔之人乎夫賢才
者惟上所養苟養非其道取
非其養則士習不正士習不
正則聖賢之道不明其何才
之獲故唐王師旦謂張昌齡
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄後序

鄉試錄者，鄉舉士名氏若文及有事試事者也。山東鄉試錄成，〔潔〕辱言於後。夫山東，古齊魯鄒滕之國，山川甲他省，然所產無甚殊異以發其藏也，而人之生也宜獨異焉。

故古昔聖賢繼出，漢唐以下，多名臣大儒。今山川猶昔也，豈可謂無昔之人乎？夫賢才者，惟上所養。苟養非其道，取非其養，則士習不正；士習不正，則聖賢之道不明，其何才之獲？故唐王師旦謂張昌齡
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

A Provincial Examination Record contains the names and writings of the men recommended by the province, together with those who took part in conducting the examination. The Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination having been completed, I, 〔Jie 潔〕, have been honored with the invitation to add some words at its end. Shandong comprises the lands of the ancient states of Qi, Lu, Zou, and Teng. Its mountains and rivers surpass those of other provinces, yet its products are not especially extraordinary manifestations of its hidden riches. It is therefore in the people born there that its exceptional qualities should find their particular expression.

Thus, in antiquity, sages and worthies emerged one after another, and from the Han and Tang onward there have been many renowned ministers and great Confucian scholars. Its mountains and rivers remain as they were: how could one say that it no longer has people like those of old? Worthy and talented men depend upon cultivation by those above. If they are cultivated contrary to the proper Way, and selection does not accord with their cultivation, the habits of scholars will become improper. If their habits are improper, the Way of the sages and worthies will not be made clear. What talent, then, could be obtained? Thus Wang Shidan of the Tang said of Zhang Changling…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
華文藻浮艶非令器黜之宋
歐陽修惡時文險恠即有譽
如劉幾亦在所擯故知詞科
之弊久矣然識者少救其偏
而貞觀嘉祐之治已不可及
嗚乎可不愼與我
朝貢舉之制以六經正學爲本
===
詩賦諸科皆置不用然其得
人致治之盛有由來矣顧治
久文盛士習漸澆襲取者非
深造記誦者非自得其爲文
也違易趨險剖竒鬬靡渾厚
光大之氣索矣是故取之不
如其用名之不如其實而
punctuated:
華文藻浮艶，非令器，黜之。宋歐陽修惡時文險恠，即有譽如劉幾，亦在所擯。故知詞科之弊久矣，然識者少救其偏，而貞觀、嘉祐之治已不可及。嗚乎！可不愼與？
我朝貢舉之制，以六經正學爲本，詩賦諸科皆置不用。然其得人致治之盛，有由來矣。顧治久文盛，士習漸澆，襲取者非深造，記誦者非自得。其爲文也，違易趨險，剖竒鬬靡，渾厚光大之氣索矣。是故取之不如其用，名之不如其實，而
translation_en:
…the ornate literary embellishment was frivolously lavish [?]; he was no worthy talent, and was rejected. In the Song, Ouyang Xiu disliked the strained and bizarre style of contemporary examination writing; even someone as renowned as Liu Ji was among those he rejected. Thus we know that the abuses of literary examinations are longstanding. Yet few discerning men have remedied their distortions, and already the good government of the Zhenguan and Jiayou reign periods lies beyond our reach. Alas! Can we fail to exercise caution?
Our dynasty’s system of recruitment through examinations takes orthodox learning in the Six Classics as its foundation; examination categories devoted to poetry and rhapsodies have all been set aside. Its outstanding success in obtaining worthy men and bringing about good government therefore has a foundation. Yet, after a long period of orderly government and literary flourishing, scholars’ habits have gradually grown shallow. Those who borrow from others do not pursue profound learning; those who memorize and recite do not attain understanding for themselves. In their writing, they forsake simplicity and pursue difficulty, elaborate curiosities and vie in ornate extravagance. The generous, substantial, luminous, and expansive spirit has been exhausted. Thus success in selection does not correspond to usefulness in service, nor reputation to actual merit, and…

title: 正德十一年山東鄉試錄
text:
國家養士之意則甚悖也潔等
惟是之懼故取諸文也本之
以學察之以識輔之以氣潤
之以才學正則義醇識遠則
智辨氣昌則體弘才峻則詞
嚴醇者所以善其用也辨者
所以御其幾也弘者所以重
其任也嚴者所以光其業也
===
必如是然後取之否則棄之
登斯錄者尚不愧昔人矣乎
雖然取之者今日之事也效
之者士之所自盡也惟士之
文也不爽於行信哉山川之
所鍾不異於昔也已
punctuated:
國家養士之意則甚悖也。潔等惟是之懼，故取諸文也，本之以學，察之以識，輔之以氣，潤之以才。學正則義醇，識遠則智辨，氣昌則體弘，才峻則詞嚴。醇者所以善其用也，辨者所以御其幾也，弘者所以重其任也，嚴者所以光其業也。必如是然後取之，否則棄之。登斯錄者，尚不愧昔人矣乎？
雖然，取之者今日之事也，效之者士之所自盡也。惟士之文也不爽於行，信哉，山川之所鍾不異於昔也已！
translation_en:
…the state's intention in nurturing scholars is thus gravely contravened. We, Jie and his colleagues, fear precisely this. Therefore, in selecting essays, we take learning as their foundation, examine their discernment, look for the support of vital force and the enrichment of talent. When learning is correct, meaning is pure; when discernment is far-reaching, understanding is discriminating; when vital force flourishes, composition is ample; when talent is lofty, expression is rigorous. Purity enables scholars to serve well; discrimination enables them to respond to the first stirrings of events; amplitude enables them to bear weighty responsibilities; rigor enables them to bring distinction to their undertakings. Only essays meeting these standards are selected; otherwise, they are rejected. May those entered in this record prove worthy of their predecessors!
Yet selection is the business of today; demonstrating its results requires the scholars themselves to exert their utmost. If only their conduct accords with their writing, then truly the gifts bestowed by these mountains and rivers will be no different from those of old!
